2396 // Data.
2397
2398 /**
2399 * The builder engine config for out-messages: Small data store, such that the Struct_builder
2400 * `Builder_config::Builder` (really the containing class of #Builder_config) main-ctor
2401 * takes an object of this type, its contents being knobs controlling the behavior of the resulting Struct_builder.
2402 * - The *type* #Builder_config (a template parameter) determines the logic part of the serialization policy:
2403 * what is the source of RAM for segments (heap? SHM?), as the user mutates an out-message? How big is each
2404 * segment?
2405 * - The *members* inside #m_struct_builder_config further tweak the application of that logic by being
2406 * knobs: Should prefix/postfix space be left in the serialization? How quickly should the segments grow?
2407 * Where to log?
2408 * - This `Config` is passed to `Builder` ctor to configure it.
2409 *
2410 * ### Rationale ###
2411 * By storing this value, copied from the one passed to ctor, we delegate the policy decision (as to what kind
2412 * of capnp-structured-to-binary serialization engine to use) to the `*this` config (user). The knobs
2413 * controlling the configuration of that engine, each time it's created for a given out-message, depend
2414 * on the builder concrete type, so we don't know what they are or even their nature or number.
2415 * They are stored opaquely (to us) inside this item.
2416 *
2417 * Every user out-message created via create_msg() is supplied by the latter with #m_struct_builder_config
2418 * as the builder config.
2419 * - So the schema template param is `<Msg_body_t>`, the `Channel` template param from the user.
2420 * - The user is allowed to simply direct-construct the #Msg_out without any create_msg(). They have to
2421 * supply the builder config themselves again, though. It has to be the same type as
2422 * #m_struct_builder_config, or it won't compile; but in theory it could have different knob values.
2423 * E.g., it could have a null `Logger`, while `*this` one logs-galore.
2424 *
2425 * So it's an important member, but arguably its type is more important than its contents (knobs).
2426 */
2427 const Builder_config m_struct_builder_config;
2428
2429 /**
2430 * Value (possibly of size 0 depending on this type) to pass to Msg_out_impl::emit_serialization()
2431 * to indicate the opposing side of the #Owned_channel. If the type is Null_session (empty type), then
2432 * no information is necessary to indicate this.
2433 */
2434 const typename Builder_config::Builder::Session m_struct_lender_session;
2435
2436 /// Analogous to #m_struct_builder_config but for deserialization.
2437 const Reader_config m_struct_reader_config;
2438
2439 /**
2440 * Handles the protocol negotiation at the start of the pipe, as pertains to algorithms perpetuated by
2441 * `*this` class's code.
2442 *
2443 * @see Protocol_negotiator doc header for key background on the topic.
2444 */
2445 Protocol_negotiator m_protocol_negotiator;
2446
2447 /**
2448 * Handles the protocol negotiation at the start of the pipe, as pertains to algorithms perpetuated outside
2449 * of `*this` class's code but instead in #Builder_config #m_struct_builder_config and
2450 * #Reader_config #m_struct_reader_config and related.
2451 *
2452 * @see Protocol_negotiator doc header for key background on the topic.
2453 */
2454 Protocol_negotiator m_protocol_negotiator_aux;
2455
2456 /**
2457 * Error, or lack thereof, recorded by start_ops() (having returned `true`) when synchronously sending out
2458 * protocol-negotiation and channel-header message(s). More specifically send_init_msgs() sets it.
2459 * If truthy, subsequent start_and_poll(), send(), async_request(), or contextually similar (whichever happens
2460 * first) will promote it to #m_channel_err_code_or_ok and emit it in the normal fashion.
2461 */
2462 Error_code m_init_msg_err_code_or_ok;
2463
2464 /**
2465 * Whether start_ops() has been called yet or not. We could've used #m_channel built-in guards against that,
2466 * but then as of this writing there's no way to check that at the top of our own various APIs
2467 * (check_not_started_ops()).
2468 */
2469 bool m_started_ops;
2470
2471 /**
2472 * The channel-hosed error reporting handler. See start_and_poll() + class doc header for discussion of
2473 * error semantics.
2474 */
2475 flow::async::Task_asio_err m_on_err_func;
2476
2477 /**
2478 * 1 or 2 active `struct`s containing policy (via their types, passed around as template args to methods) and
2479 * state (as data members) w/r/t receipt of low-level (unstructured) messages with the aim to complete the
2480 * next structured in-message(s). Either only `.front()` or both elements are non-null.
2481 *
2482 * @see Msg_in_pipe doc header for detailed algorithm overview.
2483 *
2484 * ### Rationale: General ###
2485 * This is mostly explained in the aforementioned doc header, but as far as a couple technicalities:
2486 *
2487 * This thing is nothing more than a way for each Msg_in_pipe to keep existing starting with start_and_poll().
2488 * Nothing even accesses `m_rcv_pipes` by name after it is loaded; the pointer to each of the 1-2 relevant
2489 * pipe objects is passed continuously through each pipe's chain of methods/async-ops, as method args or
2490 * lambda captures (the latter when an async-op is involved; in fact specifically an async-receive op on
2491 * #m_channel). In fact the actual type of each non-null element is erased; note it is `shared_ptr<void>`; so
2492 * that information is passed around *only* as template parameters to the various methods.
2493 *
2494 * It would have been pretty easy to even get rid of #m_rcv_pipes entirely: just make a
2495 * `shared_ptr<Msg_in_pipe<...>>` and pass that thing around instead of a raw `Msg_in_pipe*`. It would get freed
2496 * on error or `*this` destruction via `shared_ptr` ref-counting. The reason we do it the current way is (1) it is
2497 * a bit faster (no ref-counting to track when a raw pointer is passed-around), and (2) it's no less
2498 * straightforward stylistically.
2499 *
2500 * ### Rationale: Why `shared_ptr<void>`? ###
2501 * ...as opposed to `unique_ptr` or `optional` or something? Well, (1) it doesn't matter
2502 * perf-wise or style-wise much (it only "matters" in start_and_poll(), once, and then ~at destruction), and (2)
2503 * `unique_ptr` cannot do type erasure in a natural way; while `optional` cannot at all. Though actually
2504 * see the following to-do regarding `any`.
2505 *
2506 * @todo Changing Channel::m_rcv_pipes to store `any` instead of `shared_ptr<void>` might be *slightly* prettier.
2507 * As noted ahead of this to-do, though, the only places that would actually change at all would be
2508 * at init (start_and_poll()) and ~at destruction. Perf-wise that means it doesn't matter. Style-wise it would
2509 * only matter in start_and_poll() in ~3 lines and here at the declaration site. Arguably `any` (all else being
2510 * equal, which it is here) is simply a more expressive way to represent a type-erased value. It's just slow
2511 * (in certain contexts -- but not ours).
2512 *
2513 * But I (ygoldfel) digress. It's fine!
2514 *
2515 * ### Rationale: Why `array`? ###
2516 * ...Whatever. `vector<>` would have been fine too... or two members. `array<2>` just seemed a nice way
2517 * to express there can be only up to 2 pipes; that's all.
2518 */
2519 boost::array<boost::shared_ptr<void>, 2> m_rcv_pipes;
2520
2521 /// See set_unexpected_response_handler().
2522 On_unexpected_response_func m_on_unexpected_response_func_or_empty;
2523
2524 /// See set_remote_unexpected_response_handler().
2525 On_remote_unexpected_response_func m_on_remote_unexpected_response_func_or_empty;
2526
2527 /**
2528 * The opposing peer's self-reported credentials (such as process ID); unknown/null until
2529 * the read chain started in start_and_poll() passes protocol negotiation and immediately following that
2530 * receives the `ChannelHeader` containing that info; unchanged after that point.
2531 *
2532 * As of this writing it is used in accessor remote_peer_process_credentials().
2533 */
2534 std::optional<util::Process_credentials> m_peer_process_creds;
2535
2536 /**
2537 * Session token: in Phase::S_LOGGED_IN to send in every out-message and check-against every in-message;
2538 * in log-in phase *as client* equals nil; in log-in phase *as server* it is auto-generated at construction.
2539 * In non-log-in phase, it's either provided by user in ctor (if log-in phase skipped), or:
2540 * - inherited from log-in phase (if *as server*);
2541 * - deserialized from the log-in response (if *as client*).
2542 *
2543 * It's used in 2 ways:
2544 * - It is sent in every (structured) message -- namely in the lead unstructured message.
2545 * So whenever an `mdt` message is created, we load #m_session_token into it at that time.
2546 * - Every message is checked against it (if not correct, channel is hosed immediately).
2547 * - There is exactly one exception to this: The log-in request (received in log-in phase *as server*)
2548 * must have nil session token: we have not yet sent #m_session_token (which we generated at ction)
2549 * to it in the response message, so the client could not have known it.
2550 */
2551 Session_token m_session_token;
2552
2553 /// Next out-message ID (for the next send() or async_request()).
2554 msg_id_out_t m_snd_msg_next_id;
2555
2556 /**
2557 * Phase (w/r/t log-in or lack thereof) of `*this` peer. It is either Phase::S_LOGGED_IN throughout; or
2558 * starts as one of the other 2 values, then is assigned LOGGED_IN and unmodified further.
2559 *
2560 * If not LOGGED_IN from the start (see ctors) then it is written exactly once:
2561 * - Phase::S_SRV_LOG_IN => Phase::S_LOGGED_IN (see ctors): When send() of the log-in response is invoked.
2562 * - Phase::S_CLI_LOG_IN => Phase::S_LOGGED_IN (see ctors): When response to the async_request() of the
2563 * log-in request is received.
2564 *
2565 * It is generally checked at the start of all or most APIs (check_phase_and_prior_error()).
2566 * In particular many APIs, such as expect_msg(), no-op and return sentinel unless LOGGED_IN; ~one
2567 * (expect_log_in_request()) does the same unless in a proper `*_LOG_IN` phase.
2568 * If the user is acting sanely, they would invoke the log-in APIs before
2569 * entry to LOGGED_IN and vice versa for the logged-in APIs; namely:
2570 * - SRV_LOG_IN -> LOGGED_IN: After send() of the log-in response which itself would be only
2571 * after the handler passed to expect_log_in_request() fires.
2572 * - CLI_LOG_IN -> LOGGED_IN: After the handler, passed to async_request() along with log-in request out-message,
2573 * fires indicating receiving the expected log-in response.
2574 *
2575 * If the user disregards these best practices and invokes a logged-in API before those points, then they're
2576 * engaging in a race. Worst-case, they'll get an unexpected sentinel return of something like expect_msg() --
2577 * their own fault.
2578 */
2579 Phase m_phase;
2580
2581 /**
2582 * Used when #m_phase is Phase::S_SRV_LOG_IN, this starts `false` and is changed
2583 * to `true` at thread-U call of expect_log_in_request(); if already `true` then a 2nd (illegal)
2584 * expect_log_in_request() call has been made and shall be ignored (no-op, return sentinel).
2585 */
2586 bool m_phase_log_in_started;
2587
2588 /**
2589 * Starts falsy; becomes forever truthy (with a specific #Error_code that will not change thereafter)
2590 * when one of the following detects the first channel-hosing condition: send() or async_request(), on-receive
2591 * handlers `rcv_on_*()` (either via underlying-`Owned_channel` detecting lower-layer error; or our layer
2592 * detecting protocol error et al). Once that becomes the case:
2593 * - Any *subsequent* on-receive handler (possibly none but at most one per ongoing async-read chain, of which
2594 * there are 1-2) will immediately no-op and end async chain.
2595 * - Any *subsequent* send() or async_request() will immediately no-op and return `false`.
2596 * - Any subsequent other mutable-state-touching API -- e.g., session_token(), expect_msg() -- will immediately
2597 * no-op and return `false`/null/sentinel value. Exception: async_end_sending() (see below).
2598 * create_msg() is a convenience thing that does not touch mutable state, so it won't care either.
2599 * - All registered expectations (#m_rcv_expecting_msg_map, #m_rcv_expecting_response_map) and the
2600 * unexpected-response handlers are discarded (not absolutely required but very good hygiene).
2601 *
2602 * Use hose() to make it truthy.
2603 *
2604 * @note async_end_sending() is orthogonal to this. It is a `transport::Channel`-level call that (per its doc
2605 * header) simply forwards to Channel::async_end_sending(), no questions asked. The `F()` passed to
2606 * async_end_sending() may well trigger synchronous emission of `E`, with `E == m_channel_err_code_or_ok`;
2607 * or not; but nothing should or does count on this.
2608 *
2609 * @see Msg_in_pipe::m_gracefully_closed doc header; it explains how and why, in a 2-pipe situation, a lower-layer
2610 * graceful-close "error" along in-pipe 1 may not necessarily hose() (make `m_channel_err_code_or_ok` truthy);
2611 * namely if in-pipe 2 is at that time healthy. Only relevant if Channel::S_HAS_2_PIPES.
2612 */
2613 Error_code m_channel_err_code_or_ok;
2614
2615 /// Map storing current policy for expecting responses. See #Expecting_response_map doc header for details.
2616 Expecting_response_map m_rcv_expecting_response_map;
2617
2618 /**
2619 * Map storing current policy for expecting non-response messages. See #Expecting_msg_map and Expecting_msg
2620 * doc headers for details.
2621 */
2622 Expecting_msg_map m_rcv_expecting_msg_map;
2623
2624 /**
2625 * Next expected in-message ID (sequence #), incremented from initial value 1 to 2, 3, ... on in-order message
2626 * receipt. It is used purely for sanity checking of the opposing sender's payloads, when #Owned_channel stores
2627 * only 1 pipe (Channel::S_HAS_2_PIPES is `false`). Or: it is used with
2628 * #m_rcv_reassembly_q if #Owned_channel stores 2 pipes (Channel::S_HAS_2_PIPES is `true`).
2629 *
2630 * ### Algorithm summary: 2 in-pipes ###
2631 * In that latter case a handle-less in-message may arrive along the blobs in-pipe;
2632 * while a handle-paired message may arrive along the handles in-pipe; and since the two might race, the one
2633 * sent 1st might arrive 2nd, and vice versa. Then the out-of-order one would be stored temporarily in
2634 * #m_rcv_reassembly_q. (In theory this could occur for several in-messages.) This is detected by noting that
2635 * an in-message's message ID (sequence number) exceeds #m_rcv_msg_next_id. If it equals it, then it is in-order
2636 * and skips #m_rcv_reassembly_q. If it is lower, then that is misbehavior by the opposing peer and hoses
2637 * the pipe.
2638 *
2639 * Technically we could be more stringent in our sanity checking: while races may occur between the 2 in-pipes,
2640 * for a *given* 1 of 2 pipes (the blobs pipe; the handles pipe), the message IDs must always be increasing,
2641 * as these are reliable, in-order pipes. However we choose to not worry about this enforcement; in-order
2642 * behavior of our various transports shall (possibly) be checked elsewhere and is a hard assumption. On
2643 * the other hand it is cheap to check for non-repeating (always increasing) message IDs along the totality of
2644 * the pipes, so we do.
2645 *
2646 * ### Algorithm summary: 1 in-pipe ###
2647 * Each message received must contain ID, in fact, equal #m_rcv_msg_next_id which is then incremented. There is no
2648 * reassembly, as there is only 1 in-pipe, and it must be in-order. This is (as noted just above) easy to
2649 * sanity-check.
2650 */
2651 msg_id_in_t m_rcv_msg_next_id;
2652
2653 /**
2654 * When `Owned_channel::S_HAS_2_PIPES`, stores the reassembly queue of in-messages to feed into
2655 * #m_rcv_pending_msgs once the #msg_id_in_t (sequence #) gap between
2656 * #m_rcv_msg_next_id and `m_rcv_reassembly_q.front()` is filled by in-messages. Once that occurs, the maximally long
2657 * sequence of in-messages at the front of this queue are moved into #m_rcv_pending_msgs (or fed to waiting
2658 * handlers immediately if possible). Left uninitialized if `!S_HAS_2_PIPES`.
2659 *
2660 * @see #m_rcv_msg_next_id for algorithm summary; #Reassembly_q doc header for data structure details.
2661 */
2662 std::optional<Reassembly_q> m_rcv_reassembly_q;
2663
2664 /**
2665 * Queues of in-messages, keyed by #Msg_which_in, each in #msg_id_in_t (sequence #) order, for which no
2666 * #Msg_which_in handler has yet been registered by the user (expect_msg(), expect_msgs(), expect_log_in_request()).
2667 * They'll stay there until such a thing is indeed registered; once it is, that queue's elements are fed, in order,
2668 * to that handler, and the element is removed from #m_rcv_pending_msgs.
2669 *
2670 * ### Corner case: a response arrives to an originating out-message for which no response is expected ###
2671 * It is relatively normal, if ideally avoided (informally speaking), that there is no #Msg_which_in
2672 * listener yet registered for a given in-message. (One can be registered later: then such messages will be
2673 * flushed to that handler.) By contrast: It is a *user protocol* error that a response
2674 * arrives unexpectedly. Let's break down the realistic possibilities for how that might happen:
2675 * - A response arrives to message M, but the local user never issued a request for that message as
2676 * triggered by async_request(). The opposing user must have erroneously issued a response to
2677 * a non-request.
2678 * - A response arrives to message M, and the local user *did* issue an async_request() for that message;
2679 * but either it was a one-off request -- and this is the 2nd/3rd/...
2680 * response -- or it was an open-ended request, but the local user called undo_expect_responses() for it since.
2681 * Typically this is a miscommunication at the user level: e.g., opposing user indicated a previous
2682 * response was the last one but then erroneously sent another response anyway. Or, more simply,
2683 * it sent 2+ responses to a one-off request (again erroneously).
2684 *
2685 * Both situations involve non-trivial user-level protocol mistakes. What to do?
2686 * - We could hose the whole channel (fatal #Error_code emitted to user).
2687 * This feels too draconian and inflexible at such a high layer.
2688 * - Or we could inform the user of the problem.
2689 *
2690 * We choose the latter. In particular:
2691 * - We fire the user-protocol-error handler (see start_and_poll()) locally. We feed them the problem
2692 * in-message and then forget that message: they can do with it as they wish.
2693 * - We send an internal message to the opposing peer indicating the issue including the triggering
2694 * in-message ID (to them, out-message ID). The opposing peer `Channel` shall fire their own
2695 * user-protocol-error handler similarly.
2696 *
2697 * Other than that the channel continues operating. The user can choose to close it, or ignore the problem,
2698 * or alert, or whatever.
2699 *
2700 * To wit:
2701 * @see set_unexpected_response_handler().
2702 * @see set_remote_unexpected_response_handler().
2703 */
2704 boost::unordered_flat_map<Msg_which_in, Msg_in_q> m_rcv_pending_msgs;
2705
2706 // (End of m_rcv_* section.)
2707
2708 /**
2709 * The Channel taken-over in ctor, lifetime until dtor.
2710 *
2711 * @see also #m_channel_err_code_or_ok.
2712 */
2713 Owned_channel m_channel;
2714
2715 /// Cumulative structured-channel stats, updated incrementally on send/receive/expect operations.
2716 stat::Channel_stats m_stats;
2717
2718}; // class Channel
2719

2732TEMPLATE_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL
2733CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::Channel(flow::log::Logger* logger_ptr, Owned_channel_t&& channel,
2734 const Builder_config& struct_builder_config,
2735 const typename Builder_config::Builder::Session& struct_lender_session,
2736 const Reader_config& struct_reader_config,
2737 const Session_token& session_token_non_nil) :
2738 flow::log::Log_context(logger_ptr, Log_component::S_TRANSPORT),
2739 m_struct_builder_config(struct_builder_config),
2740 m_struct_lender_session(struct_lender_session),
2741 m_struct_reader_config(struct_reader_config),
2742
2743 /* This all will get quite a bit more complex, especially for m_protocol_negotiator_aux,
2744 * once at least one relevant protocol decides to both gain a version and still support an older version.
2745 * For now though there's just one version for both thingies, and only that version is supported (MIN == MAX).
2746 * See class doc header for discussion. Note for now the related static_assert() below. */
2747 m_protocol_negotiator(get_logger(), std::string{"struc-"} + channel.nickname(),
2748 S_PROTOCOL_VERSION_MIN, S_PROTOCOL_VERSION_MAX),
2749 m_protocol_negotiator_aux(get_logger(), std::string{"struc-aux-"} + channel.nickname(),
2750 S_PROTOCOL_VERSION_MIN, S_PROTOCOL_VERSION_MAX),
2751
2752 m_started_ops(false),
2753
2754 // Skip log-in phase. Ready to rock immediately.
2755 m_session_token(session_token_non_nil),
2756 m_snd_msg_next_id(1),
2757
2758 m_phase(Phase::S_LOGGED_IN),
2759
2760 m_rcv_msg_next_id(1),
2761
2762 m_channel(std::move(channel))
2763{
2764 static_assert(S_PROTOCOL_VERSION_MIN == S_PROTOCOL_VERSION_MAX,
2765 "Various code assumes we don't do backward-compatible protocols; if this fails please "
2766 "ensure the code all-over is thoughtfully handling this topic and delete this static-assert.");
2767
2768 // (Deets on m_channel are in printing *this.)
2769 FLOW_LOG_INFO("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Created, owning the aforementioned (SIO) Channel. "
2770 "Log-in phase bypassed; session token = [" << m_session_token << "]. "
2771 "(User must invoke start_ops() and (if needed) replace_event_wait_handles(). Assume it occurs soon.) "
2772 "Async-read chain will not start until start_and_poll(). Sends possible now.");
2773
2774 if constexpr(Owned_channel::S_HAS_2_PIPES)
2775 {
2776 m_rcv_reassembly_q.emplace();
2777 }
2778 // else { Leave the optional<> uninitialized forever. }
2779
2780 assert((!session_token_non_nil.is_nil())
2781 && "Pre-logged-in channel must be supplied a non-nil session token, presumably "
2782 "from session master channel.");
2783} // Channel::Channel()

2785TEMPLATE_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL
2786CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::Channel(flow::log::Logger* logger_ptr, Owned_channel_t&& channel,
2787 const Builder_config& struct_builder_config,
2788 const typename Builder_config::Builder::Session& struct_lender_session,
2789 const Reader_config& struct_reader_config,
2790 bool is_server) :
2791 flow::log::Log_context(logger_ptr, Log_component::S_TRANSPORT),
2792 m_struct_builder_config(struct_builder_config),
2793 m_struct_lender_session(struct_lender_session),
2794 m_struct_reader_config(struct_reader_config),
2795
2796 // See comment in earlier Channel::Channel(). @todo More code reuse?
2797 m_protocol_negotiator(get_logger(), std::string{"struc-"} + channel.nickname(),
2798 S_PROTOCOL_VERSION_MIN, S_PROTOCOL_VERSION_MAX),
2799 m_protocol_negotiator_aux(get_logger(), std::string{"struc-aux-"} + channel.nickname(),
2800 S_PROTOCOL_VERSION_MIN, S_PROTOCOL_VERSION_MAX),
2801
2802 m_started_ops(false),
2803
2804 // Start in log-in phase. They can use only the small (log-in-related) part of the public API for now.
2805 m_session_token(is_server
2806 /* @todo In practice this is done rarely per process, probably, but docs do suggest to
2807 * save the uuids::random_generator "if you can" due to possible non-trivial startup cost.
2808 * We'd have to deal with thread safety + static then though. Again in reality log-in
2809 * probably occurs in only one channel per process and quite rarely. */
2810 ? boost::uuids::random_generator()() // Server *creates* the UUID (later sends it to client).
2811 : NULL_SESSION_TOKEN), // Client lacks UUID until server sends it in log-in response.
2812 m_snd_msg_next_id(1),
2813 m_phase(is_server ? Phase::S_SRV_LOG_IN : Phase::S_CLI_LOG_IN),
2814 m_phase_log_in_started(false),
2815
2816 m_rcv_msg_next_id(1),
2817
2818 m_channel(std::move(channel))
2819{
2820 // (Deets on m_channel are in printing *this.)
2821 FLOW_LOG_INFO("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Created, owning the aforementioned (SIO) Channel. "
2822 "Log-in phase [" << (is_server ? "server" : "client") << "] in effect; session token is nil "
2823 "until log-in phase completes. "
2824 "(User must invoke start_ops() and (if needed) replace_event_wait_handles(). Assume it occurs soon.) "
2825 "Async-read chain will not start until start_and_poll(). Sends possible now.");
2826
2827 if constexpr(Owned_channel::S_HAS_2_PIPES)
2828 {
2829 m_rcv_reassembly_q.emplace();
2830 }
2831 // else { Leave the optional<> uninitialized forever. }
2832} // Channel::Channel()

2942TEMPLATE_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL
2943template<typename Event_wait_func_t>
2944bool CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::start_ops(Event_wait_func_t&& ev_wait_func)
2945{
2946 using util::sync_io::Asio_waitable_native_handle;
2947 using util::sync_io::Task_ptr;
2948
2949 if (m_started_ops)
2950 {
2951 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Start-ops requested, but they were already started. "
2952 "Ignoring.");
2953 return false;
2954 }
2955 // else
2956 m_started_ops = true;
2957
2958 FLOW_LOG_INFO("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Start-ops requested. Accordingly we forward start-ops "
2959 "requests to owned channel [" << m_channel << "] peers.");
2960 /* @todo Maybe Channel should offer a start_ops() that'll do what we do? At the moment one must do it individually
2961 * peer-by-peer; and that must exist, so that one can lock a different mutex per pipe or whatever -- or formally
2962 * for it to continue implementing the 4 sync_io::_sender/receiver concepts. However for a case like ours, where
2963 * all the op-types are handled by the same code, it would be nice to add a start_ops(). Then what we do here
2964 * would be available for other Channel users. */
2965
2966#ifndef NDEBUG
2967 bool ok;
2968#endif
2969 constexpr auto HAS_BLOB = Owned_channel::S_HAS_BLOB_PIPE;
2970 constexpr auto HAS_HNDL = Owned_channel::S_HAS_NATIVE_HANDLE_PIPE;
2971 if constexpr(HAS_BLOB)
2972 {
2973#ifndef NDEBUG
2974 ok =
2975#endif
2976 m_channel.start_send_blob_ops([this,
2977 ev_wait_func] // Capture a copy (no choice; we need to reuse it below).
2978 (Asio_waitable_native_handle* hndl_of_interest,
2979 bool ev_of_interest_snd_else_rcv,
2980 Task_ptr&& on_active_ev_func) mutable
2981 {
2982 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: SIO blob-pipe send-op module: event-wait requested.");
2983 ev_wait_func(hndl_of_interest, ev_of_interest_snd_else_rcv, std::move(on_active_ev_func));
2984 });
2985 assert(ok && "m_started_ops should have guarded against this failing.");
2986 /* This added compile-time branching is to optimize away the copying of ev_wait_func if not needed again below.
2987 * This is not a perf-critical path, probably, but this code isn't that long. Might as well.
2988 * I (ygoldfel) don't think the capture can be conditionally specified to use the move-ctor
2989 * using some compile-time ternary thing. So wordy `if constexpr()` it is. */
2990 if constexpr(HAS_HNDL)
2991 {
2992#ifndef NDEBUG
2993 ok =
2994#endif
2995 m_channel.start_receive_blob_ops([this,
2996 ev_wait_func] // Copy again.
2997 (Asio_waitable_native_handle* hndl_of_interest,
2998 bool ev_of_interest_snd_else_rcv, Task_ptr&& on_active_ev_func) mutable
2999 {
3000 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: SIO blob-pipe receive-op module: event-wait requested.");
3001 ev_wait_func(hndl_of_interest, ev_of_interest_snd_else_rcv, std::move(on_active_ev_func));
3002 });
3003 assert(ok && "m_started_ops should have guarded against this failing.");
3004 }
3005 else
3006 {
3007#ifndef NDEBUG
3008 ok =
3009#endif
3010 m_channel.start_receive_blob_ops([this,
3011 ev_wait_func = std::move(ev_wait_func)] // Do not copy.
3012 (Asio_waitable_native_handle* hndl_of_interest,
3013 bool ev_of_interest_snd_else_rcv, Task_ptr&& on_active_ev_func) mutable
3014 {
3015 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: SIO blob-pipe receive-op module: event-wait requested.");
3016 ev_wait_func(hndl_of_interest, ev_of_interest_snd_else_rcv, std::move(on_active_ev_func));
3017 });
3018 assert(ok && "m_started_ops should have guarded against this failing.");
3019 }
3020 } // if constexpr(HAS_BLOB)
3021 if constexpr(HAS_HNDL)
3022 {
3023#ifndef NDEBUG
3024 ok =
3025#endif
3026 m_channel.start_send_native_handle_ops([this,
3027 ev_wait_func] // See above.
3028 (Asio_waitable_native_handle* hndl_of_interest,
3029 bool ev_of_interest_snd_else_rcv,
3030 Task_ptr&& on_active_ev_func) mutable
3031 {
3032 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: SIO handle-pipe send-op module: event-wait requested.");
3033 ev_wait_func(hndl_of_interest, ev_of_interest_snd_else_rcv, std::move(on_active_ev_func));
3034 });
3035 assert(ok && "m_started_ops should have guarded against this failing.");
3036#ifndef NDEBUG
3037 ok =
3038#endif
3039 m_channel.start_receive_native_handle_ops([this,
3040 ev_wait_func = std::move(ev_wait_func)] // Don't need it again. Eat it.
3041 (Asio_waitable_native_handle* hndl_of_interest,
3042 bool ev_of_interest_snd_else_rcv,
3043 Task_ptr&& on_active_ev_func) mutable
3044 {
3045 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: SIO handle-pipe receive-op module: event-wait requested.");
3046 ev_wait_func(hndl_of_interest, ev_of_interest_snd_else_rcv, std::move(on_active_ev_func));
3047 });
3048 assert(ok && "m_started_ops should have guarded against this failing.");
3049 } // if constexpr(HAS_HNDL)
3050
3051 FLOW_LOG_INFO("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Start-ops requested. Done.");
3052
3053 /* We can, and must (see "Protocol negotiation" in class doc header), now send out the outgoing protocol-negotiation;
3054 * plus the channel-header info. */
3055 send_init_msgs();
3056 /* That may have set truthy m_init_msg_err_code_or_ok; in which case
3057 * start_and_poll()/send()/async_request()/etc. will pick it up (whichever happens first). */
3058
3059 return true;
3060} // Channel::start_ops()
3061
3062TEMPLATE_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL
3063bool CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::check_not_started_ops(util::String_view context) const
3064{
3065 if (!m_started_ops)
3066 {
3067 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: This operation (context [" << context << "]) requires "
3068 "start-*-ops which has not been invoked. Ignoring.");
3069 return false; // [sic]
3070 }
3071 return true;
3072}
3073
3074TEMPLATE_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL
3075template<typename Task_err>
3076bool CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::start_and_poll(Task_err&& on_err_func)
3077{
3078 using flow::util::Blob;
3079
3080 if (!check_not_started_ops("start_and_poll()"))
3081 {
3082 return false;
3083 }
3084 // else
3085
3086 if (!m_on_err_func.empty())
3087 {
3088 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Start requested, but we have already started. Ignoring.");
3089 return false;
3090 }
3091 // else
3092
3093 if (m_channel_err_code_or_ok)
3094 {
3095 // As promised do not re-emit: just follow the no-op contingency.
3096 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Start requested, but the error "
3097 "[" << m_channel_err_code_or_ok << "] [" << m_channel_err_code_or_ok.message() << "] "
3098 "was previously emitted by another send()/similar. Ignoring.");
3099 return false;
3100 } // else
3101
3102 m_on_err_func = std::move(on_err_func);
3103 assert(!m_on_err_func.empty());
3104
3105 FLOW_LOG_INFO("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Start requested. Proceeding to start "
3106 "async-receive chain(s). On-receive handlers may now execute.");
3107
3108 // send_init_msgs() explains this. Essentially think of it as a channel-hosing condition that was *just* discovered.
3109 if (m_init_msg_err_code_or_ok)
3110 {
3111 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Start requested, but the error "
3112 "[" << m_init_msg_err_code_or_ok << "] [" << m_init_msg_err_code_or_ok.message() << "] "
3113 "was previously detected when trying to internally send protocol-negotiation + channel-header "
3114 "messages over a pipe (details likely logged earlier). Emitting channel-hosing error.");
3115 handle_new_error(m_init_msg_err_code_or_ok, "start_and_poll()", true);
3116 // ^-- That fired the on-error handler synchronously, satisfying the `_and_poll` part of our name's contract.
3117 return true;
3118 }
3119 // else
3120
3121 /* This is a new structured channel. So our goal is to receive our 1st structured in-message sans handle
3122 * or 1st structured in-message with handle -- we have to be ready for both. This is where we initialize
3123 * that algorithm forever by setting up m_rcv_pipes 2-array of optional<>s (currently both storing nothing).
3124 * From that point on, there will be 1 or 2 async-read chains going, and each will get -- and keep passing along
3125 * via captures and function-args -- one pointer into m_rcv_pipes.
3126 *
3127 * See Msg_in_pipe doc header. Then come back here. This should be clear then. Hope you like reading! */
3128
3129 static_assert(decltype(m_rcv_pipes)::size() == 2, "Maintenance bug?! m_rcv_pipes[] array must have size 2.");
3130
3131 if constexpr(Owned_channel::S_HAS_BLOB_PIPE_ONLY)
3132 {
3133 using Msg_in_pipe_t // Always use m_channel.async_receive_blob*(); sender sends handle => Channel fatal error.
3134 = Msg_in_pipe<Tribool_vals::false_value>; // The Blob_receiver_obj pipe.
3135 const auto sz = m_channel.receive_blob_max_size();
3136 m_rcv_pipes.front().reset
3137 (new Msg_in_pipe_t
3138 {
3139 true, // First message is lead.
3140 0, // Segment count unknown until lead message received.
3141 {}, // We .emplace() just below.
3142 Msg_in_impl<Msg_in>::ct_base(m_struct_reader_config), // Always start with empty message.
3143 // Prepare the simple one-time protocol-negotiation read/serialize op for this pipe.
3144 Segment_blob_in{sz}, {},
3145 false, nullptr // No other pipe.
3146 });
3147 const auto pipe = static_cast<Msg_in_pipe_t*>(m_rcv_pipes.front().get());
3148 auto& batch = pipe->m_target_batch;
3149 batch.emplace(Msg_in_pipe_t::S_RCV_BATCH_SIZE);
3150 do { Segment_blob_in blob{sz}; batch->prepare_target_payload(blob.mutable_buffer(), std::move(blob)); }
3151 while (!batch->initialized());
3152 rcv_async_read_proto_neg_msg(pipe);
3153
3154 assert(!m_rcv_pipes.back());
3155 }
3156 else if constexpr(Owned_channel::S_HAS_NATIVE_HANDLE_PIPE_ONLY)
3157 {
3158 // As above; except Batch is Native_handle_receiver instead of Blob_receiver, and it's OK to receive hndl or not.
3159 using Msg_in_pipe_t = Msg_in_pipe<Tribool_vals::indeterminate_value>; // The Native_handle_receiver_obj pipe.
3160 const auto sz = m_channel.receive_meta_blob_max_size();
3161 m_rcv_pipes.front().reset
3162 (new Msg_in_pipe_t
3163 {
3164 true, 0, {}, Msg_in_impl<Msg_in>::ct_base(m_struct_reader_config), // As above.
3165 Segment_blob_in{sz}, {}, // As above.
3166 false, nullptr // As above.
3167 });
3168 // @todo Code reuse in the following snippet? Problem is it might be harder to understand/more lines.
3169 const auto pipe = static_cast<Msg_in_pipe_t*>(m_rcv_pipes.front().get());
3170 auto& batch = pipe->m_target_batch;
3171 batch.emplace(Msg_in_pipe_t::S_RCV_BATCH_SIZE);
3172 do { Segment_blob_in blob{sz}; batch->prepare_target_payload(blob.mutable_buffer(), std::move(blob)); }
3173 while (!batch->initialized());
3174 rcv_async_read_proto_neg_msg(pipe);
3175
3176 assert(!m_rcv_pipes.back());
3177 }
3178 else // Reminder: The following is only compiled if the above two compile-time conditions are false.
3179 {
3180 static_assert(Owned_channel::S_HAS_2_PIPES, "Maintenance bug?! Channel must have 1 blobs, 1 handles pipe/both.");
3181
3182 // As above, the two combined.
3183
3184 /* Always use m_channel.async_receive_native_handle*(); accept only with-handle lead messages.
3185 * Then m_rcv_pipes.back() below will in-parallel accept only sans-handle lead messages. */
3186 using Msg_in_pipe1_t = Msg_in_pipe<Tribool_vals::true_value>; // The Native_handle_receiver_obj pipe.
3187 using Msg_in_pipe2_t = Msg_in_pipe<Tribool_vals::false_value>; // The Blob_receiver_obj pipe.
3188 const auto sz1 = m_channel.receive_meta_blob_max_size();
3189 const auto sz2 = m_channel.receive_blob_max_size();
3190 m_rcv_pipes.front().reset
3191 (new Msg_in_pipe1_t
3192 {
3193 true, 0, {}, Msg_in_impl<Msg_in>::ct_base(m_struct_reader_config), // As above.
3194 Segment_blob_in{sz1}, {}, // As above.
3195 false, nullptr // Temp nullptr: see below.
3196 });
3197 m_rcv_pipes.back().reset
3198 (new Msg_in_pipe2_t
3199 {
3200 true, 0, {}, Msg_in_impl<Msg_in>::ct_base(m_struct_reader_config), // As above.
3201 Segment_blob_in{sz2}, {}, // As above.
3202 false, nullptr // Temp nullptr: see below.
3203 });
3204
3205 const auto pipe1 = static_cast<Msg_in_pipe1_t*>(m_rcv_pipes.front().get());
3206 const auto pipe2 = static_cast<Msg_in_pipe2_t*>(m_rcv_pipes.back().get());
3207 pipe1->m_other_pipe_gracefully_closed_or_null = &pipe2->m_gracefully_closed;
3208 pipe2->m_other_pipe_gracefully_closed_or_null = &pipe1->m_gracefully_closed;
3209
3210 auto& batch1 = pipe1->m_target_batch;
3211 auto& batch2 = pipe2->m_target_batch;
3212 batch1.emplace(Msg_in_pipe1_t::S_RCV_BATCH_SIZE);
3213 batch2.emplace(Msg_in_pipe2_t::S_RCV_BATCH_SIZE);
3214 do { Segment_blob_in blob{sz1}; batch1->prepare_target_payload(blob.mutable_buffer(), std::move(blob)); }
3215 while (!batch1->initialized());
3216 do { Segment_blob_in blob{sz2}; batch2->prepare_target_payload(blob.mutable_buffer(), std::move(blob)); }
3217 while (!batch2->initialized());
3218
3219 rcv_async_read_proto_neg_msg(pipe1);
3220 if (!m_channel_err_code_or_ok) // ^-- That could've hosed the Channel; e.g. a transport error immediately seen.
3221 {
3222 rcv_async_read_proto_neg_msg(pipe2);
3223 }
3224 } // else if (Owned_channel::S_HAS_2_PIPES)
3225
3226 return true;
3227} // Channel::start_and_poll()

3230template<typename Msg_in_pipe_t>
3231void CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::rcv_async_read(Msg_in_pipe_t* pipe)
3232{
3233 {
3234 /* (Given: *pipe is not hosed, just got past ChannelHeader read.) Formally this guy's doc header says
3235 * rcv_past_init_msgs() <=> we got past the negotiation read + ChannelHeader read. (As of this writing at
3236 * least handle_async_err_code() counts on this.) So let's make it happen, given that we just crossed-over
3237 * into that state. */
3238 assert((!rcv_past_init_msgs(*pipe))
3239 && "The init-messages phase should have kept the invariant that m_init_msg_blob exists.");
3240 pipe->m_init_msg_blob.make_zero();
3241 }
3242
3243 if constexpr(Msg_in_pipe_t::S_RCV_BATCH_SIZE == 1)
3244 {
3245 rcv_async_read_unbatched(pipe);
3246 }
3247 else
3248 {
3249 rcv_async_read_batched(pipe);
3250 }
3251}
