3260TEMPLATE_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL
3261template<typename Msg_in_pipe_t>
3262void CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::rcv_async_read_batched(Msg_in_pipe_t* pipe, bool pessimistic)
3263{
3264 /* The pre-condition is, we are either starting from (basically) start_and_poll(); or we have just read and fully
3265 * processed a batch (of 1+ unstructured in-messages); and now it is time to read the next.
3266 * (If `pessimistic`, then that in-batch was !full(), meaning the pipe is now in would-block, so we simply
3267 * tell the unstructured Owned_channel async-read-batch API that fact, so it can for perf skip an actual
3268 * read attempt and just async-wait right away. Otherwise it may or not be in would-block, so we tell it *that*,
3269 * and it'll try to nb-read first.)
3270 *
3271 * The algorithm below is the usual sync_io-pattern thing, where the goal is to read as much in-data as possible
3272 * until would-block (or error), processing the data fully (which also could lead to error). If no error before we
3273 * hit the would-block, then continue the read-chain by doing an async-wait. In other words it's basically (ignoring
3274 * possibility of error and `pessimistic` details):
3275 * do
3276 * {
3277 * // Either this outputs immediately into *batch, or async-waits, invoking F() eventually once in-batch received.
3278 * async_read(batch, F);
3279 * if (!<it got would-block>) { process the in-batch in *batch; }
3280 * }
3281 * while (!<it got would-block>)
3282 * void F()
3283 * {
3284 * process the in-batch in *batch;
3285 * rcv_async_read_batched(); // Continue read-chain by calling *us*.
3286 * }
3287 * That's what the below does. It's only somewhat different-looking, because (1) it deals with possibility of
3288 * channel-hosing error at various places; and (2) the batch->full() checking is in helper
3289 * rcv_on_async_read_batch() which is where <process in-batch in *batch> code is.
3290 *
3291 * As long as you grok the above algorithm, it should all be reasonably clear from there. */
3292
3293 constexpr auto LEAD_HNDL_EXPECTATION = Msg_in_pipe_t::S_LEAD_HNDL_EXPECTATION;
3294
3295 auto& batch = *pipe->m_target_batch;
3296 bool done = false;
3297 do // while (!done) // Read until would-block (async-read outstanding) or pipe hosed (async-reads finished).
3298 {
3299 // This is invoked asynchronously, if the below async_receive_*() yields would-block. Else it is ignored.
3300 auto on_recv_func = [this, pipe](const Error_code& err_code) mutable
3301 {
3302 // Got 1+ messages or error asynchronously.
3303
3304 const bool pessimistic = !rcv_on_async_read_batch(pipe, err_code);
3305 if (rcv_end_reads(*pipe))
3306 {
3307 return; // Just end read chain, as this in-pipe is hosed.
3308 }
3309 // else: Slide right back to the start of the algorithm; iff [sic] pipe in would-block then `pessimistic` is true.
3310
3311 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: The above on-received-message-batch logic was invoked "
3312 "asynchronously. Continue read-chain; `pessimistic`? = [" << pessimistic << "]; "
3313 "if true batch not totally-full => pipe in would-block => skip nb-read; "
3314 "else pipe may or may not be in would-block => do nb-read first.");
3315 rcv_async_read_batched(pipe, pessimistic);
3316 }; // auto on_recv_func =
3317
3318 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Async-batch-read starting; message 1 of next in-batch shall be "
3319 "[" << (pipe->m_next_msg_lead_else_cont ? "lead" : "continuation") << "]; "
3320 "in-pipe lead-message handle-bearing mode is "
3321 "[" << int(LEAD_HNDL_EXPECTATION) << "]. "
3322 "Pessimistic mode (pre-assumed would-block)? = [" << pessimistic << "].");
3323
3324 assert((batch.n_used() == 0) && "*this Channel should've processed all received messages, creating clean slate.");
3325
3326 Error_code sync_err_code;
3327
3328 if constexpr(LEAD_HNDL_EXPECTATION == Tribool_vals::false_value)
3329 {
3330 m_channel.template async_receive_blob_batch<Segment_blob_in>(&batch, pessimistic, &sync_err_code,
3331 std::move(on_recv_func));
3332 }
3333 else
3334 {
3335 m_channel.template async_receive_native_handle_batch<Segment_blob_in>(&batch, pessimistic, &sync_err_code,
3336 std::move(on_recv_func));
3337 }
3338 assert(((!pessimistic) || sync_err_code)
3339 && "`pessimistic` => async-read must yield would-block (at best) or other error (otherwise).");
3340
3341 if (sync_err_code == transport::error::Code::S_SYNC_IO_WOULD_BLOCK)
3342 {
3343 done = true; continue; // Loop will end. Live to fight another day: async-wait outstanding.
3344 }
3345 // else: Got 1+ messages or error synchronously. Handle it right here (a-la on_recv_func() which won't run).
3346
3347 pessimistic = !rcv_on_async_read_batch(pipe, sync_err_code);
3348 if (rcv_end_reads(*pipe))
3349 {
3350 done = true; continue; // Loop will end. As in on_recv_func(): Just end read chain, as this in-pipe is hosed.
3351 }
3352 // else
3353
3354 /* As in on_recv_func(): iff [sic] pipe in would-block then `pessimistic` is true.
3355 * Unlike there, we just continue our loop, having updated `pessimistic` to true.
3356 * (If `pessimistic` was already true, then we can't be here, as that would've caused would-block above.) */
3357
3358 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: The above on-received-message-batch logic was invoked "
3359 "synchronously (message-batch was immediately pending). "
3360 "Continue read-chain; `pessimistic`? = [" << pessimistic << "]; "
3361 "if true batch not totally-full => pipe in would-block => skip nb-read; "
3362 "else pipe may or may not be in would-block => do nb-read first.");
3363 }
3364 while (!done);
3365} // Channel::rcv_async_read_batched()
3366
3367TEMPLATE_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL
3368template<typename Msg_in_pipe_t>
3369void CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::rcv_async_read_unbatched(Msg_in_pipe_t* pipe)
3370{
3371 /* We are the exact equivalent of rcv_async_read_batched() but executed only if, basically, batching is disabled;
3372 * meaning we are only allowed to execute Owned_channel (Blob_receiver + Native_handle_receiver concepts)
3373 * single-message-read APIs rather than the batchy ones: .async_receive_{blob|native_handle}() rather than
3374 * <same>_batch(). (The batch API is always available, and even if we have RCV_BATCH_SIZE=1 and therefore
3375 * use that API with 1-batches only, it'll work perfectly well; and that layer has its own measures it takes
3376 * to avoid batch-related overhead when the batches are "batches" (contain up to only 1 message). So why does
3377 * this code-path of ours -- which avoids the batch API of Owned_channel entirely -- still exist? To repeat
3378 * the same explanation elsewhere for your convenience; 1, it was available; and 2, it *is* simpler and might
3379 * avoid certain bits of overhead. It can also be thought of as a way to roll-back more fully to the
3380 * state of the code before the batch-receiving feature existed. @todo With time we might get rid of it.
3381 * After all Blob_receiver/Native_handle_receiver impls are required to use batch emulation if no native
3382 * OS batch capabilities exist... so our having our own form thereof might be overkill at this point. Again, though,
3383 * it was available for use, so for now we have kept it.)
3384 *
3385 * We will keep ~full inline comments despite the similarity to rcv_async_read_batched(). It'll help us
3386 * sanity-check both algorithms; plus obviously it'll make the code easier to understand if somewhat lengthier.
3387 *
3388 * So: The pre-condition is, we are either starting from (basically) start_and_poll(); or we have just read and fully
3389 * processed 1 unstructured in-message; and now it is time to read the next. (Since we received, last time,
3390 * by definition of single-message async-receive, exactly 1 in-message -- equivalent to a 1-batch -- the "batch"
3391 * was indeed "full"; hence what would have been the `pessimistic` arg for us would have always been `false.
3392 * So we lack that arg, and the code below reduces to the !pessimistic-branch equivalent of what occurs
3393 * in _batched().
3394 *
3395 * The algorithm below is the usual sync_io-pattern thing, where the goal is to read as much in-data as possible
3396 * until would-block (or error), processing the data fully (which also could lead to error). If no error before we
3397 * hit the would-block, then continue the read-chain by doing an async-wait. In other words it's basically (ignoring
3398 * possibility of error):
3399 * do
3400 * {
3401 * // Either this outputs immediately into *batch, or async-waits, invoking F() eventually once in-batch received.
3402 * // target_slot is slot[0] of 1-batch in *pipe. target_slot comprises simply a Blob [and a Native_handle].
3403 * async_read(target_slot, F);
3404 * if (!<it got would-block>) { process the in-message in target_slot; }
3405 * }
3406 * while (!<it got would-block>)
3407 * void F()
3408 * {
3409 * process the in-message in target_slot;
3410 * rcv_async_read_unbatched(); // Continue read-chain by calling *us*.
3411 * }
3412 * That's what the below does. It's only somewhat different-looking, because it deals with possibility of
3413 * channel-hosing error at various places. (The equivalent of batch->full() is always true for us, so
3414 * rcv_on_async_read_one() -- our version of rcv_on_async_read_batch() -- is void instead of returning bool;
3415 * and we act as-if it returned true in the _batched() equivalent of us.)
3416 *
3417 * As long as you grok the above algorithm, it should all be reasonably clear from there. */
3418
3419 constexpr auto LEAD_HNDL_EXPECTATION = Msg_in_pipe_t::S_LEAD_HNDL_EXPECTATION;
3420
3421 auto& batch = *pipe->m_target_batch;
3422 assert((batch.n_used() == 0) && "*this Channel shouldn't use batch facilities except as a simple target store.");
3423
3424 [[maybe_unused]] Native_handle* target_hndl;
3425 if constexpr(LEAD_HNDL_EXPECTATION != Tribool_vals::false_value)
3426 {
3427 target_hndl = pipe->m_target_batch->next_target_hndl(); // Always the same.
3428 }
3429
3430 bool done = false;
3431 do // while (!done) // Read until would-block (async-read outstanding) or pipe hosed (async-reads finished).
3432 {
3433 // This is invoked asynchronously, if the below async_receive_*() yields would-block. Else it is ignored.
3434 auto on_recv_func = [this, pipe](const Error_code& err_code, size_t sz) mutable
3435 {
3436 // Got 1 message or error asynchronously.
3437
3438 rcv_on_async_read_one(pipe, err_code, sz);
3439 if (!rcv_end_reads(*pipe))
3440 {
3441 // Slide right back to the start of the algorithm.
3442 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: The above on-received-message logic was invoked "
3443 "asynchronously. Continue read-chain.");
3444 rcv_async_read_unbatched(pipe);
3445 }
3446 // else { Just end read chain, as this in-pipe is hosed. }
3447 }; // auto on_recv_func =
3448
3449 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Async-read starting; next message shall be "
3450 "[" << (pipe->m_next_msg_lead_else_cont ? "lead" : "continuation") << "]; "
3451 "in-pipe lead-message handle-bearing mode is "
3452 "[" << int(LEAD_HNDL_EXPECTATION) << "].");
3453
3454 Error_code sync_err_code;
3455 size_t sync_sz;
3456
3457 if constexpr(LEAD_HNDL_EXPECTATION == Tribool_vals::false_value)
3458 {
3459 m_channel.async_receive_blob(batch.next_target_blob(), &sync_err_code, &sync_sz,
3460 std::move(on_recv_func));
3461 }
3462 else
3463 {
3464 m_channel.async_receive_native_handle(target_hndl, batch.next_target_blob(), &sync_err_code, &sync_sz,
3465 std::move(on_recv_func));
3466 }
3467
3468 if (sync_err_code == transport::error::Code::S_SYNC_IO_WOULD_BLOCK)
3469 {
3470 done = true; continue; // Loop will end. Live to fight another day: async-wait outstanding.
3471 }
3472 // else: Got 1 message or error synchronously. Handle it right here (a-la on_recv_func() which won't run).
3473
3474 rcv_on_async_read_one(pipe, sync_err_code, sync_sz);
3475 if (rcv_end_reads(*pipe))
3476 {
3477 done = true; continue; // Loop will end. As in on_recv_func(): Just end read chain, as this in-pipe is hosed.
3478 }
3479 // else
3480
3481 /* As in on_recv_func() log a thing but unlike there, we just continue our loop to enter another async-read.
3482 * That is we enter another async-read, same as there, just no call required to do it. */
3483
3484 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: The above on-received-message logic was invoked "
3485 "synchronously (message was immediately pending). Continue read-chain.");
3486 }
3487 while (!done);
3488} // Channel::rcv_async_read_unbatched()
3489
3490TEMPLATE_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL
3491template<typename Msg_in_pipe_t>
3492bool CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::rcv_on_async_read_batch(Msg_in_pipe_t* pipe, const Error_code& err_code)
3493{
3494 using util::Own_native_handle;
3495
3496 constexpr auto LEAD_HNDL_EXPECTATION = Msg_in_pipe_t::S_LEAD_HNDL_EXPECTATION;
3497 constexpr bool NO_HNDLS = LEAD_HNDL_EXPECTATION == Tribool_vals::false_value;
3498
3499 /* Per our doc header: Our job is to fully read to one of the following having just occurred as a result of
3500 * an async-read-batch call, synchronously or otherwise:
3501 * - got an in-batch (1+ unstructured in-messages); or
3502 * - got a hosing error (not would-block).
3503 *
3504 * We are to fully handle that but *not* perpetuating the read-chain in the former case, as that's the caller's
3505 * responsibility. Also, in this and all our helpers, the only way we communicate to the caller that the
3506 * read chain must end is by setting <stuff rcv_end_reads() checks> to truthy. */
3507
3508 assert(err_code != transport::error::Code::S_OBJECT_SHUTDOWN_ABORTED_COMPLETION_HANDLER); // sync_io must not do this.
3509 assert(err_code != boost::asio::error::operation_aborted); // Or definitely this.
3510
3511 auto& batch = *pipe->m_target_batch;
3512 const auto n_rcvd = batch.n_used();
3513
3514 /* Before we return -- as enforced via inner-function below -- we must close any `Native_handle`s in
3515 * `batch` that did not get Own_native_handle-wrapped and routed to rcv_on_async_read_*_msg(); that is to
3516 * say each one belonging to a slot >X, where rcv_on_async_read_*_msg(<slot X>) detected a (channel-hosing)
3517 * error. An error in slot X => the rest of the slots are disregarded -- correctly at that, except that we don't
3518 * want to leak any possible handle(s) in "the rest of the slots."
3519 *
3520 * (As of this writing, only opposing-side-is-buggy errors are possible in this context, so -- assuming a
3521 * properly behaved peer -- this should not arise. But: (1) better safe than sorry (maybe the peer *is* buggy,
3522 * in some obscure case especially); and (2) it's conceivable opposing *user* behavior will be able to, at
3523 * some point, trigger channel-hosing here. Shouldn't be possible as of this writing, but we prefer to be
3524 * robust in the face of future code development. Thus: handle all this/don't ignore it.)
3525 *
3526 * Additionally: handle_async_err_code() might detect a (non-`err_code`) error; in which case all slots'
3527 * (potential) handles shall be cleaned, as all slots' contents shall be ignored.
3528 *
3529 * Thus: hndl_cleanup_idx shall be set so that each potential handle in slot-range [hndl_cleanup_idx, n_rcvd)
3530 * shall be closed. hndl_cleanup_idx==n_rcvd <=> empty range <=> no slots to check. */
3531 [[maybe_unused]] size_t hndl_cleanup_idx;
3532 if constexpr(!NO_HNDLS)
3533 {
3534 hndl_cleanup_idx = n_rcvd; // No cleanup, by default. Error scenarios below <=> overwrite appropriately.
3535 }
3536 // else if (NO_HNDLS) { We'll ignore hndl_cleanup_idx; no handles => no handles possible along pipe => no cleanup. }
3537
3538 const bool ret = ([&]() -> bool
3539 {
3540 // Remember: Any error (channel-hosing) return from this lambda => first set hndl_cleanup_idx, then return.
3541
3542 if (!handle_async_err_code(pipe, err_code, "rcv_on_async_read_batch()"))
3543 {
3544 /* If that detected a *new* error, it fired the on-error handler.
3545 * It's over -- the entire read chain must stop -- either because of us or an earlier pipe hosing. */
3546
3547 if constexpr(!NO_HNDLS)
3548 {
3549 /* Close *all* (potential) handles.
3550 * - If handle_async_err_code(), which returned false, did so because of err_code being truthy:
3551 * `0 == n_rcvd` anyway (<=> truthy err_code) =>
3552 * cleanup will no-op, as there is indeed nothing to clean.
3553 * - If it did so because of a prior channel-hosing (while err_code is falsy):
3554 * `n_rcvd > 0`; cleanup will indeed check 1+ slots for handles and close such.
3555 * In short: If 1+ handle(s) received, all will be closed; else nothing bad will happen (nothing to close). */
3556 hndl_cleanup_idx = 0;
3557 }
3558
3559 return false; // As advertised we return false in this case, but really they shouldn't care what we return then.
3560 }
3561 // else if (all good (including !err_code)):
3562
3563 assert((n_rcvd != 0) && "async_receive_..._batch() must yield either an error or 1+ in-messages.");
3564 assert((!rcv_end_reads(*pipe)) && "We should have returned above already due to !handle_async_err_code().");
3565
3566 for (size_t idx = 0; idx != n_rcvd; // @todo Always false first time. do/while?
3567 ++idx)
3568 /* Attn: truthy m_channel_err_code_or_ok also halts loop; but via `return`. (Normally we'd prefer to
3569 * avoid mid-loop exits outside the loop-end condition, stylistically, but in this case we felt it safer,
3570 * maintenance-wise, to keep hndl_cleanup_idx assignment next to `return`.) */
3571 {
3572 Segment_blob_in* blob_in_batch;
3573 const auto sz = batch.result_payload_blob(idx, &blob_in_batch);
3574
3575 const auto max_sz = blob_in_batch->size();
3576 assert(max_sz == blob_in_batch->capacity());
3577
3578 Own_native_handle hndl;
3579 if constexpr(!NO_HNDLS)
3580 {
3581 hndl.reset(batch.result_payload_hndl(idx));
3582 // (This method --^ does not exist if `NO_HNDLS == true`.)
3583 }
3584 // else { We used .async_receive_blob_batch(), meaning handles are not accepted at the lower layer. }
3585
3586 pipe->m_next_msg_lead_else_cont
3587 ? rcv_on_async_read_lead_msg(pipe, blob_in_batch, sz, std::move(hndl))
3588 : rcv_on_async_read_continuation_msg(pipe, blob_in_batch, sz, std::move(hndl));
3589
3590 // (Any handler(s) resulting from that call fired synchronously within it: see handlers_post().)
3591
3592 if (m_channel_err_code_or_ok)
3593 {
3594 /* Channel-hosing error occurred; stop entire read chain; so no need to even reset this `batch` slot.
3595 * So now `return false`.... */
3596
3597 if constexpr(!NO_HNDLS)
3598 {
3599 /* ...but first, ensure we shall close all (potential) handles in the *remaining* (otherwise fully ignored)
3600 * slots (if any).
3601 * - If `idx == <last idx>`: hndl_cleanup_idx == n_rcvd =>
3602 * cleanup will no-op, as there is indeed nothing to clean.
3603 * - Else if `idx < <last idx>`:
3604 * cleanup will indeed check 1+ slots for handles and close such.
3605 * In any case, `idx`th slot is already handled (hndl is auto-closing Own_native_handle). */
3606 hndl_cleanup_idx = idx + 1;
3607 }
3608
3609 return false; // As advertised we return false in this case, but really they shouldn't care what we return then.
3610 }
3611 // else: Reset this `batch` slot for the next async-receive. So do just like in start_and_poll().
3612
3613 Segment_blob_in new_blob{max_sz};
3614 batch.prepare_target_payload(new_blob.mutable_buffer(), std::move(new_blob), idx);
3615 } // for (idx in [0, n_rcvd))
3616
3617 assert((!m_channel_err_code_or_ok) && "We should have returned inside the loop, on any error.");
3618
3619 /* It's possible (actually fairly probable) there is
3620 * implied would-block, meaning that we got some messages but not enough to fill all available slots; this
3621 * implies no more messages are available right now, so indeed we should return true in that case.
3622 * Otherwise it's indeterminate: could be a coincidence we got exactly enough to fill slots; or could be
3623 * because there's more to read. */
3624 return batch.full();
3625 })(); // const bool ret = ([&]() -> bool
3626
3627 if constexpr(!NO_HNDLS) // Handle-cleanup range (usually/hopefully empty) decided above.
3628 {
3629 for (; hndl_cleanup_idx != n_rcvd; ++hndl_cleanup_idx)
3630 {
3631 Own_native_handle hndl{batch.result_payload_hndl(hndl_cleanup_idx)};
3632 if (!hndl.get().null())
3633 {
3634 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Due to channel-hosing error condition (should be logged "
3635 "above) manually closing not-otherwise-auto-closed native-handle [" << hndl.get() << "].");
3636 }
3637 // hndl.get() gets auto-.close()d here.
3638 }
3639 }
3640
3641 /* The following logic only matters `if (!rcv_end_reads())`, but it's harmless even otherwise, so no point
3642 * checking. That said the following comment assumes !rcv_end_reads():
3643 *
3644 * Lastly: we've reset all the received-into slots to accept more in-messages; so reset .n_used() == 0.
3645 * After this statement `batch` will have become a clean slate again as needed for the next read (whether it's now
3646 * or later).
3647 *
3648 * (Careful: Cannot, or at least should not, do this before the potential cleanup-loop just above; would attempt
3649 * accessor-use at idx>=0, when .n_used()==0 already.) */
3650 batch.clear_used();
3651
3652 return ret;
3653} // Channel::rcv_on_async_read_batch()
3654
3655TEMPLATE_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL
3656template<typename Msg_in_pipe_t>
3657void CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::rcv_on_async_read_one(Msg_in_pipe_t* pipe, const Error_code& err_code, size_t sz)
3658{
3659 using util::Own_native_handle;
3660
3661 /* We are the exact equivalent of rcv_on_async_read_batch() but executed only if, basically, batching is disabled;
3662 * meaning we are only allowed to execute Owned_channel (Blob_receiver + Native_handle_receiver concepts)
3663 * single-message-read APIs rather than the batchy ones: .async_receive_{blob|native_handle}() rather than
3664 * <same>_batch().
3665 *
3666 * We will keep ~full inline comments despite the similarity to rcv_async_read_batched(). It'll help us
3667 * sanity-check both algorithms; plus obviously it'll make the code easier to understand if somewhat lengthier.
3668 * ...But really, though, it's the same thing -- just instead of a loop, it handles slot 0 of the "batch"
3669 * which is where we keep the target blob [and target Native_handle].
3670 *
3671 * Per our doc header: Our job is to fully read to one of the following having just occurred as a result of
3672 * an async-read-message call, synchronously or otherwise:
3673 * - got an in-message; or
3674 * - got a hosing error (not would-block).
3675 *
3676 * We are to fully handle that but *not* perpetuating the read-chain in the former case, as that's the caller's
3677 * responsibility. Also, in this and all our helpers, the only way we communicate to the caller that the
3678 * read chain must end is by setting <stuff rcv_end_reads() checks> to truthy. */
3679
3680 constexpr auto LEAD_HNDL_EXPECTATION = Msg_in_pipe_t::S_LEAD_HNDL_EXPECTATION;
3681
3682 assert(err_code != transport::error::Code::S_OBJECT_SHUTDOWN_ABORTED_COMPLETION_HANDLER); // sync_io must not do this.
3683 assert(err_code != boost::asio::error::operation_aborted); // Or definitely this.
3684
3685 auto& batch = *pipe->m_target_batch;
3686
3687 /* A-la rcv_on_async_read_proto_neg_msg(): Wrap in-handle (if any) in auto-closing storage, ASAP, so that it cannot
3688 * be leaked. */
3689 Own_native_handle hndl;
3690 if constexpr(LEAD_HNDL_EXPECTATION != Tribool_vals::false_value)
3691 {
3692 if (!err_code)
3693 {
3694 hndl.reset(batch.result_payload_hndl(0));
3695 // (This method --^ does not exist if `LEAD_HNDL_EXPECTATION == false_value`.)
3696 }
3697 }
3698 // else { We used .async_receive_blob(), meaning handles are not accepted at the lower layer. }
3699
3700 if (!handle_async_err_code(pipe, err_code, "rcv_on_async_read_one()"))
3701 {
3702 // If that detected a *new* error, it fired the on-error handler.
3703 return; // It's over -- the entire read chain must stop -- either because of us or an earlier pipe hosing.
3704 }
3705 // else if (all good (including !err_code)):
3706
3707 Segment_blob_in* blob_in_batch;
3708 batch.result_payload_blob(0, &blob_in_batch);
3709
3710 const auto max_sz = blob_in_batch->size();
3711 assert(max_sz == blob_in_batch->capacity());
3712
3713 pipe->m_next_msg_lead_else_cont
3714 ? rcv_on_async_read_lead_msg(pipe, blob_in_batch, sz, std::move(hndl))
3715 : rcv_on_async_read_continuation_msg(pipe, blob_in_batch, sz, std::move(hndl));
3716
3717 // (Any handler(s) resulting from that call fired synchronously within it: see handlers_post().)
3718
3719 if (!m_channel_err_code_or_ok)
3720 {
3721 // Reset this `batch` slot 0 for the next async-receive. So do just like in start_and_poll().
3722 Segment_blob_in new_blob{max_sz};
3723 const auto new_blob_buf = new_blob.mutable_buffer();
3724 batch.prepare_target_payload(new_blob_buf, std::move(new_blob), 0);
3725
3726 /* Now `batch` (really its first and only slot) is a clean slate again as needed for the next read (whether it's
3727 * now or later). */
3728 }
3729 // else { Channel-hosing error occurred; stop entire read chain. No need to even reset `batch` slot 0. }
3730} // Channel::rcv_on_async_read_one()
3731
3732TEMPLATE_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL
3733template<typename Msg_in_pipe_t>
3734void CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::rcv_on_async_read_lead_msg(Msg_in_pipe_t* pipe,
3735 Segment_blob_in* target_blob_ptr, size_t sz,
3736 util::Own_native_handle&& target_hndl)
3737{
3738 constexpr auto LEAD_HNDL_EXPECTATION = Msg_in_pipe_t::S_LEAD_HNDL_EXPECTATION;
3739
3740 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Handler for would-be lead unstructured "
3741 "in-message invoked; size received = [" << sz << "]; "
3742 "native handle if any = [" << target_hndl.get() << "].");
3743
3744 if constexpr(LEAD_HNDL_EXPECTATION == Tribool_vals::true_value)
3745 {
3746 if (target_hndl.get().null())
3747 {
3748 /* This is possible but only due to remote-peer misbehavior (sending us weird stuff/over wrong channel).
3749 * So it's not an assert() situation firstly. What it's similar-ish to is when, say, a lower-level
3750 * Native_socket_stream (not that it has to be in Owned_channel -- just using it as an example/foil)
3751 * was invoked with async_receive_blob() but internally detected a Native_handle arrived too.
3752 * It's a protocol misbehavior on the part of the user of the low-level/unstructured Channel.
3753 * In our case it is also that (we are the user of said Channel); it's just that Channel cannot detect that
3754 * for us by itself (it simply lacks the API for "require Native_handle!"). If it had that capability,
3755 * it would've emitted the err_code stating that (as it does in the analogous scenario:
3756 * error::Code::S_BLOB_RECEIVER_GOT_NON_BLOB). So: we'll do just that ourselves. */
3757 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Handler for would-be lead unstructured "
3758 "in-message invoked sans low-level error; but received sans-handle low-level message "
3759 "along the handles-only pipe (of 2 pipes). Other side misbehaved?");
3760 handle_new_error(error::Code::S_STRUCT_CHANNEL_INTERNAL_PROTOCOL_MISMATCH_GOT_NO_HNDL,
3761 "rcv_on_async_read_lead_msg(1)");
3762 return;
3763 }
3764 }
3765 else if constexpr(LEAD_HNDL_EXPECTATION == Tribool_vals::false_value)
3766 {
3767 assert(target_hndl.get().null()
3768 && "Bug? Somehow we have truthy target_hndl yet should've invoked async_receive_blob() "
3769 "which can't do that.");
3770 }
3771 // else if (LEAD_HNDL_EXPECTATION == indeterminate_value) { All good; target_hndl can be truthy or falsy. }
3772
3773 /* Another corner case is a message with an empty blob. At the transport::Channel (unstructured, low) level it's
3774 * allowed. We (struc::Channel) never use this ability however. It would be a protocol error on the remote peer's
3775 * part. */
3776 if (sz == 0)
3777 {
3778 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Handler for would-be lead unstructured "
3779 "in-message invoked sans low-level error; but got no (meta-)blob at all. Other side misbehaved?");
3780 handle_new_error(error::Code::S_STRUCT_CHANNEL_INTERNAL_PROTOCOL_MISMATCH_GOT_NO_BLOB,
3781 "rcv_on_async_read_lead_msg(2)");
3782 return;
3783 }
3784 // else
3785
3786 auto& target_blob = *target_blob_ptr;
3787
3788 // Ignore garbage after the received bytes (this is permanent).
3789 target_blob.resize(sz);
3790
3791 // OK, target_blob inside *pipe is finalized; feed it into m_incomplete_msg, so that that part is also finalized.
3792 Msg_in_impl<Msg_in> incomplete_msg{ *pipe->m_incomplete_msg }; // Gain access to back-end API.
3793 incomplete_msg.add_serialization_segment(std::move(target_blob));
3794 // target_blob is now nullified, and *pipe->m_incomplete_msg owns what target_blob had just before.
3795
3796 // Finalize the Native_handle (if any) in m_incomplete_msg.
3797 incomplete_msg.store_native_handle_or_null(util::disowned_native_handle(std::move(target_hndl)));
3798
3799 // Because segment 1 inside m_incomplete_msg is now finalized, we can now access:
3800 {
3801 Error_code err_code;
3802
3803 /* Note this will update stats .m_rcv.m_msg by contract, but only if the mdt indicates it is an internal body.
3804 * Otherwise .deserialize_body() will do it (that could happen just below in rcv_struct_new_msg_in(); or
3805 * in that same method but after 1+ more blobs arrive). */
3806 pipe->m_n_segs_left_pre_last_read
3807 = incomplete_msg.deserialize_mdt(get_logger(), &err_code, &m_stats.m_rcv.m_msg);
3808 if (err_code) // It logged on error.
3809 {
3810 handle_new_error(err_code, "rcv_on_async_read_lead_msg(3)");
3811 return;
3812 }
3813 // else
3814
3815 // (W/r/t to the pretty-print -- see any comments near the somewhat-mirrored call in send_*(). May apply here.)
3816 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Deserialized (zero-copy) new structured in-message: "
3817 "mandatory metadata portion; further segment count (including one, if any, in this msg): "
3818 "[" << pipe->m_n_segs_left_pre_last_read << "]; "
3819 "here is the metadata header: "
3820 "\n" << ostreamable_capnp_full(incomplete_msg.mdt_root()));
3821 }
3822
3823 // Now to finalize dealing with the in-message.
3824
3825 if (pipe->m_n_segs_left_pre_last_read <= 1)
3826 {
3827 /* Sweet: Lead unstructured message encoded entire structured message.
3828 * (Context: Well, that's true, but if n_segs_left_including_this_read is 0, then it is an internal message;
3829 * if it is 1, then it is a user message that only required 1 capnp segment to be fully serialized -- it is shared
3830 * between the mdt header parsed by .deserialize_mdt() above and user message seg1. In fact for efficiency we
3831 * would hope that most/all user messages are like that, not requiring continuation messages/more OS-read calls.
3832 * rcv_struct_new_msg_in() will figure out which one is the case efficiently, so we don't need to tell it via
3833 * arg.) */
3834
3835 rcv_struct_new_msg_in(std::move(pipe->m_incomplete_msg));
3836 if (m_channel_err_code_or_ok)
3837 {
3838 return; // Channel-hosing deserialization error (it logged).
3839 }
3840 // else
3841
3842 // So get the next one (async)! Re-init these similarly to start_and_poll().
3843 pipe->m_incomplete_msg = Msg_in_impl<Msg_in>::ct_base(m_struct_reader_config);
3844 pipe->m_n_segs_left_pre_last_read = 0; // 1 -> 0 (or 0 -> 0, no-op).
3845 // Note: Resetting, like, target_blob and pipe->m_target_batch of which it is part = not our responsibility.
3846
3847 // And now indeed recommend reading the next lead message.
3848 assert(pipe->m_next_msg_lead_else_cont && "We are lead message... so this should not need to change.");
3849 } // if (pipe->m_n_segs_left_pre_last_read <= 1)
3850 else // if (pipe->m_n_segs_left_pre_last_read > 1)
3851 {
3852 // Need more segments to come in. Keep m_incomplete_msg, as it's still incomplete. Get next blob to async-read-to.
3853 --pipe->m_n_segs_left_pre_last_read;
3854
3855 // And now recommend reading the 1st continuation message.
3856 assert(pipe->m_next_msg_lead_else_cont);
3857 pipe->m_next_msg_lead_else_cont = false;
3858 }
3859} // Channel::rcv_on_async_read_lead_msg()
3860
3861TEMPLATE_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL
3862template<typename Msg_in_pipe_t>
3863void CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::rcv_on_async_read_continuation_msg(Msg_in_pipe_t* pipe,
3864 Segment_blob_in* target_blob_ptr, size_t sz,
3865 util::Own_native_handle&& target_hndl)
3866{
3867 constexpr auto LEAD_HNDL_EXPECTATION = Msg_in_pipe_t::S_LEAD_HNDL_EXPECTATION;
3868
3869 // In its initial basics this method is much like rcv_on_async_read_lead_msg(). Consider reading that one first.
3870
3871 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Handler for would-be continuation unstructured "
3872 "in-message invoked; size received = [" << sz << "]; "
3873 "native handle if any = [" << target_hndl.get() << "].");
3874
3875 if constexpr(LEAD_HNDL_EXPECTATION == Tribool_vals::false_value)
3876 {
3877 // Same check as in other branch, but along this no-handles channel it implies our bug as opposed to *their* bug.
3878 assert(target_hndl.get().null()
3879 && "Bug? Somehow we have truthy target_hndl yet should've invoked async_receive_blob() "
3880 "which can't do that.");
3881 }
3882 else // if constexpr(LEAD_HNDL_EXPECTATION == true_value or indeterminate_value)
3883 {
3884 if (!target_hndl.get().null())
3885 {
3886 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Handler for would-be continuation "
3887 "unstructured in-message invoked sans low-level error; but it contains native handle; "
3888 "this is not allowed for continuation messages by definition. Other side misbehaved?");
3889 handle_new_error(error::Code::S_STRUCT_CHANNEL_INTERNAL_PROTOCOL_MISMATCH_GOT_HNDL,
3890 "rcv_on_async_read_continuation_msg(1)");
3891 return;
3892 }
3893 // else if (target_hndl.get().null()) { All good; continuation messages never have handles. }
3894 }
3895
3896 // Continuation message is just the blob (we've now ensured this), and all of it is simply the next segment/chunk.
3897
3898 if (sz == 0)
3899 {
3900 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Handler for would-be continuation "
3901 "unstructured in-message invoked sans low-level error; but got no (meta-)blob at all. "
3902 "Other side misbehaved?");
3903 handle_new_error(error::Code::S_STRUCT_CHANNEL_INTERNAL_PROTOCOL_MISMATCH_GOT_NO_BLOB,
3904 "rcv_on_async_read_continuation_msg(2)");
3905 return;
3906 }
3907 // else
3908
3909 auto& target_blob = *target_blob_ptr;
3910
3911 // Ignore garbage after the received bytes (this is permanent).
3912 target_blob.resize(sz);
3913
3914 // OK, target_blob inside *pipe is finalized; feed it into m_incomplete_msg, so that that part is also finalized.
3915 Msg_in_impl<Msg_in> incomplete_msg{ *pipe->m_incomplete_msg }; // Gain access to back-end API.
3916 incomplete_msg.add_serialization_segment(std::move(target_blob));
3917 // target_blob is now nullified, and *pipe->m_incomplete_msg owns what target_blob had just before.
3918
3919 // Now to finalize dealing with the in-message.
3920 if (pipe->m_n_segs_left_pre_last_read == 1)
3921 {
3922 // Sweet: This is the last expected continuation message.
3923 rcv_struct_new_msg_in(std::move(pipe->m_incomplete_msg));
3924 if (m_channel_err_code_or_ok)
3925 {
3926 return; // Channel-hosing deserialization error (it logged).
3927 }
3928 // else
3929
3930 // So recommend getting the next structured in-message! Re-init these similarly to start_and_poll().
3931 pipe->m_incomplete_msg = Msg_in_impl<Msg_in>::ct_base(m_struct_reader_config);
3932 pipe->m_n_segs_left_pre_last_read = 0; // 1 -> 0.
3933 // Note: Resetting, like, target_blob and pipe->m_target_batch of which it is part = not our responsibility.
3934
3935 assert(!pipe->m_next_msg_lead_else_cont);
3936 pipe->m_next_msg_lead_else_cont = true;
3937 } // if (pipe->m_n_segs_left_pre_last_read == 1)
3938 else // if (pipe->m_n_segs_left_pre_last_read > 1)
3939 {
3940 // Need more segments to come in. Keep m_incomplete_msg, as it's still incomplete.
3941 --pipe->m_n_segs_left_pre_last_read;
3942
3943 assert(!pipe->m_next_msg_lead_else_cont);
3944 }
3945} // Channel::rcv_on_async_read_continuation_msg()
3946
3947TEMPLATE_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL
3948template<typename Msg_in_pipe_t>
3949void CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::rcv_async_read_proto_neg_msg(Msg_in_pipe_t* pipe)
3950{
3951 constexpr auto LEAD_HNDL_EXPECTATION = Msg_in_pipe_t::S_LEAD_HNDL_EXPECTATION;
3952
3953 /* The code here is reasonably easy to follow. We want to read exactly 1 protocol-negotiation message
3954 * (see "Protocol negotiation" in class doc header), verify it, and then rcv_async_read(pipe)
3955 * which does the real work along this pipe, async-reading the first real message (etc.). If this fails
3956 * (a read fails, or protocol negotiation fails), then stop the read chain and report error via the
3957 * on-error handler.
3958 *
3959 * That said, it may be interesting to note that this is a much simpler/cut-down version of
3960 * rcv_async_read_unbatched(); the main source of simplicity is we want up-to-1-message-or-error;
3961 * whereas they have an endless loop (conceptually speaking). Nevertheless, modulo those differences, this code
3962 * is based on that code. */
3963
3964 Error_code sync_err_code;
3965 size_t sync_sz;
3966
3967 // What happens if (and only if) our synchronous/non-blocking async_receive_*() yields message/error, not would-block.
3968 auto on_recv_func = [this, pipe](const Error_code& err_code, size_t sz) mutable
3969 {
3970 rcv_on_async_read_proto_neg_msg(pipe, err_code, sz);
3971 };
3972
3973 // With that in mind, here in sync-land: Read unstructured message.
3974
3975 if constexpr(LEAD_HNDL_EXPECTATION == Tribool_vals::false_value)
3976 {
3977 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Async-read starting for protocol-negotiation message "
3978 "along blobs-only pipe.");
3979 m_channel.async_receive_blob(pipe->m_init_msg_blob.mutable_buffer(), &sync_err_code, &sync_sz,
3980 std::move(on_recv_func));
3981 }
3982 else
3983 {
3984 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Async-read starting for protocol-negotiation message "
3985 "along blobs-and-handles pipe.");
3986 m_channel.async_receive_native_handle(&pipe->m_init_msg_hndl, pipe->m_init_msg_blob.mutable_buffer(),
3987 &sync_err_code, &sync_sz,
3988 std::move(on_recv_func));
3989 }
3990
3991 if (sync_err_code == transport::error::Code::S_SYNC_IO_WOULD_BLOCK)
3992 {
3993 return; // Live to fight another day: async-wait outstanding.
3994 }
3995 // else: Got a message or error synchronously. Handle it right here (a-la on_recv_func() which won't run).
3996
3997 rcv_on_async_read_proto_neg_msg(pipe, sync_err_code, sync_sz);
3998} // Channel::rcv_async_read_proto_neg_msg()
3999
4000TEMPLATE_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL
4001template<typename Msg_in_pipe_t>
4002void CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::rcv_on_async_read_proto_neg_msg(Msg_in_pipe_t* pipe, Error_code err_code, size_t sz)
4003{
4004 using util::Own_native_handle;
4005 using flow::util::Blob;
4006 using std::exception;
4007 auto& blob = pipe->m_init_msg_blob;
4008
4009 Own_native_handle init_msg_hndl; // Get it into an auto-closing holder to avoid any possible leak.
4010 if (!err_code)
4011 {
4012 init_msg_hndl.reset(std::move(pipe->m_init_msg_hndl));
4013 }
4014
4015 if (!handle_async_err_code(pipe, err_code, "rcv_on_async_read_proto_neg_msg()"))
4016 {
4017 blob.make_zero(); // Might as well free the memory.
4018 return; // It's over, either because of us or an earlier pipe hosing.
4019 }
4020 // else if (all good (including !err_code)):
4021
4022 if (m_protocol_negotiator.negotiated_proto_ver() != Protocol_negotiator::S_VER_UNKNOWN)
4023 {
4024 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Async-receive handler for would-be protocol-negotiation "
4025 "in-message invoked; size received = [" << sz << "]. However, the "
4026 "negotiation already succeeded along the other pipe; assuming "
4027 "this is the same information; ignoring; will continue read chain "
4028 "(grab channel-header info, then do real work along this pipe).");
4029
4030 /* @todo We fully ignore the contents of what arrived here (as just noted, because it is at best redundant info),
4031 * but if we wanted to be (more) defensive against opposing-side (whom we trust as non-malicious) bugginess,
4032 * then we'd check what arrived anyway: ensure null hndl, ensure the protocol-version info matches....
4033 * It's not high-priority (and would create another hosing-capable path to maintain). It would be nice for
4034 * increased air-tightness. */
4035
4036 // (Do not `blob.make_zero();`! The following call will reuse `blob`... same as the other `if` path below.)
4037 rcv_async_read_channel_header(pipe);
4038 return;
4039 }
4040 // else
4041
4042 Protocol_negotiator::proto_ver_t proto_ver = Protocol_negotiator::S_VER_UNKNOWN;
4043 Protocol_negotiator::proto_ver_t proto_ver_aux = Protocol_negotiator::S_VER_UNKNOWN;
4044
4045 if (!init_msg_hndl.get().null())
4046 {
4047 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Async-receive handler for would-be protocol-negotiation "
4048 "in-message invoked; size received = [" << sz << "]. The message contains a native handle; "
4049 "this is wrong in this context -- bug somewhere, possibly in opposing process? "
4050 "Protocol negotiation will fail.");
4051 }
4052 else
4053 {
4054 // Interpret the received protocol-negotiation in-message.
4055
4056 /* Ignore garbage after the received bytes (this is permanent). No need to `blob.resize(sz)`; capnp will
4057 * just ignore the garbage trailing area. This way rcv_async_read_channel_header() can just reuse `blob`
4058 * without having to futz with .resize()ing it yet again. */
4059
4060 try
4061 {
4062 Capped_sz_capnp_message_reader proto_neg_reader{blob.const_buffer()};
4063 const auto root = proto_neg_reader.getRoot<schema::detail::ProtocolNegotiation>(); // Can throw.
4064 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Would-be protocol-negotiation in-message contents:"
4065 "\n" << ostreamable_capnp_full(root));
4066
4067 proto_ver = root.getMaxProtoVer();
4068 proto_ver_aux = root.getMaxProtoVerAux();
4069 }
4070 catch (const exception& exc)
4071 {
4072 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Async-receive handler for would-be protocol-negotiation "
4073 "in-message invoked; size received = [" << sz << "]. Could not capnp-deserialize the "
4074 "contents; protocol negotiation will fail. Exception = [" << exc.what() << "].");
4075 assert(proto_ver == Protocol_negotiator::S_VER_UNKNOWN);
4076 }
4077 }
4078
4079 /* Now to negotiate (or intentionally fail, if that weird WARNING-inducing thing above happened).
4080 * Protocol_negotiator handles everything (invalid value, incompatible range...). */
4081#ifndef NDEBUG
4082 bool ok =
4083#endif
4084 m_protocol_negotiator.compute_negotiated_proto_ver(proto_ver, &err_code);
4085 assert(ok && "Protocol_negotiator breaking contract? Bug?");
4086 if (!err_code)
4087 {
4088#ifndef NDEBUG
4089 ok =
4090#endif
4091 m_protocol_negotiator_aux.compute_negotiated_proto_ver(proto_ver_aux, &err_code);
4092 assert(ok && "Protocol_negotiator breaking contract? Bug?");
4093 }
4094
4095 if (err_code)
4096 {
4097 handle_new_error(err_code, "rcv_on_async_read_proto_neg_msg()");
4098 blob.make_zero(); // As above.
4099 return; // It's over.
4100 }
4101 // else
4102
4103 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Async-receive handler for would-be protocol-negotiation "
4104 "in-message invoked; size received = [" << sz << "]. Negotiation passed. "
4105 "Will continue read chain (grab channel-header info, then do real work along this pipe).");
4106 rcv_async_read_channel_header(pipe);
4107} // Channel::rcv_on_async_read_proto_neg_msg()
4108
4109TEMPLATE_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL
4110template<typename Msg_in_pipe_t>
4111void CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::rcv_async_read_channel_header(Msg_in_pipe_t* pipe)
4112{
4113 constexpr auto LEAD_HNDL_EXPECTATION = Msg_in_pipe_t::S_LEAD_HNDL_EXPECTATION;
4114
4115 /* Negotiation passed; but we can't quite begin normal operation yet; must grab the opposing peer's
4116 * channel-header info. The code is very similar: read a single message expected to be a capnp-struct X,
4117 * where X is ChannelHeader this time. Though, as of this writing there's nothing to verify in it; it's just info
4118 * like the peer's process ID; so in that sense it is simpler. Anyway keeping comments light this time.
4119 * @todo Can we make this more compact via code reuse versus rcv_[on_]async_read_proto_neg_msg()?
4120 *
4121 * Really we would've placed the ProtocolNegotiation item as field @0 of ChannelHeader (and verified it before
4122 * touching anything past that); it's just that protocol v1 lacked any ChannelHeader, so now it's too late to
4123 * do it compatibly (probably... if we are reading https://capnproto.org/language.html rules on protocol-evolving
4124 * correctly... better safe than sorry). Perf impact should be negligible. */
4125
4126 Error_code sync_err_code;
4127 size_t sync_sz;
4128
4129 auto on_recv_func = [this, pipe](const Error_code& err_code, size_t sz) mutable
4130 {
4131 rcv_on_async_read_channel_header(pipe, err_code, sz);
4132 };
4133
4134 if constexpr(LEAD_HNDL_EXPECTATION == Tribool_vals::false_value)
4135 {
4136 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Async-read starting for channel-header message "
4137 "along blobs-only pipe.");
4138 m_channel.async_receive_blob(pipe->m_init_msg_blob.mutable_buffer(), &sync_err_code, &sync_sz,
4139 std::move(on_recv_func));
4140 }
4141 else
4142 {
4143 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Async-read starting for channel-header message "
4144 "along blobs-and-handles pipe.");
4145 m_channel.async_receive_native_handle(&pipe->m_init_msg_hndl, pipe->m_init_msg_blob.mutable_buffer(),
4146 &sync_err_code, &sync_sz, std::move(on_recv_func));
4147 }
4148
4149 if (sync_err_code != transport::error::Code::S_SYNC_IO_WOULD_BLOCK)
4150 {
4151 rcv_on_async_read_channel_header(pipe, sync_err_code, sync_sz);
4152 }
4153} // Channel::rcv_async_read_channel_header()
4154
4155TEMPLATE_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL
4156template<typename Msg_in_pipe_t>
4157void CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::rcv_on_async_read_channel_header(Msg_in_pipe_t* pipe, Error_code err_code, size_t sz)
4158{
4159 using util::Own_native_handle;
4160 using flow::util::Blob;
4161 using util::Process_credentials;
4162 using std::exception;
4163 auto& blob = pipe->m_init_msg_blob;
4164
4165 // Again keeping comments light; similar stuff to rcv_on_async_read_proto_neg_msg() (but simpler still).
4166
4167 Own_native_handle init_msg_hndl;
4168 if (!err_code)
4169 {
4170 init_msg_hndl.reset(std::move(pipe->m_init_msg_hndl));
4171 }
4172
4173 if (!handle_async_err_code(pipe, err_code, "rcv_on_async_read_channel_header()"))
4174 {
4175 blob.make_zero();
4176 return;
4177 }
4178 // else if (all good (including !err_code)):
4179
4180 /* @todo We ignore init_msg_hndl, other than ensuring no leak occurs. To be more defensive we'd check
4181 * it here and hose *this if not .get().null(), a-la rcv_on_async_read_proto_neg_msg(). It *is* optional: we
4182 * trust the opposing process is not malicious, and how defensive we are against potential bugs on the other
4183 * side is a judgment call; for example we do check this during the earlier ProtocolNegotiation phase; for
4184 * another example during the main phase (with the user-messages) we check for many protocol violations but
4185 * certainly not every single possible bad value. It'd be good here for consistency (and defensiveness obv)
4186 * anyway, but it's not high-priority (and would create another hosing-capable path to maintain).
4187 *
4188 * This would apply to both the `!m_peer_process_creds` and <the converse> paths below, not just the
4189 * former. I.e., the hypothetical presence of a non-.null() hndl along either pipe would be an error, even
4190 * though the contents of the 2nd ChannelHeader to arrive (if applicable) from a well-behaved peer are otherwise
4191 * redundant and ignored.
4192 *
4193 * A spiritually similar @todo, applicable to 2 nearby places, is below. So, basically, the overall to-do
4194 * is to add, to this helper, a defensive graceful *this-hosing code-path. */
4195
4196 if (m_peer_process_creds)
4197 {
4198 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Async-receive handler for would-be channel-header "
4199 "in-message invoked; size received = [" << sz << "]. However "
4200 "we got the info along the other pipe; assuming "
4201 "this is the same information; ignoring; will continue read chain "
4202 "(do real work along this pipe).");
4203 rcv_async_read(pipe); // (It'll blob.make_zero() itself.)
4204 return;
4205 }
4206 // else
4207
4208 try
4209 {
4210 Capped_sz_capnp_message_reader hdr_reader{blob.const_buffer()};
4211 const auto root = hdr_reader.getRoot<schema::detail::ChannelHeader>(); // Can throw.
4212 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Channel-header in-message contents:"
4213 "\n" << ostreamable_capnp_full(root));
4214
4215 if (!root.hasClaimedOwnProcessCredentials()) // See @todo below; applies here.
4216 {
4217 FLOW_LOG_FATAL("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Async-receive handler for would-be channel-header "
4218 "in-message invoked; size received = [" << sz << "]. Message lacks expected parts; "
4219 "protocol violation despite passing protocol-negotiation earlier; aborting. "
4220 "Message contents:\n" << ostreamable_capnp_full(root));
4221 assert(false && "Async-receive handler for would-be channel-header "
4222 "in-message invoked; message lacks expected parts; "
4223 "protocol violation despite passing protocol-negotiation earlier; aborting.");
4224 std::abort();
4225 }
4226 // else
4227
4228 auto claimed_proc_creds_root = root.getClaimedOwnProcessCredentials();
4229 m_peer_process_creds.emplace(claimed_proc_creds_root.getProcessId(),
4230 claimed_proc_creds_root.getUserId(),
4231 claimed_proc_creds_root.getGroupId());
4232 }
4233 catch (const exception& exc)
4234 {
4235 FLOW_LOG_FATAL("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Async-receive handler for would-be channel-header "
4236 "in-message invoked; size received = [" << sz << "]. Could not capnp-deserialize the "
4237 "contents; protocol violation despite passing protocol-negotiation earlier; aborting. "
4238 "Exception = [" << exc.what() << "].");
4239 assert(false && "Async-receive handler for would-be channel-header "
4240 "in-message invoked; could not capnp-deserialize the contents; "
4241 "protocol violation despite passing protocol-negotiation earlier; aborting.");
4242 std::abort();
4243 /* @todo Could emit civilized error instead (here + near above abort()); we do so in hairier situations later.
4244 * We don't have to do so either there or here, though; there we do so due to higher likelihood of bugs.
4245 * At this stage, it should really be fine, this close to protocol negotiation that just passed. */
4246 }
4247
4248 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Async-receive handler for channel-header "
4249 "in-message invoked; size received = [" << sz << "]. Got the info: "
4250 "peer-process credentials [" << *m_peer_process_creds << "]. "
4251 "Will continue read chain (do real work along this pipe).");
4252 rcv_async_read(pipe); // (It'll blob.make_zero() itself.)
4253} // Channel::rcv_on_async_read_channel_header()
4254
4255TEMPLATE_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL
4256void CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::rcv_struct_new_msg_in(Msg_in_ptr_uniq&& msg_in_moved)
4257{
4258 Msg_in_ptr_uniq msg_in{std::move(msg_in_moved)};
4259 // msg_in_moved is now nullified as promised. We own the Msg_in.
4260
4261 Msg_in_impl<Msg_in> msg_in_privileged{ *msg_in }; // Gain access to back-end API.
4262
4263 /* Pre-condition: msg_in is with-handle or sans-handle; and has all the serialization segments inside it that
4264 * the remote peer alleged are needed for deserialization to work; and msg_in.deserialize_mdt() has already
4265 * successfully executed. So let us attempt to deserialize the body -- if any.
4266 * Reminder: This does not involve copying or heavy-weight decoding operations, at its core: It initializes
4267 * a capnp-generated Reader class that simply reads bits out of those segments in RAM.
4268 *
4269 * That's the core thing. But the preceding .deserialize_mdt() call does perform checks on the basics, namely
4270 * everything that:
4271 * - doesn't require knowledge of other in-messages and out-messages; and
4272 * - doesn't require going *inside* .body_root() or .internal_msg_body_root() (whichever is applicable).
4273 *
4274 * Anyway, that's the rule of thumb, but in practice when we're checking some piece of data via
4275 * accessors after deserialize_*(), we must simply be aware whether a particular correctness has already been
4276 * ensured by deserialize_*(); if so great; if not either add it in there (if it fits the above rule of thumb)
4277 * or ensure it in `*this` code. */
4278
4279 /* ASAP let's make the famous session-token check that is required for all in-messages.
4280 * First refer to structured_msg.capnp StructuredMessage.AuthHeader.sessionToken and the mandated rules
4281 * for checking. They're important, so restating them here in our context:
4282 * - Each Channel is either LOGGED_IN from ction; or starts SRV_LOG_IN/CLI_LOG_IN and
4283 * enters LOGGED_IN once a very rigid log-in exchange occurs OK.
4284 * - When *_LOG_IN: only two messages are allowed in the world; call them LogInReq and LogInRsp
4285 * in this comment.
4286 * - SRV_LOG_IN:
4287 * - m_session_token is (randomly) generated locally and remains unchanged throughout `*this`;
4288 * - LogInReq is the only in-message allowed -- exactly 1 of them -- and its .sessionToken *must* be nil.
4289 * - CLI_LOG_IN:
4290 * - m_session_token is nil throughout this phase; it is changed to non-nil just before LOGGED_IN entry.
4291 * - LogInRsp is the only in-message allowed -- exactly 1 of them -- and its .sessionToken *must* not
4292 * be nil; but there is no *correct* value beyond that against which to check.
4293 * - When LOGGED_IN:
4294 * - m_session_token is non-nil and unchanged throughout this phase (until `*this` dies).
4295 * - Every in-message must have .sessionToken equal to m_session_token.
4296 *
4297 * Due to the way our state is set up, then, we can confidently perform the following check early and simply.
4298 * (E.g., we need not worry about sequence #s yet -- can check this right away.) */
4299 const auto& session_token = msg_in_privileged.session_token();
4300 if (m_phase == Phase::S_SRV_LOG_IN)
4301 {
4302 if (!session_token.is_nil())
4303 {
4304 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Log-in (as server): Deserialized new structured "
4305 "in-message which must be the log-in request, but the session token is not nil as "
4306 "required (is [" << session_token << "]). Other side misbehaved?");
4307 handle_new_error(error::Code::S_STRUCT_CHANNEL_INTERNAL_PROTOCOL_LOG_IN_MISUSED_SCHEMA,
4308 "rcv_struct_new_msg_in(2)");
4309 return;
4310 }
4311 // else: OK.
4312 }
4313 else if (m_phase == Phase::S_CLI_LOG_IN)
4314 {
4315 if (session_token.is_nil())
4316 {
4317 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Log-in (as client): Deserialized new structured "
4318 "in-message which must be the log-in response, but the session token is nil and "
4319 "not non-nil as required. Other side misbehaved?");
4320 handle_new_error(error::Code::S_STRUCT_CHANNEL_INTERNAL_PROTOCOL_LOG_IN_MISUSED_SCHEMA,
4321 "rcv_struct_new_msg_in(3)");
4322 return;
4323 }
4324 // else: OK.
4325 }
4326 else
4327 {
4328 assert(m_phase == Phase::S_LOGGED_IN);
4329 if (session_token != m_session_token)
4330 {
4331 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Deserialized new structured "
4332 "in-message, but its session token [" << session_token << "] does not match the "
4333 "established session token [" << m_session_token << "]; auth failed.");
4334 handle_new_error(error::Code::S_STRUCT_CHANNEL_INTERNAL_PROTOCOL_BAD_AUTH,
4335 "rcv_struct_new_msg_in(4)");
4336 return;
4337 }
4338 }
4339 // Got here: session_token is OK. On to ID/seq #.
4340
4341 const auto id = msg_in_privileged.id_or_none();
4342 const bool id_0 = id == 0;
4343
4344 if (id_0)
4345 {
4346 // Internal message. We'll deal with the various possibilities in here.
4347 rcv_struct_new_internal_msg_in(msg_in_privileged);
4348 return; // Note m_channel_err_code_or_ok may have just become truthy.
4349 }
4350 // else if (!id_0): User message!
4351
4352 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: About to deserialize (zero-copy) new structured in-message: "
4353 "optional user-message-body portion.");
4354 {
4355 /* Note this will update all relevant stats .m_rcv.m_msg.
4356 * If it is an internal message, that already occurred earlier during .deserialize_mdt().
4357 * Don't worry -- that guy's contract is specifically to only do that for internal messages/let
4358 * .deserialize_body() do it otherwise. */
4359 Error_code err_code;
4360 msg_in_privileged.deserialize_body(&err_code, &m_stats.m_rcv.m_msg);
4361 if (err_code)
4362 {
4363 handle_new_error(err_code, "rcv_struct_new_msg_in(1)");
4364 return;
4365 }
4366 // else
4367 }
4368
4369 // (W/r/t to the pretty-print -- see any comments near the somewhat-mirrored calls in send_*(). May apply here.)
4370 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Deserialized user message [" << msg_in_privileged.m_base << "].");
4371 FLOW_LOG_DATA("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: The complete user message: "
4372 "\n" << ostreamable_capnp_full(msg_in_privileged.m_base.body_root()));
4373
4374 /* Let's recap. (All the background info necessary is in the various data member doc headers and possibly class
4375 * doc header; here we orient ourselves within that body of knowledge.) We have a valid (in and of itself, maybe
4376 * not relative to other messages) in-message bearing a user message body. So it's in the structured layer
4377 * for the 1st time. Where to emit it now? Ultimately the layers are (goal being to move down this list ASAP):
4378 * - Just entered structured layer <- we are here. We will immediately move it to one of these:
4379 * - Reassembly queue m_rcv_reassembly_q.
4380 * - Moves in to this layer if: the message's ID (seq #) is not the next one expected.
4381 * - Moves down from this layer when: subsequent in-message(s) bridge(s) the gap to the message's ID (seq #).
4382 * - Skips this layer if: the message's ID (seq #) *is* the next one expected.
4383 * - Note: This is *always* the case unless Owned_channel::S_HAS_2_PIPES. Otherwise a skipped seq # =
4384 * protocol error.
4385 * - Side effect: if that also fills the gap to the lowest-seq-# in m_rcv_reassembly_q, then
4386 * feed 1+ in-messages in m_rcv_reassembly_q to the next layers.
4387 * - Unregistered-Msg_which in-message store m_rcv_pending_msgs.
4388 * - Moves in to this layer if: *both* hold:
4389 * - the message is not a response (originating_msg_id_or_none() == 0); and
4390 * - neither expect_msg() or expect_msgs() has been registered to wait for its body_root().which() yet.
4391 * - Moves down from this layer if: expect_msg() or expect_msgs() registers a handler for body_root().which().
4392 * - Skips this layer if: the message is a response; or it's not, and its body_root().which() has a registered
4393 * handler from a prior expect_msg() or expect_msgs().
4394 * - ONE OF:
4395 * - Response handler F in m_rcv_expecting_response_map is called F(msg_in) and (if one-off) then removed
4396 * from said map.
4397 * - Moves in to this layer if: the message is a response (originating_msg_id_or_none() != 0).
4398 * - m_rcv_expecting_response_map[<that ID>] must exist.
4399 * - If it doesn't, then it's an error at the user's protocol level and reported as such
4400 * (set_unexpected_response_handler()).
4401 * - Msg_which-handler F in m_rcv_expecting_msg_map is called F(msg_in) and (if one-off) then removed
4402 * from said map.
4403 * - Moves in to this layer if: the message is not a response (originating_msg_id_or_none() == 0).
4404 * See above.
4405 *
4406 * So let's get to it: Deal with the message ID (seq #). */
4407 if (id != m_rcv_msg_next_id)
4408 {
4409 if (id < m_rcv_msg_next_id)
4410 {
4411 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Deserialized new structured in-message, but its ID "
4412 "[" << id << "] is duplicate: next expected ID [" << m_rcv_msg_next_id << "] exceeds it. "
4413 "Other side misbehaved?");
4414 handle_new_error(error::Code::S_STRUCT_CHANNEL_INTERNAL_PROTOCOL_MISUSED_SCHEMA,
4415 "rcv_struct_new_msg_in(5)");
4416 return;
4417 }
4418 // else
4419
4420 if constexpr(!Owned_channel::S_HAS_2_PIPES) // C++17: #if-like compile-time check.
4421 {
4422 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Deserialized new structured in-message, but its ID "
4423 "[" << id << "] is not sequential to next expected ID [" << m_rcv_msg_next_id << "], even "
4424 "though the channel has only 1 in-pipe. Other side misbehaved?");
4425 handle_new_error(error::Code::S_STRUCT_CHANNEL_INTERNAL_PROTOCOL_MISUSED_SCHEMA,
4426 "rcv_struct_new_msg_in(6)");
4427 return;
4428 }
4429 else // if constexpr(Owned_channel::S_HAS_2_PIPES) // Note: it's like #else; so shouldn't just omit it after return.
4430 {
4431 if (m_phase != Phase::S_LOGGED_IN)
4432 {
4433 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Deserialized new structured in-message, but its ID "
4434 "[" << id << "] is not sequential to next expected ID [" << m_rcv_msg_next_id << "] -- and "
4435 "we are in a log-in phase (during which only the log-in request or response, with seq#=1, "
4436 "is allowed). Other side misbehaved?");
4437 handle_new_error(error::Code::S_STRUCT_CHANNEL_INTERNAL_PROTOCOL_MISUSED_SCHEMA,
4438 "rcv_struct_new_msg_in(7)");
4439 return;
4440 }
4441 // else
4442
4443 const auto insert_result = m_rcv_reassembly_q->emplace(id, std::move(msg_in));
4444 if (!insert_result.second)
4445 {
4446 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Deserialized new structured in-message, but its ID "
4447 "[" << id << "] is not sequential to next expected ID [" << m_rcv_msg_next_id << "] -- and "
4448 "the reassembly queue already has an in-message with that ID. So it's a duplicate ID. "
4449 "Other side misbehaved?");
4450 handle_new_error(error::Code::S_STRUCT_CHANNEL_INTERNAL_PROTOCOL_MISUSED_SCHEMA,
4451 "rcv_struct_new_msg_in(8)");
4452 return;
4453 }
4454 // else: inserted OK. msg_in is now null.
4455
4456 const auto q_sz = m_rcv_reassembly_q->size();
4457
4458 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Deserialized new structured in-message, but its ID "
4459 "[" << id << "] is not sequential to next expected ID [" << m_rcv_msg_next_id << "]; "
4460 "inserted it into the reassembly queue which now has size "
4461 "[" << q_sz << "].");
4462
4463 // Stats: reassembly queue insertion + depth gauge + depth high-water mark.
4464 {
4465 ++m_stats.m_rcv.m_reassembly_q_insertions;
4466 m_stats.m_rcv.m_reassembly_q_depth = q_sz;
4467 flow::util::stat::update_hi_wmark(&m_stats.m_rcv.m_reassembly_q_hi_wmark, q_sz);
4468 }
4469
4470 return; // That's it for now. Await the seq # gap to be filled by future in-message(s).
4471 } // else if constexpr(Owned_channel::S_HAS_2_PIPES)
4472 assert(false && "Either invalid in-message, or it should've been inserted into reassembly queue + returned.");
4473 } // if (id != m_rcv_msg_next_id)
4474 // else if (id == m_rcv_msg_next_id):
4475
4476 // Corner case possibility for IDs >= 2, during non-LOGGED_IN:
4477 if ((m_rcv_msg_next_id > 1) && (m_phase != Phase::S_LOGGED_IN))
4478 {
4479 assert((m_phase == Phase::S_SRV_LOG_IN)
4480 && "Phase is CLI_LOG_IN with seq#>=2, but seq#=1 in-message should have immediately moved to "
4481 "LOGGED_IN or hosed channel... bug?");
4482
4483 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Deserialized new structured in-message, and its ID "
4484 "[" << id << "] is sequential to next expected ID [" << m_rcv_msg_next_id << "] -- but "
4485 "we are in SRV_LOG_IN phase, during which we are to receive at most 1 in-message. "
4486 "Other side misbehaved?");
4487 handle_new_error(error::Code::S_STRUCT_CHANNEL_INTERNAL_PROTOCOL_MISUSED_SCHEMA,
4488 "rcv_struct_new_msg_in(9)");
4489 return;
4490 }
4491 // else
4492
4493 ++m_rcv_msg_next_id;
4494
4495 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Deserialized new structured in-message, and its ID "
4496 "[" << id << "] is sequential to next expected ID which has now been incremented to that value. "
4497 "Handling in-order in-message now.");
4498
4499 /* We have a good, in-order message. When logged-in: we should indeed handle the bottom 2 layers (see summary above)
4500 * as written. But during log-in we have to handle that specific, somewhat rigid message exchange.
4501 * It is easier to follow if we just handle that in a separate method (where we can assume many simplifications
4502 * -- e.g., no reassembly queue to deal with) instead of interspersing the general (logged-in) code path with
4503 * confusing if()finess that handles the somewhat-special log-in messages. So: */
4504 switch (m_phase)
4505 {
4506 case Phase::S_CLI_LOG_IN:
4507 rcv_struct_new_msg_in_during_log_in_as_cli(std::move(msg_in)); return; // m_channel_err_code_or_ok may be truthy.
4508 case Phase::S_SRV_LOG_IN:
4509 rcv_struct_new_msg_in_during_log_in_as_srv(std::move(msg_in)); return; // Ditto.
4510 case Phase::S_LOGGED_IN:
4511 // Fall through:
4512 break;
4513 } // Compiler should warn if we missed an enum value.
4514
4515 // Yay, this is the mainstream (logged-in) case.
4516
4517 // This handles the next layers (see summary above) for a given in-order message.
4518 rcv_struct_new_msg_in_is_next_expected(std::move(msg_in));
4519 if (m_channel_err_code_or_ok)
4520 {
4521 return;
4522 }
4523 // else
4524
4525 // As noted in the summary we may have bridged gap to m_rcv_reassembly_q.begin() seq #. Let's handle those too.
4526 if constexpr(Owned_channel::S_HAS_2_PIPES)
4527 {
4528 typename Reassembly_q::iterator first_reassembly_q_it;
4529 while ((!m_rcv_reassembly_q->empty())
4530 && (first_reassembly_q_it = m_rcv_reassembly_q->begin())->first == m_rcv_msg_next_id)
4531 {
4532 Msg_in_ptr_uniq msg_in{std::move(first_reassembly_q_it->second)};
4533 m_rcv_reassembly_q->erase(first_reassembly_q_it);
4534
4535 ++m_rcv_msg_next_id;
4536 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: ID (sequence #) gap bridged to "
4537 "[" << m_rcv_msg_next_id << "]. Handling in-order in-message now.");
4538
4539 // As above for the new message:
4540 rcv_struct_new_msg_in_is_next_expected(std::move(msg_in));
4541 if (m_channel_err_code_or_ok)
4542 {
4543 return;
4544 }
4545 // else: continue.
4546 } // while ((!m_rcv_reassembly_q->empty()) && (m_rcv_reassembly_q lowest seq # == m_rcv_msg_next_id))
4547
4548 // Stats (if no -- catastrophic, as opposed to normal channel-hosing -- error):
4549 m_stats.m_rcv.m_reassembly_q_depth = m_rcv_reassembly_q->size();
4550 } // if constexpr(Owned_channel::S_HAS_2_PIPES)
4551} // Channel::rcv_struct_new_msg_in()

4553TEMPLATE_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL
4554void CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::rcv_struct_new_internal_msg_in(const Msg_in_impl<Msg_in>& msg_in_privileged)
4555{
4556 using std::string;
4557
4558 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Deserialized new structured in-message: it is an internal "
4559 "message, meaning it does not carry a user-generated body.");
4560 const auto& root = msg_in_privileged.internal_msg_body_root();
4561
4562 /* Maintenance note: When InternalMessageBody becomes a union -- adds more message types --
4563 * replace the following with `switch (root.which())`. For now though there's only one possibility: */
4564
4565 if (!root.hasUnexpectedResponse())
4566 {
4567 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Deserialized new structured in-message: it is an internal "
4568 "message, but its type is unknown: currently only `unexpectedResponse` is supported. "
4569 "This should not be possible under proper remote peer behavior, as we maintain a strict "
4570 "protocol version/capability system. Other side misbehaved?");
4571 handle_new_error(error::Code::S_STRUCT_CHANNEL_INTERNAL_PROTOCOL_INTERNAL_MSG_TYPE_UNKNOWN,
4572 "rcv_struct_new_internal_msg_in(1)");
4573 return;
4574 }
4575 // else
4576
4577 const auto originating_msg_id = msg_in_privileged.originating_msg_id_or_none();
4578 const auto rsp_root = root.getUnexpectedResponse();
4579 string mdt_text = rsp_root.getOriginatingMessageMetadataText();
4580 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("Unexpected-response message regarding earlier out-message with ID [" << originating_msg_id << "]; "
4581 "metadata text = [" << mdt_text << "]; will inform user via special handler if registered.");
4582
4583 if (originating_msg_id == 0)
4584 {
4585 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Deserialized new structured in-message: it is an internal "
4586 "message indicating unexpected response out-message, but the ID of that out-message is 0 which "
4587 "is a violation of our internal protocol. Other side misbehaved?");
4588 handle_new_error(error::Code::S_STRUCT_CHANNEL_INTERNAL_PROTOCOL_MISUSED_SCHEMA,
4589 "rcv_struct_new_internal_msg_in(2)");
4590 return;
4591 }
4592 // else
4593
4594 handlers_post<typename Handlers::Remote_unexpected_response>("rcv_struct_new_internal_msg_in()",
4595 originating_msg_id, std::move(mdt_text));
4596 // See Remote_unexpected_response::execute() for body. --^
4597} // Channel::rcv_struct_new_internal_msg_in()
