4599TEMPLATE_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL
4600void CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::rcv_struct_new_msg_in_during_log_in_as_cli(Msg_in_ptr_uniq&& msg_in_moved)
4601{
4602 Msg_in_ptr_uniq msg_in{std::move(msg_in_moved)};
4603 // msg_in_moved is now nullified as promised. We own the Msg_in.
4604
4605 Msg_in_impl<Msg_in> msg_in_privileged{ *msg_in }; // Gain access to back-end API.
4606
4607 /* We are the logging-in client (CLI_LOG_IN). During this phase the only message we can receive is
4608 * a single log-in response to the log-in request we'd earlier sent. So now we shall ascertain that is
4609 * what is happening. Namely:
4610 * - m_rcv_expecting_response_map must have exactly 1 registered-for-response message (the log-in).
4611 * - How this can break:
4612 * - If they hadn't (successfully, meaning with an on-response handler provided) send()t the log-in request.
4613 * - If they hadn't even constructed the latter at all.
4614 * - msg_in is a response, and it indeed indicates the log-in out-message (by necessity having msg_id_out_t = 1)
4615 * is the originating message to which it is a response.
4616 * - It has a non-nil session-token... which, by the way, we save onto our currently-nil m_session_token!
4617 * Oh and m_phase shall go to LOGGED_IN foreva!
4618 * - How these can break: By the other side misbehaving.
4619 * - Note: We could assert() a bunch of other things (@todo maybe we should), but I'm (ygoldfel) fairly
4620 * confident we wouldn't have allowed any other ways of breaking this; that's why we prohibit general
4621 * expect_msg(), etc., etc., until logged-in phase.
4622 *
4623 * Let's go.... */
4624
4625 if (m_rcv_expecting_response_map.size() != 1)
4626 {
4627 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Log-in: Would-be log-in response message "
4628 "received outside the situation where we'd sent the log-in request and are awaiting response; "
4629 "the await-rsp map should have 1 element but instead has "
4630 "[" << m_rcv_expecting_response_map.size() << "]. Other side misbehaved?");
4631 handle_new_error(error::Code::S_STRUCT_CHANNEL_INTERNAL_PROTOCOL_LOG_IN_MISUSED_SCHEMA,
4632 "rcv_struct_new_msg_in_during_log_in_as_cli(1)");
4633 return;
4634 }
4635 // else
4636
4637 assert(flow::util::key_exists(m_rcv_expecting_response_map, 1)
4638 && "During CLI_LOG_IN the message expecting response must be the log-in request, with ID 1.");
4639
4640 if (msg_in_privileged.originating_msg_id_or_none() != 1)
4641 {
4642 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Log-in: Would-be log-in response message "
4643 "received as expected -- except it does not specify originating message ID=1 as required "
4644 "in this specific situation; it specifies "
4645 "[" << msg_in_privileged.originating_msg_id_or_none() << "]. Other side misbehaved?");
4646 handle_new_error(error::Code::S_STRUCT_CHANNEL_INTERNAL_PROTOCOL_LOG_IN_MISUSED_SCHEMA,
4647 "rcv_struct_new_msg_in_during_log_in_as_cli(2)");
4648 return;
4649 }
4650 // else
4651
4652 assert(m_session_token.is_nil() && "While CLI_LOG_IN our saved session_token must be nil.");
4653 m_session_token = msg_in_privileged.session_token();
4654 if (m_session_token.is_nil())
4655 {
4656 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Log-in: Would-be log-in response message "
4657 "received as expected and is a response to the log-in request; but it lacks a non-nil "
4658 "session-token! Cannot complete log-in. Other side misbehaved?");
4659 handle_new_error(error::Code::S_STRUCT_CHANNEL_INTERNAL_PROTOCOL_LOG_IN_MISUSED_SCHEMA,
4660 "rcv_struct_new_msg_in_during_log_in_as_cli(3)");
4661 return;
4662 }
4663 // else if (we've updated m_session_token to its foreva-value):
4664
4665 FLOW_LOG_INFO("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Log-in: Would-be log-in response message "
4666 "received as expected and is a response to the log-in request; session token "
4667 "[" << m_session_token << "] saved; entering LOGGED_IN phase.");
4668 m_phase = Phase::S_LOGGED_IN;
4669
4670 /* Awesome! So now we can just use the general code path, same as what the logged-in case invokes for the
4671 * new in-order message (individually -- it doesn't worry about then scanning the reassembly queue).
4672 * It will do some slight re-computations like the above is-it-a-response check, but that's fine; they're
4673 * quick and easy, and it's worth it for the simpler code.
4674 *
4675 * We just needed to check that and save the session-token and update m_phase; now everything is normal
4676 * forever (in the shiny new LOGGED_IN phase). */
4677 rcv_struct_new_msg_in_is_next_expected(std::move(msg_in));
4678 // m_channel_err_code_or_ok may have just become truthy.
4679} // Channel::rcv_struct_new_msg_in_during_log_in_as_cli()
4680
4681TEMPLATE_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL
4682void CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::rcv_struct_new_msg_in_during_log_in_as_srv(Msg_in_ptr_uniq&& msg_in_moved)
4683{
4684 Msg_in_ptr_uniq msg_in{std::move(msg_in_moved)};
4685 // msg_in_moved is now nullified as promised. We own the Msg_in.
4686
4687 const auto which = msg_in->body_root().which();
4688 Msg_in_impl<Msg_in> msg_in_privileged{ *msg_in }; // Gain access to back-end API.
4689
4690 /* We are the logged-in-to server (SRV_LOG_IN). During this phase the only message we can receive is
4691 * a single log-in request which either is expected due to expect_log_in_request() -- or isn't, but then
4692 * they can call it later (and if so they'll only be allowed to call it with the Which received here --
4693 * or it's a protocol error... but that's not our problem here). So now we shall ascertain that is what is
4694 * happening. Namely:
4695 * - msg_in isn't a response to anything (is unsolicited: notification or request).
4696 * Subtlety: It can't be a response to anything anyway: in SRV_LOG_IN we cannot send
4697 * anything except the log-in response (which cannot happen until we process the present log-in,
4698 * by advertised contract of expect_log_in_request()), so there's nothing to which to respond, and this would
4699 * be detected in regular rcv_struct_new_msg_in_is_next_expected() we'd call below.
4700 * However, receiving an unexpected response
4701 * is not (unlike most mismatches) considered a pipe-hosing error but instead a user error normally
4702 * reported via set_unexpected_response_handler() (etc.) -- which they can treat how they want.
4703 * In this case, during log-in, we want to be totally rigid and just outlaw the whole situation totally.
4704 * - How this can break: Remote peer could send a response. Actually this wouldn't be easy: there's no
4705 * API that'll work for it in the CLI_LOG_IN phase... but who knows what code they have; we err on the
4706 * side of <whatever>.
4707 * - m_rcv_expecting_msg_map has either 0 or 1 registered expectation.
4708 * - If the latter: its Msg_which_in must equal the one in msg_in (in-message received here).
4709 * - How this can break: If they called expect_log_in_request() but with a different `which` than
4710 * delivered here. Could be local user error; remote user error; or both.
4711 * - If the former: this one will be cached to match up to a future expect_log_in_request() message... but
4712 * it must be the only one thus cached (only one log-in request is allowed).
4713 * - How this can break: Remote peer could send a request 2x. Actually this wouldn't be easy: there's no
4714 * API that'll work for it in the CLI_LOG_IN phase... but who knows what code they have; we err on the
4715 * side of <whatever>.
4716 * - Note: We could assert() a bunch of other things (some, we do; @todo maybe we should do more),
4717 * but I'm (ygoldfel) fairly confident we wouldn't have allowed any other ways of breaking this; that's why
4718 * we prohibit general expect_msg(), etc., etc., until logged-in phase.
4719 *
4720 * Let's go.... */
4721
4722 assert(m_rcv_expecting_response_map.empty() && "Only a single expect_log_in_request() allowed in SRV_LOG_IN phase.");
4723 if (msg_in_privileged.originating_msg_id_or_none() != 0)
4724 {
4725 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Log-in: Would-be log-in request message "
4726 "received -- except it's a response to something; this is illegal. Other side misbehaved?");
4727 handle_new_error(error::Code::S_STRUCT_CHANNEL_INTERNAL_PROTOCOL_LOG_IN_MISUSED_SCHEMA,
4728 "rcv_struct_new_msg_in_during_log_in_as_srv(4)");
4729 return;
4730 }
4731 // else if (it's not a response; is unsolicited): OK, perform the other checks above.
4732
4733 if (m_rcv_expecting_msg_map.size() == 1)
4734 {
4735 const auto exp_which = m_rcv_expecting_msg_map.begin()->first;
4736 if (exp_which != which)
4737 {
4738 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Log-in: Would-be log-in request message "
4739 "received as expected -- except it does not specify union-which = [" << int(exp_which) << "] "
4740 "as specified by earlier local expect_log_in_request() call but rather "
4741 "[" << int(which) << "]. This might be a protocol error on the user's part on this "
4742 "or other side or both.");
4743 /* Subtlety: Normally we'd emit S_STRUCT_CHANNEL_INTERNAL_PROTOCOL_LOG_IN_MISUSED_SCHEMA; but that's for
4744 * internal errors -- in this case the error can/is the user's by saying they expect X locally but sending
4745 * Y remotely; both X and Y are user decisions. So it's not an internal error. */
4746 handle_new_error(error::Code::S_STRUCT_CHANNEL_GOT_UNEXPECTED_LOG_IN_REQUEST,
4747 "rcv_struct_new_msg_in_during_log_in_as_srv(5)");
4748 return;
4749 }
4750 // else
4751
4752 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Log-in: Would-be log-in request message "
4753 "received as expected -- and it specifies union-which = [" << int(exp_which) << "] "
4754 "as specified by earlier local expect_log_in_request() call.");
4755 } // if (m_rcv_expecting_msg_map.size() == 1)
4756 else // if (m_rcv_expecting_msg_map.size() == 0, or >= 2)
4757 {
4758 assert(m_rcv_expecting_msg_map.empty() && "Only a single expect_log_in_request() allowed in SRV_LOG_IN phase.");
4759
4760 if (!m_rcv_pending_msgs.empty())
4761 {
4762 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Log-in: Would-be log-in request message "
4763 "received as expected -- but no expect_log_in_request() registered yet. Would await that "
4764 "and ensure its union-which matches -- except apparently such a would-be log-in request "
4765 "has already been received and cached; this is not allowed. Other side misbehaved?");
4766 handle_new_error(error::Code::S_STRUCT_CHANNEL_INTERNAL_PROTOCOL_LOG_IN_MISUSED_SCHEMA,
4767 "rcv_struct_new_msg_in_during_log_in_as_srv(6)");
4768 return;
4769 }
4770 // else
4771
4772 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Log-in: Would-be log-in request message "
4773 "received as expected -- but no expect_log_in_request() registered yet. Will await that "
4774 "and ensure its union-which matches.");
4775 } // else if (m_rcv_expecting_msg_map.size() == 0)
4776
4777 /* Awesome! So now we can just use the general code path, same as what the logged-in case invokes for the
4778 * new in-order message (individually -- it doesn't worry about then scanning the reassembly queue).
4779 * It will do some slight re-computations like the above is-it-a-response check, but that's fine; they're
4780 * quick and easy, and it's worth it for the simpler code.
4781 *
4782 * We just needed to check the above. Though, note, we're still not in LOGGED_IN phase; that will occur
4783 * only once they send() their response to this log-in request. */
4784 rcv_struct_new_msg_in_is_next_expected(std::move(msg_in));
4785 // m_channel_err_code_or_ok may have just become truthy.
4786} // Channel::rcv_struct_new_msg_in_during_log_in_as_srv()
4787
4788TEMPLATE_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL
4789void CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::rcv_struct_new_msg_in_is_next_expected(Msg_in_ptr_uniq&& msg_in_moved)
4790{
4791 using flow::util::stat::Histogram_counter;
4792 using flow::Fine_clock;
4793 using boost::promise;
4794 using boost::chrono::round;
4795 using boost::chrono::microseconds;
4796
4797 Msg_in_ptr_uniq msg_in{std::move(msg_in_moved)};
4798 // msg_in_moved is now nullified as promised. We own the Msg_in.
4799
4800 Msg_in_impl<Msg_in> msg_in_privileged{ *msg_in }; // Gain access to back-end API.
4801
4802 const auto id = msg_in_privileged.id_or_none();
4803 assert(id != 0);
4804
4805 /* Refer to the summary comment (regarding layers of handling structured in-messages) in our caller.
4806 * We are handling the last 2 layers mentioned there in this method.
4807 *
4808 * So either it's a response or unsolicited. */
4809 const auto originating_msg_id = msg_in_privileged.originating_msg_id_or_none();
4810 if (originating_msg_id != 0)
4811 {
4812 // It's a response.
4813 const auto exp_rsp_it = m_rcv_expecting_response_map.find(originating_msg_id);
4814 if (exp_rsp_it == m_rcv_expecting_response_map.end())
4815 {
4816 /* It's a response to something that doesn't exist or didn't express it desired a response.
4817 * See rationale for how we handle it in m_rcv_pending_msgs doc header. So do that: namely,
4818 * - send an internal-message (out-of-band, meaning seq #s are irrelevant -- message ID 0)
4819 * informing remote peer;
4820 * - emit offending msg_in to special handler (if registered) and forget it. */
4821 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Structured in-message ID "
4822 "[" << id << "] is itself in-order but is a response to "
4823 "alleged out-message ID [" << originating_msg_id << "] which either never existed or "
4824 "is not registered as awaiting a response. This is an error on the user's part and thus "
4825 "not fatal. Will send this as an internal-message to remote peer; and will fire "
4826 "registered on-unexpected-rsp handler (if any) locally.");
4827
4828 ++m_stats.m_rcv.m_unexpected_responses;
4829
4830 rcv_struct_inform_of_unexpected_response(std::move(msg_in));
4831 assert((!m_channel_err_code_or_ok) && "That guy is best-effort and should not be hosing channel.");
4832 return;
4833 } // if (exp_rsp_it not found)
4834 // else if (exp_rsp_it found)
4835
4836 const Expecting_response& exp_rsp = *exp_rsp_it->second;
4837 const bool one_off = exp_rsp.m_one_expected; // Delete exp_rsp_it below if true (single response expected).
4838 auto on_msg_func = exp_rsp.m_on_msg_func;
4839 assert(!on_msg_func->empty());
4840
4841 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Structured in-message ID "
4842 "[" << id << "] is itself in-order and is a response to "
4843 "out-message ID [" << originating_msg_id << "] which is expecting the response "
4844 "(one-off? = [" << one_off << "]). "
4845 "Will delete expectation if one-off; post handler.");
4846
4847 if (one_off)
4848 {
4849 // One-off request RTT histogram (microseconds).
4850 const auto rtt_usec
4851 = round<microseconds>(Fine_clock::now() - exp_rsp.m_sent_when).count();
4852 m_stats.m_rcv.m_histo_one_off_request_rtt_usec.record_value
4853 (static_cast<Histogram_counter::value_t>(rtt_usec));
4854
4855 --m_stats.m_rcv.m_expect_response_one_off_active;
4856 m_rcv_expecting_response_map.erase(exp_rsp_it);
4857 }
4858
4859 handlers_post<typename Handlers::Message>("rcv_struct_new_msg_in_is_next_expected(on-rsp)",
4860 std::move(msg_in), std::move(on_msg_func));
4861 // See Message::execute() for body.
4862 return;
4863 } // if (originating_msg_id != 0) (is response)
4864 // else if (originating_msg_id == 0) (is unsolicited)
4865
4866 /* Refer once again to the summary comment in calling method. Unsolicited message may need to be cached -- or not.
4867 * (That's unlike responses: Either something was expecting it; or not and it's an error.) */
4868
4869 const Msg_which_in which = msg_in->body_root().which();
4870 const auto exp_msg_it = m_rcv_expecting_msg_map.find(which);
4871 if (exp_msg_it == m_rcv_expecting_msg_map.end())
4872 {
4873 auto& q = m_rcv_pending_msgs[which]; // Create queue if needed.
4874 q.emplace(std::move(msg_in)); // Move the unique_ptr into cached queue.
4875 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Structured in-message ID "
4876 "[" << id << "] is itself in-order and unsolicited; currently no handler is registered "
4877 "for its union-which = [" << int(which) << "]; cached into per-union-which queue now sized "
4878 "[" << q.size() << "].");
4879
4880 // Stats.
4881 {
4882 auto& rcv = m_stats.m_rcv;
4883 ++rcv.m_unsolicited_msgs_cached;
4884 ++rcv.m_pending_msgs_depth;
4885 flow::util::stat::update_hi_wmark(&rcv.m_pending_msgs_hi_wmark, rcv.m_pending_msgs_depth);
4886 }
4887 return;
4888 }
4889 // else if (exp_msg_it exists)
4890
4891 // This is much like the response handling above.
4892
4893 const Expecting_msg& exp_msg = *exp_msg_it->second;
4894 const bool one_off = exp_msg.m_one_expected; // Delete exp_msg_it below if true (single response expected).
4895 auto on_msg_func = exp_msg.m_on_msg_func;
4896 assert(!on_msg_func->empty());
4897
4898 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Structured in-message ID "
4899 "[" << id << "] is itself in-order and unsolicited; currently expecting its "
4900 "union-which = [" << int(which) << "] (one-off? = [" << one_off << "]). "
4901 "Will fire handler and delete expectation if one-off.");
4902
4903 if (one_off)
4904 {
4905 m_rcv_expecting_msg_map.erase(exp_msg_it);
4906
4907 --m_stats.m_rcv.m_expect_msg_active; // Attn: Stats (also just below).
4908 }
4909 ++m_stats.m_rcv.m_unsolicited_msgs_routed;
4910
4911 handlers_post<typename Handlers::Message>("rcv_struct_new_msg_in_is_next_expected(on-msg)",
4912 std::move(msg_in), std::move(on_msg_func));
4913 // See Message::execute() for body.
4914} // Channel::rcv_struct_new_msg_in_is_next_expected()
4915
4916TEMPLATE_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL
4917void CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::rcv_struct_inform_of_unexpected_response(Msg_in_ptr_uniq&& msg_in)
4918{
4919 using schema::detail::StructuredMessage;
4920 using util::Blob_mutable;
4921 using util::Blob_const;
4922 using flow::error::Runtime_error;
4923 using flow::util::ostream_op_string;
4924 using flow::util::ceil_div;
4925 using boost::array;
4926 using Word = ::capnp::word;
4927
4928 /* This constant (call it N temporarily) needs to be enough to store the mdt header below. This topic bears
4929 * discussing, as there are some subtleties.
4930 * - Perf-wise: We assume we are not called often; so perf of this actual function is not too important;
4931 * basically as long as N is not too big for the stack (where we allocate this space below), it's fine.
4932 * - Once we serialize the internal-message-containing StructuredMessage, we'll only send_core()
4933 * the actual used-for-serialization (as determined by capnp) leading area, not all N bytes. Hence
4934 * N can't be too big in the sense of, "is it wasteful to send probably-lots of wasted bytes in every
4935 * internal message?".
4936 * - Receiver (Msg_in) will deserialize from byte 0 of what we send_core() here; it does not reject
4937 * the (lead message) blob for being too big or anything. Then since it's an internal message, there's
4938 * nothing else to consider; there's no user message segment(s) after, etc.
4939 * - So, all we need is N that comfortably exceeds any potential stuff we will try to serialize into it
4940 * below. Now to consider what's in there:
4941 * - There's the load_mdt() stuff: message ID zero, session token, and so on.
4942 * Basically it is similar (shared StructuredMessage schema) to what a user-message header would
4943 * hold. A user-message header is limited to BUILDER_CONFIG_FRAME_PREFIX_SZ_VIA_STRUC_CHANNEL bytes.
4944 * - There's the internal message payload itself; that's the part we must carefully contemplate.
4945 * In this function (as of this writing the only internal message type) it's an UnexpectedResponse
4946 * struct which contains originatingMessageMetadataText which is a pretty-print of msg_in's
4947 * own (user-message) mdt-header. Again, that guy is limited to
4948 * BUILDER_CONFIG_FRAME_PREFIX_SZ_VIA_STRUC_CHANNEL bytes in binary form; the pretty-print will not
4949 * be as compact.
4950 * - So, in sum, suppose we take N = BUILDER_CONFIG_FRAME_PREFIX_SZ_VIA_STRUC_CHANNEL * 32;
4951 * this includes our own metadata itself plus the pretty-print, wherein the latter is the main thing,
4952 * and we provide enough space for ~30x wastefulness of pretty-print versus the binary form it describes.
4953 * - As of this writing, BUILDER_CONFIG_FRAME_PREFIX_SZ_VIA_STRUC_CHANNEL=128, so N=4Ki. That's reasonable
4954 * for ~all IPC forms.
4955 *
4956 * The above relies (stack size aside) on certain estimates which really should all bear out, but
4957 * let's plan contingencies for that failing after all. Note, here, that if send_core() -- the actual send --
4958 * fails below (say due to transmission problem), we do *not* hose() *this or emit any error to our user;
4959 * any hosedness is detected by procedures that aren't a best-effort action, which is what this function is
4960 * doing (we'll do what we can, but if it fails, we move on). So then:
4961 * - Limitation 1: The generous margin for N was not enough for serializing the pretty-print. Result: when we
4962 * try to load that, serializer fails (throws exception). Handling: we catch it; log; move on without
4963 * sending.
4964 * - Limitation 2: The (sized N or less) serialization we try to send_core() is too big for IPC after all. Result:
4965 * send_core() emits some error.
4966 * Handling: as noted: we ignore it and accept that our best effort failed.
4967 * - In point of fact: as required by Native_handle/Blob_sender::send_*() concept: "some error" will
4968 * be INVALID_ARGUMENT, and it must not even hose the underlying channel (or *this) (rationale: it is
4969 * basically user error). Life goes on; even subsequent user send()s (et al) would not
4970 * be borked by our adventures here.
4971 * - Details omitted but briefly: even if it emitted a send-pipe-hosing error, counter to the concept as of
4972 * this writing, still our (lack of) reaction would basically result in acceptable behavior, now and after.
4973 * @todo Pre-check against send_*blob_max_size() to avoid having to rely on any of that for any reasoning,
4974 * essentially making this corner of struc::*Channel more independent and therefore maintainable.
4975 * Low-priority but would reduce this text wall's length. */
4976 constexpr size_t INTERNAL_MSG_MAX_SZ = BUILDER_CONFIG_FRAME_PREFIX_SZ_VIA_STRUC_CHANNEL * 32;
4977
4978 assert((m_phase == Phase::S_LOGGED_IN)
4979 && "We do not mess with internal messages until log-in has finished. Bug?");
4980 assert((!m_channel_err_code_or_ok)
4981 && "Reached only from the receive path, which stops on hosing; and nothing below can hose.");
4982
4983 /* There are 2 actions below: send_core() an internal message about the unexpected response, for the other
4984 * side's benefit (it can fire its on-*remote*-unexpected-response handler if applicable); and -- separately --
4985 * fire our on-*local*-unexpected-response handler. The latter definitely should be handlers_post()ed to
4986 * avoid recursive mayhem as usual. Should the send_core() action also be handlers_post()ed, or could we just
4987 * do it synchronously? Back when Channel was async-I/O all the way (before sync_io pattern existed)
4988 * I had post()ed it onto thread W which at the time was used exclusively for firing user handlers; the idea
4989 * was to emulate the user themselves send()ing a thing. Now, though, that appears unnecessary: it's an internal
4990 * best-effort message; we don't even care about any error, and it cannot be replied-to. */
4991
4992 Msg_in_impl<Msg_in> msg_in_privileged{ *msg_in }; // Gain access to back-end API.
4993
4994 // Send the internal message. Forego some of the vanilla-send() steps and ignore errors (spirit = do our best).
4995
4996 /* What we are about to do is exceedingly simple: make a small buffer (on the stack even) sufficient
4997 * to store the internal-message mdt header (a StructuredMessage that specifies an internal msg as opposed to user
4998 * msg); load that header in there (the rudimentary info we want to convey about the problem);
4999 * and send_core() the buffer. For context though:
5000 *
5001 * The receiver, when receiving the first (of 1+) low-level blob comprised by the structured-message, doesn't
5002 * pre-know if it's gonna be an internal message or user message. It has to be able to figure it out first-thing
5003 * (upon receiving that blob), and that's done simply by looking inside the mdt header (StructuredMessage)
5004 * which in civilized fashion states whether it's a user message or internal message; and in the former case
5005 * how many more per-segment blobs to read to get the whole thing. For user messages this is slightly tricky;
5006 * first it treats the entire blob as an encoding of the mdt header (any non-header -- user message payload -- in
5007 * the rest of that blob is ignored by capnp at that stage as trailing junk); then upon realizing it *is* a
5008 * user message it will take the post-header part of blob 1; and that's seg 1 of the user message. See
5009 * send_impl() where this blob 1 (with mdt header and seg 1 of user message) is composed, if you want.
5010 *
5011 * For us, though, it is much simpler: There *is* nothing but the mdt header. So that's all we send! The only
5012 * trick is to make it so that the receiver can handle either type (internal versus user). Happily, there is
5013 * no trick: either way, the first thing in blob 1 is the mdt header, of whichever type (StructuredMessage
5014 * schema either way). Then in our case it'll just say, "OK, got the internal message. Let's wait for/read the
5015 * next in-message of whatever type." In the other case it'll interpret the rest of blob 1 and so on, until
5016 * all segments are received; and then wait for/read the next in-message of whatever type.
5017 *
5018 * Anyway. Do that simple thing then. */
5019
5020 // Array-of-words, not bytes: capnp requires word-aligned segments; a stack byte-array guarantees nothing.
5021 array<Word, ceil_div(INTERNAL_MSG_MAX_SZ, sizeof(Word))> blob_out;
5022 Capped_sz_capnp_message_builder int_msg_builder{Blob_mutable{blob_out.data(), INTERNAL_MSG_MAX_SZ},
5023 true}; // Gotta zero it for capnp; array<> lacks ctor and does not.
5024
5025 StructuredMessage::InternalMessageBody::Builder int_msg_root{nullptr};
5026 {
5027 Error_code err_code;
5028#ifndef NDEBUG
5029 const bool ok =
5030#endif
5031 load_mdt(&int_msg_builder, &int_msg_root, &err_code,
5032 m_session_token, msg_in_privileged.id_or_none());
5033 // Indicate we're referencing offending msg *msg_in. -------^
5034 assert(ok && "It should only fail if we try to reuse an existing int_msg_builder.");
5035 assert((!err_code) && "No mdt-loading issues should be possible when accompanying internal-messages.");
5036 }
5037
5038 /* For the metadata-text, shove in a pretty-printing of the metadata header with lots of goodies in there --
5039 * but reasonably capped in length (and in compute used, though certainly not super-quick either) and
5040 * *not* including the user message body itself. However do add the top-level union-which as well.
5041 *
5042 * Again: Careful to make this fit into INTERNAL_MSG_MAX_SZ (see above) or change it if needed.
5043 * Again: If we failed at it after all (INTERNAL_MSG_MAX_SZ too small), catch it and whine in logs but move on. */
5044 bool ok = false;
5045 try
5046 {
5047 int_msg_root.initUnexpectedResponse()
5048 .setOriginatingMessageMetadataText
5049 (ostream_op_string("user-msg-union-which = ", int(msg_in_privileged.m_base.body_root().which()),
5050 ", metadata-header =\n", ostreamable_capnp_full(msg_in_privileged.mdt_root())));
5051 ok = true;
5052 }
5053 catch (const Runtime_error& exc)
5054 {
5055 assert((exc.code() == error::Code::S_INVALID_ARGUMENT)
5056 && "Capped_sz_capnp_message_builder should throw INVALID_ARGUMENT, if capnp ran out of seg1 space and "
5057 "tried to allocateSegment() a 2nd time.");
5058
5059 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Wanted to send internal-message, "
5060 "but the would-be contents could not fit in the buffer sized "
5061 "[" << INTERNAL_MSG_MAX_SZ << "]; this is a bug not a fatal one; opposing side will not "
5062 "receive this best-effort internal-message. Flow-IPC devs: Please look into logic "
5063 "concerning the value of struc::sync_io::Channel's INTERNAL_MSG_MAX_SZ.");
5064 }
5065
5066 if (ok)
5067 {
5068 const auto int_msg_sz = int_msg_builder.getSegmentsForOutput()[0].asBytes().size();
5069
5070 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Sending internal-message (size [" << int_msg_sz << "]): "
5071 "[" << ostreamable_capnp_full(int_msg_builder.getRoot<StructuredMessage>()
5072 .asReader()) << "].");
5073
5074 send_core({ Blob_const{blob_out.data(), int_msg_sz} },
5075 {}, nullptr); // Last nullptr => ignore error.
5076
5077 // Stats: internal msg is always single-seg, single-blob.
5078 {
5079 auto& msg = m_stats.m_snd.m_msg;
5080 ++msg.m_internal_msgs;
5081 ++msg.m_single_segment_msgs;
5082 ++msg.m_total_segments;
5083 ++msg.m_total_low_lvl_blobs;
5084 msg.m_histo_msg_sz.record_value(int_msg_sz);
5085 }
5086 }
5087 else // if (!ok)
5088 {
5089 ++m_stats.m_snd.m_internal_msgs_unserializable; // Non-zero => bug (see its doc header).
5090 }
5091
5092 // Fire the local handler (the 2nd of the 2 actions).
5093 handlers_post<typename Handlers::Message>("rcv_struct_inform_of_unexpected_response()",
5094 std::move(msg_in), On_msg_handler_ptr{});
5095 // See Message::execute() for body.
5096} // Channel::rcv_struct_inform_of_unexpected_response()

5098TEMPLATE_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL
5099template<typename Msg_in_pipe_t>
5100bool CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::rcv_end_reads([[maybe_unused]] const Msg_in_pipe_t& pipe) const
5101{
5102 if constexpr(Owned_channel::S_HAS_2_PIPES)
5103 {
5104 return m_channel_err_code_or_ok || pipe.m_gracefully_closed;
5105 /* See latter's doc header for algorithm/rationale. In short: This pipe may be hosed, specifically by way
5106 * of having received graceful-close (opposing user did async_end_sending()), while the other pipe is fine --
5107 * meaning *this is not yet hosed (m_channel_err_code_or_ok is still falsy). Or, both pipes may be hosed
5108 * (either because one of them got non-graceful-close error, or because both got graceful-close), in which
5109 * case *this is hosed <=> m_channel_err_code_or_ok is truthy. */
5110 }
5111 else
5112 {
5113 return bool(m_channel_err_code_or_ok);
5114 /* If there is only 1 pipe to begin with, that stuff all just collapses into "did pipe get hosed?".
5115 * (Oh, alternatively, a higher-layer (our) error was detected; usually it's capnp protocol errors; but in any
5116 * case that just means *this is hosed immediately as well => m_channel_err_code_or_ok truthy.) */
5117 }
5118}
5119
5120TEMPLATE_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL
5121template<typename Msg_in_pipe_t>
5122bool CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::handle_async_err_code(Msg_in_pipe_t* pipe,
5123 const Error_code& err_code, util::String_view context)
5124{
5125 const auto this_is_hosed = bool(err_code);
5126 const auto overall_hosed = bool(m_channel_err_code_or_ok);
5127
5128 if (!this_is_hosed)
5129 {
5130 if (overall_hosed)
5131 {
5132 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: An operation [" << context << "] yielded success, "
5133 "but the channel was previously hosed; so ignoring the operation's result and potentially "
5134 "ending the calling async chain.");
5135 return false;
5136 }
5137 // else if (!overall_hosed):
5138 return true;
5139 } // else if (this_is_hosed):
5140
5141 /* Mark this flag (don't care if it will be used or how); reaching this line is rare per *this -- no perf
5142 * impact -- and for maintainability let's not worry about how/whether it'll be consumed. Note also this flag
5143 * is only made true here. */
5144 if (err_code == transport::error::Code::S_RECEIVES_FINISHED_CANNOT_RECEIVE)
5145 {
5146 assert((!pipe->m_gracefully_closed) && "Got graceful-close error twice? Why did we try receiving again after "
5147 "that pipe showed error first time? Must be a bug somewhere.");
5148 pipe->m_gracefully_closed = true;
5149 }
5150
5151 if (overall_hosed) // && this_is_hosed
5152 {
5153 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: An operation [" << context << "] yielded failure "
5154 "[" << err_code << "] [" << err_code.message() << "]; but the channel was previously already "
5155 "hosed for reason "
5156 "[" << m_channel_err_code_or_ok << "] [" << m_channel_err_code_or_ok.message() << "]; "
5157 "so ignoring the operation's result and potentially ending the calling async chain.");
5158 }
5159 else // if (!overall_hosed) // && this_is_hosed
5160 {
5161 if (pipe->m_gracefully_closed
5162 && pipe->m_other_pipe_gracefully_closed_or_null // <=> HAS_2_PIPES, incidentally.
5163 && (!*pipe->m_other_pipe_gracefully_closed_or_null)
5164 && rcv_past_init_msgs(*pipe))
5165 {
5166 /* See m_gracefully_closed doc header for algorithm rationale (short version is in the log message).
5167 *
5168 * Here we explain just one new subtlety: the rcv_past_init_msgs() check; it needs to be true
5169 * for *pipe having just become m_gracefully_closed to prevent hosing of *this. Why? Answer:
5170 * there is no legitimate reason to get graceful-close before the pipe got through reading the
5171 * init-messages. Specifically graceful-close <=> opposing user did async_end_sending() on underlying
5172 * Channel pipe <=> either directly through owned_channel_mutable()-> ("you're on your own" type of behavior
5173 * on their part); or via this->async_end_sending() (allowed, in fact encouraged). But:
5174 * this->async_end_sending() is gated on start_ops() having been called previously; and start_ops()
5175 * synchronously/immediately does send_init_msgs(); so this->async_end_sending() shouldn't be possible
5176 * for opposing user to have pulled off. (Reiterating that doing it through owned_channel_mutable()-> is,
5177 * informally speaking, dodgy if not unsanctioned.) That's all as-of-this-writing and legalistic
5178 * (could conceivably change), but the essence of it is simply this:
5179 *
5180 * An unstructured-transport-layer graceful-close in-token appearing before the last in-msg of the
5181 * negotiation/etc. phase = a violation of the protocol => hose *this. (Conversely such in-token anytime
5182 * after that point => legit and encouraged.) Therefore it should hose *this, straight up.
5183 * (@todo Would be nice to log dedicated WARNING about that case. Low-priority, as it's either (1)
5184 * our bug or (2) user making effort to weirdly mess with *owned_channel_mutable(); both unlikely.
5185 * Moreover: in either case the right thing would happen anyway: Channel is hosed before any user messages:
5186 * hard to miss. Other WARNINGs would show the hosing and why: RECEIVES_FINISHED_CANNOT_RECEIVE.) */
5187
5188 FLOW_LOG_INFO("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: An operation [" << context << "] yielded "
5189 "graceful-close ([" << err_code << "] [" << err_code.message() << "]) along one (of 2) in-pipe "
5190 "(details may be logged just above); but the other in-pipe is not yet hosed; "
5191 "therefore we will *not* hose the entire channel yet -- not until other in-pipe is also hosed, "
5192 "gracefully or otherwise -- but *will* end this in-pipe's calling async-read chain. "
5193 "This is normal: It will allow for any messages along the other pipe to be delivered; "
5194 "opposing user choosing to async_end_sending() for this pipe does not negate that.");
5195 }
5196 else
5197 {
5198 /* Only one pipe exists + it's down
5199 * => entire pipe hosed.
5200 * Two pipes exist, but our pipe is down un-gracefully (down not-due to their async_end_sending())
5201 * => both pipes assumed down ~same time.
5202 * Two pipes exist, our pipe is down gracefully (due to their async_end_sending()), but other pipe earlier
5203 * went down the same way (also due to async_end_sending())
5204 * => both pipes are in fact down.
5205 * Two pipes exist, our pipe is down gracefully (due to their async_end_sending()), and other pipe
5206 * is still healthy... but their async_end_sending() was issued somehow before they had sent out all the
5207 * init (pre-user-messages phase) msgs
5208 * => protocol-violating behavior by someone or something.
5209 *
5210 * In all cases these amount to a regular *this-hosing. */
5211
5212 handle_new_error(err_code, context, true);
5213 /* (Arg=true because: err_code came from an Owned_channel async-completion (transport-layer failure);
5214 * the relevant sub-object will have hosed/logged its own stats already.) */
5215 }
5216 } // else // if (!overall_hosed) // && this_is_hosed
5217
5218 return false;
5219} // Channel::handle_async_err_code()
5220
5221TEMPLATE_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL
5222void CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::handle_new_error(const Error_code& err_code_not_ok, util::String_view context,
5223 bool lower_layer_originating)
5224{
5225 const auto& err_code = err_code_not_ok; // For brevity.
5226
5227 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: An operation [" << context << "] yielded failure "
5228 "[" << err_code << "] [" << err_code.message() << "] thus hosing the channel; "
5229 "saving that fail-reason and potentially ending the calling async chain.");
5230 hose(err_code, context, lower_layer_originating); // Sets m_channel_err_code_or_ok; logs final stats.
5231
5232 handlers_post<typename Handlers::Error>("handle_new_error()"); // See Error::execute() for body.
5233} // Channel::handle_new_error()

5235TEMPLATE_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL
5236template<typename Handler_variety, typename... Members>
5237void CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::handlers_post(util::String_view context, Members&&... members)
5238{
5239 // Attn: Handler-posting is a sensitive act with mandatory rules; see our doc header before adding call sites.
5240
5241 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Handler with context "
5242 "[" << context << "] shall synchronously execute right now.");
5243
5244 /* (A decent optimizer should generate pretty-much the body of Handler_variety::execute(this) here, inlined.
5245 * The constructor, even if really executed, just copied over a scalar or two-ish onto some stack variable(s).
5246 * .execute() then did the actual "stuff," using those value(s) if any.) */
5247 Handler_variety handler_of_known_variety{ std::forward<Members>(members)... };
5248 handler_of_known_variety.execute(this);
5249} // Channel::handlers_post()

5273bool CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::check_unsendable(const Msg_out& msg) const
5274{
5275 if constexpr(Owned_channel::S_HAS_BLOB_PIPE_ONLY) // C++17: This is #if-like.
5276 {
5277 const auto hndl = msg.native_handle_or_null();
5278 if (!hndl.null())
5279 {
5280 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Send request wants to send native handle "
5281 "[" << hndl << "], but the owned channel is incapable of such "
5282 "transport. Ignoring. Bug by user?");
5283 return false;
5284 }
5285 // else
5286 }
5287 return true;
5288} // Channel::check_unsendable()

5300template<typename On_msg_handler>
5301bool CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::async_request(Msg_out* msg_ptr, const Msg_in* originating_msg_or_null,
5302 msg_id_out_t* id_unless_one_off, On_msg_handler&& on_rsp_func,
5303 Error_code* err_code)
5304{
5305 using boost::make_shared;
5306
5307 return check_not_started_ops("async_request()")
5308 && check_unsendable(*msg_ptr)
5309 && check_prior_error("async_request()")
5310 && send_impl(msg_ptr, originating_msg_or_null, err_code,
5311 make_shared<typename On_msg_handler_ptr::element_type>(std::move(on_rsp_func)),
5312 id_unless_one_off);

5314
5315TEMPLATE_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL
5316bool CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::send_impl(Msg_out* msg_public_ptr, const Msg_in* originating_msg_or_null,
5317 Error_code* err_code,
5318 // @todo Make it && for a little perf boost.
5319 const On_msg_handler_ptr& on_rsp_func_or_null, msg_id_out_t* id_unless_one_off)
5320{
5321 using util::Blob_const;
5322 using flow::Fine_clock;
5323
5324 FLOW_ERROR_EXEC_AND_THROW_ON_ERROR(bool, send_impl,
5325 msg_public_ptr, originating_msg_or_null, _1,
5326 on_rsp_func_or_null, id_unless_one_off);
5327 // ^-- Call ourselves and return if err_code is null. If got to present line, err_code is not null.
5328
5329 // See send() doc header which summarizes our course of action. See also m_channel doc header for context.
5330
5331 Msg_out_impl<Msg_out> msg{ *msg_public_ptr }; // Gain access to internal (back end) API of the Msg_out.
5332 const bool one_off = !bool(id_unless_one_off);
5333
5334 /* In general, try to detect errors (that would prevent actual message send) early. Among those, start with
5335 * those checks that don't need any state to change first (as then we needn't undo such changes or worry about
5336 * whether we should).
5337 *
5338 * As of this writing one can do pretty much anything, except that in a log-in m_phase there are rigid
5339 * limitations:
5340 * - CLI_LOG_IN sends only request, SRV_LOG_IN sends only response, etc.
5341 * - Limited # of messages can be sent at all (can use m_snd_msg_next_id to see how many have been
5342 * sent already).
5343 * Go: */
5344 if (m_phase != Phase::S_LOGGED_IN) // (Else, as noted, there are no limitations in this context.)
5345 {
5346 if (m_phase == Phase::S_SRV_LOG_IN)
5347 {
5348 if (!originating_msg_or_null)
5349 {
5350 /* Unsolicited. That is certainly fine, usually, except that in SRV_LOG_IN this *must* be the
5351 * log-in response and hence *must* be a... response. */
5352 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Log-in (as server): Send attempt of what must be "
5353 "the log-in response, but they failed to specify that it *is* a response. Ignoring. "
5354 "In theory they can try sending this log-in response again with the proper form of send().");
5355 return false;
5356 } // if (!originating_msg_or_null)
5357 // else: Fall through.
5358 } // if (m_phase == SRV_LOG_IN)
5359 else // if (m_phase == CLI_LOG_IN)
5360 {
5361 if (originating_msg_or_null)
5362 {
5363 /* Response. That is certainly fine, usually, except that in CLI_LOG_IN this *must* be the
5364 * log-in request which cannot be replying to anything else. A little hard to imagine how the rest of the
5365 * logic would let things get this far, but anyway better safe than sorry. */
5366 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Log-in (as client): Send attempt of what must be "
5367 "the log-in request, but somehow they specified it's a response itself. Ignoring. "
5368 "In theory they can try sending this log-in request again with the proper form of send().");
5369 return false;
5370 }
5371 // else:
5372 if (!on_rsp_func_or_null)
5373 {
5374 /* No response expectation (it's a non-request). That is certainly fine, usually, except that in CLI_LOG_IN
5375 * this *must* be the log-in request and hence *must* expect response. */
5376 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Log-in (as client): Send attempt of what must be "
5377 "the log-in request, but they failed to specify it expects a (log-in) response (used send() "
5378 "instead of async_request()). Ignoring. "
5379 "In theory they can try sending this log-in request again with the proper API which is "
5380 "async_request().");
5381 return false;
5382 } // else if (!on_rsp_func_or_null)
5383 // else: Fall through.
5384 } // else // if (m_phase == CLI_LOG_IN)
5385
5386 /* Got here: they're allowed to send a msg of this (response/unsolicited)x(request/not) type in this Phase.
5387 * That leaves one more possible mis-use: */
5388
5389 if (m_snd_msg_next_id != 1)
5390 {
5391 assert((m_snd_msg_next_id == 2) && "How in the hell did we get past this error last time?");
5392 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Log-in: Send request wants to send out-message, "
5393 "but in this phase one can send at most one (log-in request on client, response on "
5394 "server), and this is message 2. Ignoring.");
5395 return false;
5396 }
5397 // else { Fall through. }
5398 } // if (m_phase != LOGGED_IN)
5399 // else if (m_phase == LOGGED_IN) { As noted: no restrictions in the main phase. }
5400
5401 /* First state change: generate ID (and seq #; it is important we only generate it now, at actual sync-send time,
5402 * as opposed to somehow earlier which could mis-order the seq #s). The response-expectation tracking below
5403 * needs the new ID and (as of this writing) can't fail, so now is the time. */
5404 const auto id = m_snd_msg_next_id++;
5405 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Send request: Generated out-message ID [" << id << "].");
5406
5407 /* Second (potential) state change:
5408 * Before sending there's this to take care of: now that the send-time has come, we know the ID (a/k/a seq #,
5409 * though that doesn't matter here), and can therefore register the response expectation, if any,
5410 * in m_rcv_expecting_msg_map.
5411 *
5412 * on_rsp_func_or_null non-null => They've supplied async handler for response.
5413 * m_rcv_expecting_response_map marks down that a response is being awaited. */
5414 if (on_rsp_func_or_null)
5415 {
5416 /* A response expectation (a/k/a request). Mental sanity-check for various phases:
5417 * - LOGGED_IN: Allowed, of course.
5418 * - CLI_LOG_IN: Required (log-in request => await response to it). We checked this earlier.
5419 * - SRV_LOG_IN: Allowed, though perhaps a bit unorthodox (typically log-in request => log-in response; and
5420 * that ends any exchange). However, we don't care. We enter LOGGED_IN phase below upon successful send;
5421 * and if they want to get a response to that, that's their business. */
5422
5423#ifndef NDEBUG
5424 const auto result =
5425#endif
5426 m_rcv_expecting_response_map.emplace(id,
5427 new Expecting_response{ { one_off, on_rsp_func_or_null },
5428 Fine_clock::now() });
5429 assert(result.second && "IDs do not repeat, so dupe-insertion should not be possible.");
5430
5431 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Registered a (one-off? = [" << one_off << "]) "
5432 "response expectation (request about to be sync-nb-sent); that raises their total count to "
5433 "[" << m_rcv_expecting_response_map.size() << "].");
5434 /* Note: Any failure to send() below is fatal to *this, meaning no further send()s (or receives for that matter)
5435 * are going to happen. Hence it does not matter how we've changed m_snd_msg_next_id and other things;
5436 * it's not like they can be "put back" and "reused." */
5437 } // if (on_rsp_func_or_null)
5438
5439 /* From this point on, if anything fails, then *this is hosed (at least in the send direction; as of this
5440 * writing the somewhat-odd case of SENDS_FINISHED_CANNOT_SEND leaves the rcv-direction to operate; no hose()
5441 * call to "really" hose *this in that one case). The point:
5442 *
5443 * In particular, about state that we've affected above, and whether we need to "put it back":
5444 * - m_snd_msg_next_id does not matter anymore; there will be no more sending. Don't need to re-decrement it
5445 * or any such thing. (In the SENDS_FINISHED_CANNOT_SEND case they'll keep wasting higher and higher IDs but
5446 * it'll just keep not working; seems fine.)
5447 * - m_rcv_expecting_response_map:
5448 * The user-error/non-mainstream case of SENDS_FINISHED_CANNOT_SEND below (non-hose()ing) will
5449 * keep a useless, never-gonna fire response-expectation (if any) in m_rcv_expecting_response_map.
5450 * Plus, until *this is actually hose()d, any repeated attempts will keep adding more of them (new ID each
5451 * time, etc.). That's not great. It's strange user behavior in the first place, but we might as well
5452 * undo that part. So see that below, if it comes up.
5453 * - The mainstream/non-user-error case where a send error hose()s *this below: hose() cleans out
5454 * m_rcv_expecting_response_map and similar. So don't worry about it in that case. */
5455
5456 /* Let's prep the binaries to send! This is the other side of the logic on the receive side. See start_and_poll()
5457 * where that's kicked off. It will refer you to Msg_in_pipe doc header and so on. The below should follow
5458 * from that understanding. So we'll keep inline comments fairly svelte, unless there's new info. */
5459
5460 msg_id_t originating_msg_id_or_none = 0;
5461 if (originating_msg_or_null)
5462 {
5463 const Msg_in_impl<Msg_in> originating_msg_privileged{ *const_cast<Msg_in*>(originating_msg_or_null) };
5464 /* (The const_cast<> works around the deficiency of the facade technique Msg_in_impl uses; it cannot wrap
5465 * a const object, as it stores a ref to non-const Msg_in. We even made the object const to guarantee we won't
5466 * do anything untoward with it. @todo Nevertheless try to think of a nicer way to do this.) */
5467 originating_msg_id_or_none = originating_msg_privileged.id_or_none();
5468 }
5469
5470 Segment_bufs buffers_out; // Place buffer ptrs/sizes into this.
5471 /* Plumbed out of emit_serialization() only for seg-related stats and/or logs below.
5472 * Perf cost is low, as it just move()s a thing it already prepared internally, according to its contract. */
5473 Split_segments split_segs_out;
5474 msg.emit_serialization(&buffers_out, &split_segs_out, m_struct_lender_session, err_code,
5475 m_session_token, originating_msg_id_or_none, id);
5476 if (*err_code)
5477 {
5478 // Try to be helpful with logging depending on which error occurred, for things we specifically know about.
5479 if ((*err_code == error::Code::S_SERIALIZE_FAILED_SPLIT_ENCODING_TOO_BIG)
5480 || (*err_code == error::Code::S_SERIALIZE_FAILED_SPLIT_SEGS_TOO_MANY))
5481 {
5482 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Send request wants to send out-message; "
5483 "mdt header in seg1 would contain session-token [" << m_session_token << "], "
5484 "replying-to msg ID [" << originating_msg_id_or_none << "], our msg ID [" << id << "]. "
5485 "However an error occurred ([" << *err_code << "] [" << err_code->message() << "]). "
5486 "Split-segments-related error (which one: see code above): additional relevant info "
5487 "follows in logs below. "
5488 "For reference: Message itself (may be truncated): [" << msg.m_base << "]. "
5489 "This is a channel-hosing error; emitting it.");
5490
5491 /* By contract, on these particular errors, out-arg split_segs_out shall be valid. Printing it will
5492 * show the general situation w/r/t seg-splitting; e.g., one can see which entry or entries would trigger
5493 * the error. */
5494 size_t idx = 0;
5495 for (const auto& split_seg : split_segs_out)
5496 {
5497 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: "
5498 "Split-segments entry [" << (++idx) << '/' << split_segs_out.size() << "]: "
5499 "start_idx = [" << split_seg.m_start_idx << "], "
5500 "n_cont_subsegs = [" << split_seg.m_n_cont_subsegs << "].");
5501 }
5502 /* (Incidentally: if no error then this info is probably still TRACE-logged and/or DATA-logged one way or
5503 * another. Here we want to make pretty sure it is visible, as if this does happen it'll probably feel
5504 * quite annoying, and it's nice to have some debug info immediately ready in such cases. Hence WARNING.)
5505 * @todo Maybe do some join()/transform() type stuff => log 1 msg? The above is fine too though. */
5506 }
5507 else if (*err_code == error::Code::S_INVALID_ARGUMENT)
5508 {
5509 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Send request wants to send out-message; "
5510 "mdt header in seg1 would contain session-token [" << m_session_token << "], "
5511 "replying-to msg ID [" << originating_msg_id_or_none << "], our msg ID [" << id << "]. "
5512 "However an error occurred ([" << *err_code << "] [" << err_code->message() << "]). "
5513 "INVALID_ARGUMENT: there was insufficient or no space for this mdt header; "
5514 "if you use a custom Builder_config when forming your Msg_out, please be sure "
5515 "to set its .m_frame_prefix_sz to at least "
5516 "[" << BUILDER_CONFIG_FRAME_PREFIX_SZ_VIA_STRUC_CHANNEL << "]. "
5517 "For reference: Message itself (may be truncated): [" << msg.m_base << "]. "
5518 "This is a channel-hosing error; emitting it.");
5519 }
5520 else
5521 {
5522 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Send request wants to send out-message; "
5523 "mdt header in seg1 would contain session-token [" << m_session_token << "], "
5524 "replying-to msg ID [" << originating_msg_id_or_none << "], our msg ID [" << id << "]. "
5525 "However a misc error occurred ([" << *err_code << "] [" << err_code->message() << "]). "
5526 "For reference: Message itself (may be truncated): [" << msg.m_base << "]. "
5527 "This is a channel-hosing error; emitting it.");
5528 }
5529
5530 /* @todo Does it need to be channel-hosing really? INVALID_ARGUMENT and SERIALIZE_FAILED_SPLIT_ENCODING_TOO_BIG
5531 * at least are per-message problems; it is conceivable one could recover, continuing to use *this Channel
5532 * for other things. The trade-off is versus a simpler contract and a higher chance user notices the error,
5533 * if it hoses the whole Channel just by coming in contact with this message. */
5534 hose(*err_code, "send_core()/emit_serialization", false);
5535
5536 return true; // This is similar to send_core() failing below, as far as the user is concerned.
5537 } // if (*err_code) (from emit_serialization())
5538 // else:
5539
5540 /* `msg` ostream printout has some other interesting info plus a (possibly truncated) one-line representation of
5541 * .body_root() contents. */
5542 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Send request wants to send (user) out-message; "
5543 "mdt header in seg1 contains session-token [" << m_session_token << "], "
5544 "replying-to msg ID [" << originating_msg_id_or_none << "], our msg ID [" << id << "], "
5545 "segment-count [" << buffers_out.size() << "]. Message itself (may be truncated): "
5546 "[" << msg.m_base << "].");
5547
5548 /* Print the entire contents with indentation/newlines.
5549 * The user message could be giant. By definition that is for DATA verbosity only.
5550 * In addition even the mere computation of what to print (e.g., if we wanted to truncate it before printing
5551 * at TRACE level) is potentially cripplingly slow; so absolutely do not do it outside the log macro. */
5552 FLOW_LOG_DATA("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Here is the complete user "
5553 "message:\n" << ostreamable_capnp_full(msg.m_base.body_root()->asReader()));
5554
5555 // OK! Send it/them out.
5556 const auto send_core_ok = send_core(buffers_out, msg.m_base.native_handle_or_null(), err_code);
5557 if ((!send_core_ok) || *err_code)
5558 {
5559 /* In a comment above we've determined that, w/r/t state that has already been affected by this function
5560 * before send_core(): we need not worry about m_snd_msg_next_id; but we should undo m_rcv_expecting_response_map
5561 * change we'd made (if any) (but if the error hose()d us, then no point).
5562 *
5563 * Lastly there is the matter of stats. By a (possibly unwritten) convention, we don't agonize whether to
5564 * record stats when something encounters a basically fatal error (meaning no further related stat changes
5565 * will follow); just do what's convenient. So we could record stats or not. That said, there's a special
5566 * case here (admittedly it's obscure and requires user error): If send_core() did not hose() us -- meaning
5567 * SENDS_FINISHED_CANNOT_SEND -- then these stats, including whatever crazy split_segs stats were recorded
5568 * (for example), get recorded; and moreover by nature of SENDS_FINISHED_CANNOT_SEND they can keep retrying
5569 * and recording these stats, as if that stuff is all going out. That is lame. So just don't record stats...
5570 * for either type of error scenario. No point and avoids that weirdness. */
5571 if ((!send_core_ok) && on_rsp_func_or_null)
5572 {
5573#ifndef NDEBUG
5574 const bool erase_ok = 1 ==
5575#endif
5576 m_rcv_expecting_response_map.erase(id);
5577 assert(erase_ok && "We should have just registered this request. Bug?");
5578 }
5579
5580 return send_core_ok;
5581 } // if ((!send_core_ok) || *err_code)
5582 // else: Everything went great!
5583
5584 if (on_rsp_func_or_null && (!one_off))
5585 {
5586 *id_unless_one_off = id; // Let them know the out-message ID: they can use it in undo_expect_responses().
5587
5588 // @todo Maybe require one_off=true in CLI_LOG_IN? I guess it could be fine; just odd.
5589 }
5590
5591 // Stats: send-side user-message classification + seg/split stats, response expectation gauges.
5592 {
5593 /* @todo (Maybe/revisit) The symmetrical receive-side logic sits in Msg_in[_impl]::deserialize_body(),
5594 * so for consistency it might be nice to put the below nearby in msg.hpp in Msg_out[_impl]::emit_serialization().
5595 * It might also be a bit more efficient about the split-seg stuff, if it can load it up in the same loop
5596 * as the actual splitting (if any). On the other hand we'd have to pass some info that only we have,
5597 * like at least bool(on_rsp_func_or_null) and one_off. It's more or less fine this way too. As for perf
5598 * specifically: it's probably all right, particularly since the splitting should be a rare (with SHM backing,
5599 * non-existent) event. */
5600
5601 auto& snd_msg = m_stats.m_snd.m_msg;
5602 ++snd_msg.m_user_msgs;
5603 if (on_rsp_func_or_null) // Request path (async_request()).
5604 {
5605 ++snd_msg.m_requests;
5606 one_off && (++snd_msg.m_requests_one_off);
5607 originating_msg_or_null && (++snd_msg.m_request_responses);
5608
5609 // Attn: m_stats.m_rcv (the rest around here deals with snd-side m_stats.)
5610 ++(one_off ? m_stats.m_rcv.m_expect_response_one_off_active
5611 : m_stats.m_rcv.m_expect_response_sticky_active);
5612 }
5613 else // Notification path (send()).
5614 {
5615 ++snd_msg.m_notifications;
5616 originating_msg_or_null && (++snd_msg.m_notification_responses);
5617 }
5618
5619 msg.m_base.native_handle_or_null().null() || (++snd_msg.m_handle_bearing_msgs);
5620
5621 // Seg/split stats from emit_serialization() output.
5622 auto n_segs = buffers_out.size(); // # of blobs now; we'll "correct" it to # of segs below.
5623 snd_msg.m_total_low_lvl_blobs += n_segs;
5624
5625 // Original (pre-split) segment count: subtract split overhead.
5626 for (const auto& split_seg : split_segs_out)
5627 {
5628 n_segs -= split_seg.m_n_cont_subsegs; // m_n_cont_subsegs = # of blobs excluding the first one.
5629 snd_msg.m_histo_split_blobs_per_seg.record_value(split_seg.m_n_cont_subsegs + 1);
5630 }
5631
5632 snd_msg.m_total_segments += n_segs;
5633 ++((n_segs == 1) ? snd_msg.m_single_segment_msgs : snd_msg.m_multi_segment_msgs);
5634 split_segs_out.empty() || (++snd_msg.m_msgs_with_split_segments);
5635
5636 /* Total serialization size (sum of all blobs).
5637 * Perf: @todo It would be nice to do that in an existing loop in emit_serialization() somewhere. */
5638 size_t total_sz = 0;
5639 for (const auto& blob : buffers_out)
5640 {
5641 total_sz += blob.size();
5642 }
5643 snd_msg.m_histo_msg_sz.record_value(total_sz);
5644 } // Stats.
5645
5646 return true;
5647} // Channel::send_impl()
5648
5649TEMPLATE_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL
5650bool CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::send_core(const Segment_bufs& blobs_out,
5651 Native_handle hndl, Error_code* err_code_or_ignore)
5652{
5653 /* `sink` used only if err_code_or_ignore is null -- we are to ignore any error and let the next send*() catch it.
5654 * As of this writing used only for internal messages which are best-effort. */
5655 Error_code sink;
5656 Error_code* const err_code = err_code_or_ignore ? err_code_or_ignore : &sink;
5657
5658 // See send() doc header which summarizes our course of action. See also m_channel doc header for context.
5659
5660 /* One more thing before we really do stuff -- as discussed in send_init_msgs() -- if protocol-negotiation
5661 * message send failed, and we got here (meaning check_prior_error() is false, meaning !m_channel_err_code_or_ok,
5662 * meaning no prior send_core()/remote_peer_process_liveness_check()/.../start_and_poll() got to it first), then
5663 * promote that saved protocol-negotiation-send error to m_channel_err_code_or_ok and emit it (the latter done one
5664 * time per *this, as usual). */
5665 if (m_init_msg_err_code_or_ok)
5666 {
5667 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Send request wants to send out-message, "
5668 "but earlier protocol-negotiation message send along a pipe failed (error "
5669 "[" << m_init_msg_err_code_or_ok << "] [" << m_init_msg_err_code_or_ok.message() << "]). "
5670 "We now promote this to a channel-hosing error; emitting it.");
5671
5672 assert(err_code_or_ignore
5673 && "No internal messages shall be sent before start_and_poll() begins read chain. Did this change? "
5674 "Just did not want to deal with the subtleties of that + m_init_msg_err_code_or_ok "
5675 "until really necessary, if ever.");
5676 *err_code = m_init_msg_err_code_or_ok;
5677 hose(*err_code, "send_core()/init-msg promotion", true);
5678 return true; // This is similar to send_*() failing below, as far as the user is concerned.
5679 } // if (m_init_msg_err_code_or_ok)
5680
5681 // That's it. Now it's just blobs to send out, regardless of what they represent.
5682
5683 [[maybe_unused]] const bool has_hndl = !hndl.null();
5684
5685 // Synchronous helpers.
5686 [[maybe_unused]] const auto send_blobs = [&]()
5687 {
5688 if constexpr(Owned_channel::S_HAS_BLOB_PIPE)
5689 {
5690 for (const auto& blob : blobs_out)
5691 {
5692#ifndef NDEBUG
5693 const bool ok =
5694#endif
5695 m_channel.send_blob(blob, err_code);
5696 assert(ok); // Only false if not PEER state; we promised undefined behavior in that case.
5697
5698 if (*err_code)
5699 {
5700 return;
5701 }
5702 }
5703 }
5704 else
5705 {
5706 assert(false && "We shouldn't be called; see code below.");
5707 }
5708 }; // const auto send_blobs =
5709 [[maybe_unused]] const auto send_meta_blobs = [&]()
5710 {
5711 if constexpr(Owned_channel::S_HAS_NATIVE_HANDLE_PIPE)
5712 {
5713 bool first = true;
5714 for (const auto& blob : blobs_out)
5715 {
5716#ifndef NDEBUG
5717 const bool ok =
5718#endif
5719 m_channel.send_native_handle(first ? (first = false, hndl) : Native_handle{},
5720 blob, err_code);
5721 assert(ok); // Same as above.
5722
5723 if (*err_code)
5724 {
5725 return;
5726 }
5727 }
5728 }
5729 else
5730 {
5731 assert(false && "We shouldn't be called; see code below.");
5732 }
5733 }; // const auto send_meta_blobs =
5734
5735 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Send request wants to send out-message, "
5736 "and the serialization shall now be sent: total of [" << blobs_out.size() << "] segments, 1 per blob; "
5737 "1st blob contains (ahead of potential user message payload) metadata header "
5738 "including ID and the further-segments count, plus native handle (unless null) = [" << hndl << "].");
5739
5740 if constexpr(Owned_channel::S_HAS_BLOB_PIPE_ONLY)
5741 {
5742 assert((!has_hndl) && "Attempting to send a native-handle over an Owned_channel without a native handles pipe.");
5743 send_blobs();
5744 }
5745 else if constexpr(Owned_channel::S_HAS_NATIVE_HANDLE_PIPE_ONLY)
5746 {
5747 send_meta_blobs();
5748 }
5749 else
5750 {
5751 static_assert(Owned_channel::S_HAS_2_PIPES, "This code assumes 1 blobs pipe, 1 handles pipe, or both exactly.");
5752 has_hndl ? send_meta_blobs() : send_blobs();
5753 }
5754
5755 // `msg` may now be safely destroyed.
5756
5757 if (*err_code)
5758 {
5759 // A send_*() failed. There is one special case however which we promised to emit in a special way.
5760 if (*err_code == transport::error::Code::S_SENDS_FINISHED_CANNOT_SEND)
5761 {
5762 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Send request wants to send out-message, "
5763 "and we tried to send the serialization: total of [" << blobs_out.size() << "] segs, 1/blob; "
5764 "1st blob contains (ahead of potential user message payload) metadata header "
5765 "including ID and the further-segments count, plus native handle (unless null) = "
5766 "[" << hndl << "]. However Channel reports "
5767 "we had already sent graceful-close. Therefore ignoring send attempt after all.");
5768 /* Subtlety regarding bool(err_code_or_ignore):
5769 * - Regardless of that, we are not to record this "error" into m_channel_err_code_or_ok by our contract.
5770 * - What remains, then, is whether to return true or false.
5771 * - If bool(err_code_or_ignore) is true (not ignoring errors) then return false by contract.
5772 * - Otherwise, 1, still return false as promised; but 2, the caller won't care anyway.
5773 * So return false. */
5774 err_code->clear();
5775 return false;
5776 }
5777 // else
5778 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Send request wants to send out-message, "
5779 "and we tried to send the serialization: total of [" << blobs_out.size() << "] segs, 1/blob; "
5780 "(ahead of potential user message payload) metadata header "
5781 "including ID and the further-segments count, plus native handle (unless null) = "
5782 "[" << hndl << "]. However Channel reports "
5783 "a send failed (error [" << *err_code << "] [" << err_code->message() << "]). "
5784 "This is a channel-hosing error; emitting it "
5785 "unless internally-ignoring (are we? = [" << (!err_code_or_ignore) << "]).");
5786 if (err_code_or_ignore)
5787 {
5788 // Owned_channel sender pipe just hosed at the transport layer; it has hosed/logged itself already.
5789 hose(*err_code, "send_core()/Owned_channel send fail", true);
5790 }
5791 return true;
5792 }
5793 // else cool! But one last thing possibly:
5794
5795 if (m_phase == Phase::S_SRV_LOG_IN)
5796 {
5797 FLOW_LOG_INFO("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Log-in (as server): Successfully sent what must be the "
5798 "log-in response message. Changing phase to logged-in.");
5799 m_phase = Phase::S_LOGGED_IN;
5800 }
5801
5802 assert(!*err_code);
5803 return true;
5804} // Channel::send_core()
5805
5806TEMPLATE_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL
5807void CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::send_init_msgs()
5808{
5809 using flow::util::ceil_div;
5810 using util::Blob_mutable;
5811 using util::Blob_const;
5812 using boost::array;
5813 using Word = ::capnp::word;
5814
5815 constexpr size_t SEG_SZ = 256; // Enough to serialize a ProtocolNegotiation or ChannelHeader capnp-struct in 1 seg.
5816
5817 /* See "Protocol negotiation" in class doc header for background.
5818 * Our job here is straightforward enough (like a much-simpler send_core(), albeit along both pipes if relevant, with
5819 * a really simple payload contained in 1 blob-message), and the code below is easy enough to follow.
5820 *
5821 * (Update: Now, also, we send the ChannelHeader struct immediately following that.)
5822 *
5823 * The only subtlety has to do with error handling. Recall we are called at the end of successful start_ops(), hence
5824 * before any user send()/async_request() and before start_and_poll() (which is when we begin the read chain, and
5825 * error handler is registered and can be subsequently invoked). What we do below is synchronous.
5826 * Vast majority of the time all will work below, so nothing to worry about; now suppose an m_channel.send_*()
5827 * below fails (into err_code). Now what?
5828 *
5829 * Short-circuiting discussion of various other possibilities, basically, we treat this as the whole channel being
5830 * hosed; so we save error into m_init_msg_err_code_or_ok (ref = err_code). Only question is when to emit it.
5831 * We execute before start_and_poll() (through which incoming-direction work becomes possible) and before
5832 * and send()/async_request() (through which outgoing-direction work happens). (The two interact fine in either
5833 * order; a given new error is emitted to the first such API call.) So what we do is check m_init_msg_err_code_or_ok
5834 * here and check it in start_and_poll(); if truthy then immediately promote it to m_channel_err_code_or_ok
5835 * and emit via handle_new_error() as usual. What if send()/async_request() happens first though? Similarly
5836 * there. */
5837
5838 auto& err_code = m_init_msg_err_code_or_ok;
5839 assert(!err_code);
5840
5841 const auto protocol_ver_to_send = m_protocol_negotiator.local_max_proto_ver_for_sending();
5842 const auto protocol_ver_to_send_aux = m_protocol_negotiator_aux.local_max_proto_ver_for_sending();
5843 assert((protocol_ver_to_send != Protocol_negotiator::S_VER_ALREADY_SENT)
5844 && (protocol_ver_to_send_aux != Protocol_negotiator::S_VER_ALREADY_SENT)
5845 && "How'd we get to this line twice? Or Protocol_negotiator bug?");
5846 assert((m_protocol_negotiator.local_max_proto_ver_for_sending() == Protocol_negotiator::S_VER_ALREADY_SENT)
5847 && (m_protocol_negotiator_aux.local_max_proto_ver_for_sending() == Protocol_negotiator::S_VER_ALREADY_SENT)
5848 && "Protocol_negotiator not properly marking the once-only sending-out of protocol version?");
5849
5850 // Array-of-words, not bytes: capnp requires word-aligned segments; a stack byte-array guarantees nothing.
5851 array<Word, ceil_div(SEG_SZ, sizeof(Word))> blob_out1;
5852 array<Word, ceil_div(SEG_SZ, sizeof(Word))> blob_out2;
5853 Capped_sz_capnp_message_builder builder1{Blob_mutable{blob_out1.data(), SEG_SZ},
5854 true}; // Gotta zero it for capnp; array<> lacks ctor and does not.
5855 Capped_sz_capnp_message_builder builder2{Blob_mutable{blob_out2.data(), SEG_SZ},
5856 true};
5857 /* The two headers are expected in this particular order. Must pass protocol-negotiation first before even looking
5858 * at anything past that, including ChannelHeader. This is a formal requirement of the Protocol_negotiator
5859 * pattern. */
5860 {
5861 auto root = builder1.initRoot<schema::detail::ProtocolNegotiation>();
5862 root.setMaxProtoVer(protocol_ver_to_send);
5863 root.setMaxProtoVerAux(protocol_ver_to_send_aux);
5864 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Here is the prepended protocol-negotiation header we shall send:"
5865 "\n" << ostreamable_capnp_full(root.asReader()));
5866 }
5867 {
5868 auto root = builder2.initRoot<schema::detail::ChannelHeader>();
5869 auto claimed_own_proc_creds = root.initClaimedOwnProcessCredentials();
5870 claimed_own_proc_creds.setProcessId(util::Process_credentials::own_process_id());
5871 claimed_own_proc_creds.setUserId(util::Process_credentials::own_user_id());
5872 claimed_own_proc_creds.setGroupId(util::Process_credentials::own_group_id());
5873 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Here is the prepended channel-header we shall send:"
5874 "\n" << ostreamable_capnp_full(root.asReader()));
5875 }
5876
5877 const Blob_const seg_blob_out1{blob_out1.data(),
5878 builder1.getSegmentsForOutput()[0].asBytes().size()};
5879 const Blob_const seg_blob_out2{blob_out2.data(),
5880 builder2.getSegmentsForOutput()[0].asBytes().size()};
5881
5882 // That's it. Now it's just <blob>x2 to send out.
5883
5884 // Synchronous helpers.
5885 [[maybe_unused]] const auto send_blobs = [&]()
5886 {
5887 if constexpr(Owned_channel::S_HAS_BLOB_PIPE)
5888 {
5889 m_channel.send_blob(seg_blob_out1, &err_code);
5890 err_code || m_channel.send_blob(seg_blob_out2, &err_code);
5891 }
5892 // else if constexpr(true) { No-op: We won't be called; see below. }
5893 };
5894 [[maybe_unused]] const auto send_meta_blobs = [&]()
5895 {
5896 if constexpr(Owned_channel::S_HAS_NATIVE_HANDLE_PIPE)
5897 {
5898 m_channel.send_native_handle(Native_handle{}, seg_blob_out1, &err_code);
5899 err_code || m_channel.send_native_handle(Native_handle{}, seg_blob_out2, &err_code);
5900 }
5901 // else if constexpr(true) { No-op: We won't be called; see below. }
5902 };
5903
5904 if constexpr(Owned_channel::S_HAS_BLOB_PIPE_ONLY)
5905 {
5906 send_blobs();
5907 }
5908 else if constexpr(Owned_channel::S_HAS_NATIVE_HANDLE_PIPE_ONLY)
5909 {
5910 send_meta_blobs();
5911 }
5912 else
5913 {
5914 static_assert(Owned_channel::S_HAS_2_PIPES, "This code assumes 1 blobs pipe, 1 handles pipe, or both exactly.");
5915 send_meta_blobs();
5916 if (!err_code)
5917 {
5918 send_blobs();
5919 }
5920 }
5921} // Channel::send_init_msgs()
5922
5923TEMPLATE_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL
5924bool CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::remote_peer_process_liveness_check(Error_code* err_code)
5925{
5926 using util::process_running;
5927
5928 FLOW_ERROR_EXEC_AND_THROW_ON_ERROR(bool, remote_peer_process_liveness_check, _1);
5929 // ^-- Call ourselves and return if err_code is null. If got to present line, err_code is not null.
5930
5931 if (!check_prior_error("remote_peer_process_liveness_check()"))
5932 {
5933 return false;
5934 }
5935 // else
5936
5937 ++m_stats.m_rcv.m_liveness_checks;
5938
5939 /* One more thing before we really do stuff -- as discussed in send_init_msgs() -- perform the same check as
5940 * in send_core() at this stage. Please read that comment; then come back here.
5941 *
5942 * If this is truthy, this is our doc header's "channel is not healthy for reason E, and this is our first chance
5943 * to emit this" outcome. */
5944 if (m_init_msg_err_code_or_ok)
5945 {
5946 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: They want to check whether opposing process is alive "
5947 "and hose channel/emit error if not; "
5948 "but earlier protocol-negotiation message send along a pipe failed (error "
5949 "[" << m_init_msg_err_code_or_ok << "] [" << m_init_msg_err_code_or_ok.message() << "]). "
5950 "We now promote this to a channel-hosing error; emitting it. Note that this does not "
5951 "mean the opposing process is dead (though it might be); but that the channel is hosed, as we "
5952 "are emitting this for the first and only time now, opportunistically.");
5953
5954 assert((m_init_msg_err_code_or_ok != transport::error::Code::S_PEER_PROCESS_NO_LONGER_EXISTS)
5955 && "At any rate we promised this! Indeed any init-msg sends don't do liveness checking.");
5956 *err_code = m_init_msg_err_code_or_ok;
5957 hose(*err_code, "remote_peer_process_liveness_check()/init-msg promotion", true);
5958 } // if (m_init_msg_err_code_or_ok)
5959 else if (!m_peer_process_creds) // && (!m_init_msg_err_code_or_ok)
5960 {
5961 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: They want to check whether opposing process is alive "
5962 "and hose channel/emit error if not; but we do not know its PID yet; must assume it is alive for "
5963 "now. This can only occur if (1) they have not yet invoked start_and_poll(); or (2) they have, but "
5964 "we have not yet received the mandatory init-messages (protocol-negotiation + channel-header).");
5965 err_code->clear();
5966 }
5967 else if (process_running(m_peer_process_creds->process_id()))
5968 {
5969 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Opposing process with creds [" << *m_peer_process_creds << "] "
5970 "is still alive according to OS.");
5971 err_code->clear();
5972 }
5973 else // if (!process_running(opposing PID))
5974 {
5975 *err_code = transport::error::Code::S_PEER_PROCESS_NO_LONGER_EXISTS;
5976 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Opposing process with creds [" << *m_peer_process_creds << "] "
5977 "is (no longer) alive according to OS; emitting dedicated peer-dead channel-hosing error "
5978 "[" << *err_code << "] [" << err_code->message() << "].");
5979 hose(*err_code, "remote_peer_process_liveness_check()/peer-not-running", false);
5980 }
5981
5982 return true;
5983} // Channel::remote_peer_process_liveness_check()
5984

5994bool CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::check_prior_error(util::String_view context) const
5995{
5996 if (m_channel_err_code_or_ok)
5997 {
5998 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: In context [" << context << "]: A prior error "
5999 "[" << m_channel_err_code_or_ok << "] [" << m_channel_err_code_or_ok.message() << "] shall "
6000 "prevent further action in this context: bailing out of this operation.");

6003 // else

6008bool CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::check_phase_and_prior_error(Phase required_phase, util::String_view context) const

6020 return false;

6022 // else
6023
6024 return true;

6040TEMPLATE_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL
6041typename CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::Msg_out CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::create_msg
6042 (size_t msg_sz_cap_estimate_or_zero, Native_handle&& hndl_or_null) const
6043{
6044 // We are just a convenience helper really; all we do is pass-in m_struct_builder_config memorized for convenience.
6045
6046 if (msg_sz_cap_estimate_or_zero == 0)
6047 {
6048 return create_msg(std::move(hndl_or_null));
6049 }
6050 // else
6051
6052 auto& cfg_ref = m_struct_builder_config;
6053 if (cfg_ref.m_segment_sz_init == msg_sz_cap_estimate_or_zero)
6054 {
6055 return create_msg(std::move(hndl_or_null));
6056 }
6057 // else
6058
6059 auto cfg_copy = cfg_ref;
6060
6061 // It'll be rounded to an aligned-width thing, so don't waste time doing it ourselves.
6062 cfg_copy.m_segment_sz_init = msg_sz_cap_estimate_or_zero;
6063
6064 Msg_out msg{cfg_copy};
6065 if (!hndl_or_null.null()) // Tiny optimization to skip past some boring checks inside store_...().
6066 {
6067 msg.store_native_handle_or_null(std::move(hndl_or_null));
6068 }
6069 return msg;
6070}

6073template<typename On_msg_handler>
6074bool CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::expect_msg(Msg_which_in which, Msg_in_ptr* qd_msg, On_msg_handler&& on_msg_func)
6075{
6076 using boost::make_shared;
6077
6078 assert(qd_msg);
6079 if (!check_phase_and_prior_error(Phase::S_LOGGED_IN, "expect_msg()"))
6080 {
6081 return false;
6082 }
6083 // else
6084
6085 Msgs_in qd_msgs;
6086 const bool ok = expect_msgs_impl(&qd_msgs,
6087 true, // One-off expectation (one message expected).
6088 which,
6089 make_shared<typename On_msg_handler_ptr::element_type>(std::move(on_msg_func)));
6090
6091 if (ok && (!qd_msgs.empty()))
6092 {
6093 assert((qd_msgs.size() == 1) && "Desiring 1 message -- should have emitted at most 1 already-ready message.");
6094 *qd_msg = std::move(qd_msgs.front());
6095 }
6096 else
6097 {
6098 qd_msg->reset();
6099 }
6100
6101 return ok;
6102} // Channel::expect_msg()

6106bool CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::expect_msgs(Msg_which_in which, Msgs_in* qd_msgs, On_msg_handler&& on_msg_func)

6124template<typename On_msg_handler>
6125bool CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::expect_log_in_request(Msg_which_in which, Msg_in_ptr* qd_msg,
6126 On_msg_handler&& on_log_in_req_func)
6127{
6128 using boost::make_shared;
6129

6132 {
6133 return false;
6134 }
6135 // else
6136
6137 if (m_phase_log_in_started)
6138 {
6139 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Log-in: expect_log_in_request() called again. "
6140 "Ignoring.");
6141 return false;
6142 }
6143 // else
6144 m_phase_log_in_started = true;
6145
6146 Msgs_in qd_msgs;
6147 const bool ok = expect_msgs_impl(&qd_msgs,
6148 true, // One-off expectation (one message -- the log-in response -- expected).
6149 which,

6151 (std::move(on_log_in_req_func)));
6152 if (ok && (!qd_msgs.empty()))
6153 {

6155 *qd_msg = std::move(qd_msgs.front());
6156 }
6157 else
6158 {
6159 qd_msg->reset();
6160 }

6162 return ok;
