6164
6165TEMPLATE_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL
6166bool CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::expect_msgs_impl(Msgs_in* qd_msgs, bool one_off, Msg_which_in which,
6167 On_msg_handler_ptr&& on_msg_func_moved)
6168{
6169 const auto insert_result
6170 = m_rcv_expecting_msg_map.emplace(which, new Expecting_msg{ one_off, on_msg_func_moved });
6171 auto& exp_msg_it = insert_result.first;
6172 const bool inserted = insert_result.second;
6173
6174 if (!inserted)
6175 {
6176 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Wanted to register a (one-off? = [" << one_off << "]) "
6177 "message expectation (union-which = [" << int(which) << "]); but there is already one registered "
6178 "for that union-which. Ignoring.");
6179 return false;
6180 }
6181 // else if (inserted):
6182
6183 // Stats: total registration count + active gauge.
6184 if (one_off)
6185 {
6186 ++m_stats.m_rcv.m_expect_msg_count;
6187 ++m_stats.m_rcv.m_expect_msg_active;
6188 }
6189 else
6190 {
6191 ++m_stats.m_rcv.m_expect_msgs_count;
6192 ++m_stats.m_rcv.m_expect_msgs_active;
6193 }
6194
6195 const bool logging_in = m_phase != Phase::S_LOGGED_IN;
6196 const auto msgs_in_q_it = m_rcv_pending_msgs.find(which);
6197 const bool found = msgs_in_q_it != m_rcv_pending_msgs.end();
6198
6199 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Registered a (one-off? = [" << one_off << "]) "
6200 "message expectation (union-which = [" << int(which) << "]); that raises their total count to "
6201 "[" << m_rcv_expecting_msg_map.size() << "]. Will immediately return qd-msgs if "
6202 "we had collected 1+ messages matching that union-which; had we? = [" << found << "].");
6203 if (!found)
6204 {
6205 if (logging_in && (!m_rcv_pending_msgs.empty()))
6206 {
6207 assert((m_phase == Phase::S_SRV_LOG_IN) && "Unless LOGGED_IN we should only be called by expect_log_in_request() "
6208 "which implies SRV_LOG_IN.");
6209 assert((m_rcv_pending_msgs.size() == 1)
6210 && "Other code is supposed to ensure we cache at most the log-in request and no more in-messages while "
6211 "in SRV_LOG_IN phase.");
6212 assert((m_rcv_expecting_msg_map.size() == 1)
6213 && "Other code is supposed to prevent logged-in APIs like expect_msg() in this phase; and more than one "
6214 "successful call to expect_log_in_request(); yet somehow we'd saved more expectations than exactly "
6215 "1 in m_rcv_expecting_msg_map.");
6216
6217 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Registered a (one-off? = [" << one_off << "]) "
6218 "*log-in request* expectation (union-which = [" << int(which) << "]); that raises their "
6219 "total count to 1. Would immediately queue handler(s) to fire if "
6220 "we had collected 1 messages matching that union-which; but we had not; however we had "
6221 "cached 1 message with different union-which = "
6222 "[" << int(m_rcv_pending_msgs.begin()->first) << "]. "
6223 "So: peer expects log-in request X, while other side sent log-in request Y. "
6224 "This might be a protocol error on the user's part on this or other side or both.");
6225 // Subtlety: See similar comment in the on-receive handler where it also emits this error.
6226 handle_new_error(error::Code::S_STRUCT_CHANNEL_GOT_UNEXPECTED_LOG_IN_REQUEST, "expect_msgs_impl()");
6227 /* ^-- That fired the on-error handler, synchronously, within the user's expect_log_in_request() call --
6228 * a documented exception (see that guy's doc header + class doc header): this is the one plain API able
6229 * to *detect* a new channel-hosing error, and the sync_io pattern offers no later point to defer to.
6230 * Correspondingly return `true` just below: the operation ran and reported its (fatal) result -- a-la
6231 * start_and_poll() immediately emitting new error -- while `false` remains reserved for no-op/pre-condition
6232 * situations. */
6233
6234 return true;
6235 }
6236 // else
6237
6238 return true; // Cool -- just await future in-message(s) with `which`.
6239 } // if (!found)
6240 // else if (found):
6241
6242 qd_msgs->clear();
6243
6244 auto& msgs_in_q = msgs_in_q_it->second;
6245 assert((!msgs_in_q.empty()) && "We always erase m_rcv_pending_msgs[] queue once it's empty... yet a queue is empty.");
6246
6247 if (one_off)
6248 {
6249 qd_msgs->reserve(1); // Little optimization. Maybe it'll make it reserve 1 exactly; maybe it's a no-op.
6250
6251 Msg_in_ptr_uniq msg_in{std::move(msgs_in_q.front())};
6252 msgs_in_q.pop();
6253 if (msgs_in_q.empty()) // Empty -> immediately erase.
6254 {
6255 m_rcv_pending_msgs.erase(msgs_in_q_it); // msg_in_q now points to garbage (do not touch it).
6256 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("Popped 1 (because one-off expectation); queue is now empty.");
6257 }
6258 else
6259 {
6260 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("Popped 1 (because one-off expectation); queue is now sized [" << msgs_in_q.size() << "].");
6261 }
6262
6263 qd_msgs->emplace_back(Msg_in_ptr{std::move(msg_in)}); // Upgrade to shared_ptr<> by the way.
6264
6265 // ...and un-insert the registered expectation, since it was immediately met. @todo Can perf this up probably.
6266 m_rcv_expecting_msg_map.erase(exp_msg_it);
6267
6268 // Stats.
6269 {
6270 ++m_stats.m_rcv.m_expect_q_immediate_pops; // Popped cached msg on registration.
6271 --m_stats.m_rcv.m_pending_msgs_depth;
6272 --m_stats.m_rcv.m_expect_msg_active; // One-off expectation immediately satisfied.
6273 }
6274 return true;
6275 }
6276 // else if (!one_off):
6277
6278 // Emit the entire queue of waiting messages.
6279 qd_msgs->reserve(msgs_in_q.size()); // Little optimization.
6280
6281 do // while (!msgs_in_q.empty())
6282 {
6283 qd_msgs->emplace_back(msgs_in_q.front().release()); // Upgrade to shared_ptr<> by the way.
6284 msgs_in_q.pop();
6285 }
6286 while (!msgs_in_q.empty());
6287 m_rcv_pending_msgs.erase(msgs_in_q_it); // Empty -> immediately erase.
6288
6289 // Stats.
6290 {
6291 ++m_stats.m_rcv.m_expect_q_immediate_pops; // Popped (all) cached msgs on registration. Still counts for 1 here.
6292 m_stats.m_rcv.m_pending_msgs_depth -= qd_msgs->size();
6293 }
6294
6295 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("Popped all [" << qd_msgs->size() << "] cached in-message from queue.");
6296
6297 // And leave m_rcv_expecting_msg_map alone: new element will stay there until undo_expect_msgs().
6298
6299 return true;
6300} // Channel::expect_msgs_impl()

6302TEMPLATE_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL
6303bool CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::undo_expect_msgs(Msg_which_in which)
6304{
6305 if (!check_phase_and_prior_error(Phase::S_LOGGED_IN, "undo_expect_msgs()"))
6306 {
6307 return false;
6308 }
6309 // else
6310
6311 const auto exp_msg_it = m_rcv_expecting_msg_map.find(which);
6312 if (exp_msg_it == m_rcv_expecting_msg_map.end())
6313 {
6314 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Attempt to erase in-message expectation "
6315 "[" << int(which) << "]: Failed, as there was no such expectation registered. "
6316 "Their total number remains [" << m_rcv_expecting_msg_map.size() << "].");
6317 return false;
6318 }
6319 // else
6320 if (exp_msg_it->second->m_one_expected)
6321 {
6322 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Attempt to erase in-message expectation "
6323 "[" << int(which) << "]: Failed, as it is a one-off expectation (via expect_msg()) which "
6324 "cannot be undone. Their total number remains [" << m_rcv_expecting_msg_map.size() << "].");
6325 return false;
6326 }
6327 // else
6328
6329 m_rcv_expecting_msg_map.erase(exp_msg_it);
6330 --m_stats.m_rcv.m_expect_msgs_active;
6331
6332 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Attempt to erase in-message expectation "
6333 "[" << int(which) << "]: Success. Their total number is now "
6334 "[" << m_rcv_expecting_msg_map.size() << "].");
6335 return true;
6336} // Channel::undo_expect_msgs()

6339bool CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::undo_expect_responses(msg_id_out_t originating_msg_id)
6340{
6341 assert((originating_msg_id != 0) && "send() would never set *id_unless_one_off = 0.");
6342
6343 if (!check_phase_and_prior_error(Phase::S_LOGGED_IN, "undo_expect_responses()"))
6344 {
6345 return false;
6346 }
6347 // else
6348
6349 const auto exp_rsp_it = m_rcv_expecting_response_map.find(originating_msg_id);
6350 if (exp_rsp_it == m_rcv_expecting_response_map.end())
6351 {
6352 FLOW_LOG_WARNING("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Attempt to erase response expectation for sent "
6353 "message with ID [" << originating_msg_id << "]: Failed, as there was no such "
6354 "expectation registered. Their total number remains "
6355 "[" << m_rcv_expecting_response_map.size() << "].");
6356 return false;
6357 }
6358 // else
6359 if (exp_rsp_it->second->m_one_expected)

6362 "message with ID [" << originating_msg_id << "]: Failed, as it is a one-off expectation "
6363 "(via the one-off form of async_request()) which cannot be undone. Their total number remains "
6364 "[" << m_rcv_expecting_response_map.size() << "].");
6365 return false;
6366 }
6367 // else
6368
6369 m_rcv_expecting_response_map.erase(exp_rsp_it);
6370 --m_stats.m_rcv.m_expect_response_sticky_active;
6371
6372 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: Attempt to erase response expectation for sent "
6373 "message with ID [" << originating_msg_id << "]: Success. Their total number is now "
6374 "[" << m_rcv_expecting_response_map.size() << "].");
6375 return true;
6376} // Channel::undo_expect_responses()

6487TEMPLATE_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL
6488void CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::Handlers::Message::execute(Channel* daddy)
6489{
6490 if (m_on_msg_func_if_expected)
6491 {
6492 /* Fast path: Report message via saved handler (response to request/expected notification).
6493 * Don't even TRACE-log (avoid log setup).
6494 *
6495 * Upgrade to shared_ptr when giving to user. */
6496 (*m_on_msg_func_if_expected)(Msg_in_ptr{std::move(m_msg_in)});
6497 }
6498 else // if (!m_on_msg_func_if_expected)
6499 {
6500 // Unexpected response: this is rare. So setting up logging (and logging if it comes to it) is fine.
6501 FLOW_LOG_SET_CONTEXT(daddy->get_logger(), daddy->get_log_component());
6502
6503 if (daddy->m_on_unexpected_response_func_or_empty.empty())
6504 {
6505 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *daddy << "]: Would invoke on-unexpected-rsp user handler; "
6506 "but none is configured. Restating some details: "
6507 "Structured in-message ID "
6508 "[" << Msg_in_impl<Msg_in>{ *m_msg_in }.id_or_none() << "] is a response to "
6509 "alleged out-message ID "
6510 "[" << Msg_in_impl<Msg_in>{ *m_msg_in }.originating_msg_id_or_none() << "] "
6511 "which either never existed or is not registered as awaiting a response.");
6512 }
6513 else
6514 {
6515 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *daddy << "]: Invoking on-unexpected-rsp user handler.");
6516 daddy->m_on_unexpected_response_func_or_empty(std::move(m_msg_in));
6517 }
6518 }
6519} // Channel::Handlers::Message::execute()
6520
6521TEMPLATE_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL
6522void CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::Handlers::Remote_unexpected_response::execute(Channel* daddy)
6523{
6524 using std::string;
6525
6526 // Unexpected response: this is rare. So setting up logging (and logging if it comes to it) is fine.
6527 FLOW_LOG_SET_CONTEXT(daddy->get_logger(), daddy->get_log_component());
6528
6529 string mdt_text{std::move(m_mdt_text)}; // For ultra-cleanliness (so both paths act the same w/r/t m_mdt_text).
6530 if (daddy->m_on_remote_unexpected_response_func_or_empty.empty())
6531 {
6532 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *daddy << "]: Would invoke on-remote-unexpected-rsp user handler; "
6533 "but none is configured. Restating the details: "
6534 "out-message with ID [" << m_originating_msg_id << "]; metadata text = [" << mdt_text << "].");
6535 }
6536 else
6537 {
6538 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *daddy << "]: Invoking on-remote-unexpected-rsp user handler.");
6539 daddy->m_on_remote_unexpected_response_func_or_empty(m_originating_msg_id, std::move(mdt_text));
6540 }

6544void CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::Handlers::Error::execute(Channel* daddy)
6545{
6546 // Error: this is rare. So setting up logging (and logging if it comes to it) is fine.
6547 FLOW_LOG_SET_CONTEXT(daddy->get_logger(), daddy->get_log_component());
6548 auto& err_func = daddy->m_on_err_func;
6549
6550 FLOW_LOG_TRACE("struc::Channel [" << *daddy << "]: Invoking on-error user handler.");
6551 assert((!err_func.empty()) && "Bug? Error shall be reported at most once.");
6552 err_func(daddy->m_channel_err_code_or_ok);
6553
6554 err_func.clear(); // Save RAM. Also help detect any breaking of promise that we'd invoke it at most once.
6555}

6557TEMPLATE_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL
6558void CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::hose(const Error_code& err_code_not_ok, util::String_view context,
6559 bool lower_layer_originating)
6560{
6561 assert(err_code_not_ok && "hose() must be called with a truthy error code.");
6562 assert((!m_channel_err_code_or_ok)
6563 && "hose() must be called only when channel is not already hosed. This is the single funnel "
6564 "for transitioning m_channel_err_code_or_ok from falsy to truthy.");
6565
6566 m_channel_err_code_or_ok = err_code_not_ok; // It will now never change.
6567
6568 // These would just waste memory at this point at best. Receive-chain is stopped; these won't fire.
6569 m_rcv_expecting_msg_map.clear(); // Attn: m_stats GAUGEs updated below accordingly.
6570 m_rcv_expecting_response_map.clear();
6571 m_on_remote_unexpected_response_func_or_empty.clear();
6572 m_on_unexpected_response_func_or_empty.clear();
6573
6574 /* We want to do this pretty much as soon as m_channel_err_code_or_ok has become truthy; anything -- including
6575 * but not necessarily limited to handler-posting/execution -- that could happen in-between = entropy.
6576 *
6577 * On lower-layer-originating hosing the relevant Owned_channel per-pipe sub-object has hosed/logged itself
6578 * already; otherwise the per-pipe sub-objects are still healthy and may not hose for a while, so snapshot
6579 * their stats too.
6580 *
6581 * @todo Technically, in the HAS_2_PIPES setup, if lower_layer_originating=true, then the other pipe would
6582 * still be healthy; yet in this logic we aren't going to print its stats -- though they're going to freeze
6583 * at this point, as we either operate all 1-2 pipes we own or none at any given time point* -- until
6584 * dtor. So for the cleanest possible behavior: `lower_layer_originating` and its forwardee should
6585 * really be about *which* pipe(s) (if any) should stat-log (maybe 2 bools to log_stats() and a 3-way
6586 * enum to us and handle_new_error()). There's definitely an elegant way to propagate that info, but it's
6587 * also definitely non-trivial effort for only a bit of added visibility.
6588 *
6589 * (*) One exception to this is where, with 2 pipes, pipe 1 has m_gracefully_closed==true, while pipe 2
6590 * is healthy. In that case one pipe is operating; the other is not. The difference here is that
6591 * the non-operating (technically hosed) pipe is thus by way of opposing user intentionally indicating
6592 * no more in-messages will follow; the graceful-close is in a sense itself an in-message, received
6593 * in-order versus the it-preceding in-msgs. So it's not operating, but it isn't "broken"; just done.
6594 * This caveat only reinforces the to-do's existence, loosely speaking. */
6595 log_stats(context, !lower_layer_originating);
6596
6597 { // Stats.
6598 auto& rcv = m_stats.m_rcv;
6599 rcv.m_expect_msg_active = 0;
6600 rcv.m_expect_msgs_active = 0;
6601 rcv.m_expect_response_sticky_active = 0;
6602 rcv.m_expect_response_one_off_active = 0;
6603 } // Stats.
6604}

6607void CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::log_stats(util::String_view context, bool log_owned_channel_stats) const
6608{
6609 using flow::util::stat::print;
6610
6611 FLOW_LOG_INFO("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: In context [" << context << "]: Stats: "
6612 "[" << print(m_stats) << "].");
6613
6614 if (log_owned_channel_stats)
6615 {
6616 if constexpr(Owned_channel::S_HAS_BLOB_PIPE)
6617 {
6618 FLOW_LOG_INFO("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: In context [" << context << "]: "
6619 "Owned_channel blob-stats: snd[" << print(m_channel.blob_send_stats()) << "] "
6620 "rcv[" << print(m_channel.blob_receive_stats()) << "].");
6621 }
6622 if constexpr(Owned_channel::S_HAS_NATIVE_HANDLE_PIPE)
6623 {
6624 FLOW_LOG_INFO("struc::Channel [" << *this << "]: In context [" << context << "]: "
6625 "Owned_channel hndl-stats: snd[" << print(m_channel.native_handle_send_stats()) << "] "
6626 "rcv[" << print(m_channel.native_handle_receive_stats()) << "].");
6627 }
6628 }
6629}

6643TEMPLATE_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL
6644void CLASS_SIO_STRUCT_CHANNEL::stats_configure_rcv_one_off_request_rtt_histogram(size_t n_buckets,
6645 util::Fine_duration bucket_sz)
6646{
6647 using flow::util::stat::Histogram_counter;
6648 using boost::chrono::round;
6649 using boost::chrono::microseconds;
6650
6651 /* The histogram's sole record site is in read-chain processing which begins (incl. for the internally-consumed
6652 * init messages) only at start_and_poll(); the m_on_err_func check below = has-start_and_poll()-happened. */
6653 assert(m_on_err_func.empty()
6654 && "stats_configure_rcv_one_off_request_rtt_histogram() must be called before start_and_poll().");
6655 const auto usec = round<microseconds>(bucket_sz).count();
6656 m_stats.m_rcv.m_histo_one_off_request_rtt_usec = Histogram_counter{n_buckets, usec, usec, 0};
6657}
